findings.title: DH-01 auger head is not fastened to AG-01: the M3 x 12 screws never reach the post
findings.evidence: auger_west.py: the DH-01 bridge is box(40,250,135 -> 100,299,148), so it is 13.0 mm thick. The clearance holes are holes(...,148,134,3.4). The AG-01 pilots are holes([(48,262.5),(62,262.5)],135,125,2.5): Ø2.5, 10 mm deep, top at Z135. In meshes.json the two 'SHCS ISO 4762 M3x12' under 'Measuring + auger station' run from head Z148-151 down to a shank tip at Z136.0. The tip stops 1.0 mm above the post top (Z135), so thread engagement is 0 mm. README rows 388 and 513 specify M3 x 12. The 'interference PASS' check could not catch a screw that is too short. As specified, the head, hopper and motor sit loose on the post.
findings.required_change: Use M3 x 22 SHCS: the tip lands at Z126, giving 9 mm engagement in the existing Ø2.5 x 10 pilots and 1 mm above the pilot bottom. A better option, since AG-01 is being reprinted anyway: change the pilots to Ø4.0 x 8 mm bores, fit ruthex M3 x 5.7 heat-set inserts and use M3 x 20. Update the CAD fastener occurrences, the README fastener table and the BOM to match. Do this before tonight's A1 print of AG-01/DH-01.

findings.title: DH-01 tube, hopper and outlet hang off the bridge by a ~50 mm² sliver
findings.evidence: auger_west.py: the bridge box stops at Y299 and the tube is ycyl(87,155, 299->381, r9.5), so the two bodies meet only where their end faces overlap on the plane Y=299. I sliced the DH-01 STL along Y. At Y<=298.9 the section is bridge only (Z135-148.9, 779 mm²); at Y>=299.1 it is tube only (Z145.6-164.4). The overlap of the 298.95 and 299.05 masks is 45.6-57 mm², a strip X79.4-94.6 by Z144.8-148.8 (about 15.6 x 4 mm, so Z_bend ≈ 42 mm³ and the torsion constant is tiny). About 26 cm³ of tube and hopper (64.6 total minus 38.2 for the bridge), plus up to 35 mL of yeast (~21 g) and DH-02, cantilevers from it with its CG about 36 mm out at Z~170. A 10 N lateral hand load on the hopper rim while refilling (Z205, 58 mm above the sliver) gives a torsional shear of ~0.58 N·m / (0.29·15.6·4²) ≈ 8 MPa on horizontal layer planes, before any Kt. A 10 N downward push gives σ ≈ 0.31 N·m / 42 mm³ ≈ 7.5 MPa. The part also prints on tree supports with the tube hanging off this joint.
findings.required_change: Add a web under the tube: X79-95, Y299-350, Z135-152. It joins the bridge, the tube underside and the hopper floor, with R3 fillets on all re-entrant edges, giving a bonded section of at least 800 mm² (target ≥15 x 50 mm). Stop the web at Y350 so the Ø10 outlet (Y365-375) stays open. The web bottom at Z135 clears the carousel beaker rims (Z121.2) by 13.8 mm. Re-slice DH-01 at Y299 and Y320 to verify more than 600 mm² of continuous section before printing.

findings.title: Carousel is over-constrained: the deck is bolted to the servo horn AND VHB-bonded to a hand-placed lazy Susan
findings.evidence: README fastener table: 'Carousel SHCS M3 x 10 x4, deck → TT-03 → tapped horn' and '3M 4950 VHB, 2 layers, TT-01 top → lazy Susan → deck underside'. Nothing registers the lazy Susan to the servo axis: 'Hole pattern unpublished, so it's taped, not screwed'. The TT-01 STL top (Z42.8) is a cross-shaped opening with four corner pads, and TT-02 has only a Ø9 centre hole, so there is no spigot to locate the 53.3 mm lazy-Susan bore. Any offset e between the lazy-Susan axis and the servo spline axis forces a relative displacement d = 2e·sin(θ/2) across the bonded VHB. The ±67.5° yeast move gives d = 1.1e at the centre and more toward the edge. Shear stiffness of the bond ≈ G·A/t = 0.5 MPa x ~6,600 mm² / 2.2 mm ≈ 1,500 N/mm. With hand placement e ≈ 0.5-1.5 mm, that is 0.8-2.5 kN of radial load on the M45CHW output bearing, the 4 x M3 in PLA and the VHB. The carousel will bind or stall short of its station, or tear the tape.
findings.required_change: Remove the upper VHB layer. Bond only the lazy Susan's bottom plate to TT-01. Let the deck rest on the top plate through a 1.0 mm adhesive PTFE/UHMW sheet on the deck underside, which keeps the stack within 0.1 mm: horn shim 0.5 → 0.6 mm. The deck is then located radially only by the 25T spline and drives the top plate by friction. Also add a printed Ø53.0 -0.2 spigot on TT-01 that registers the lazy-Susan bore, so the thrust support is concentric to within 0.3 mm. Update the TT stack table in the README.

findings.title: ST-01 Ø18 stop posts have an R0.7 root fillet; the claimed SF 3.0 is really ~1.2 at stall and <1 on impact
findings.evidence: ST-01 STL slices around (653,112)/(653,172): the web ends at Z35.3, area 268 mm² at Z35.5 and 254 mm² (Ø18) from Z37. The fillet-excess profile fits r ≈ 0.7 mm, which is fillet_lib.iterative_g falling back to 0.35 x r_in=2.0. design_data lists ST-01 fillet_r [0.7,1.5,2.0]. load_cases.py: F = 4.41/0.030 = 147 N at Z61, lever 25.7 mm, σ_nom = 6.6 MPa across layers, compared with 20 MPa with no stress concentration. Peterson shoulder-fillet bending, r/d = 0.7/18 = 0.04: Kt ≈ 2.4, so σ_peak ≈ 16 MPa and SF ≈ 1.2 against an interlayer allowable that scatters between 10 and 25 MPa. Impact case: post stiffness k = 3EI/L³ = 3·3500·5153/25.7³ ≈ 3.2 kN/mm. Tray plus payload of 0.69 kg at the normal 0.36 m/s peak gives F ≈ √(2·0.045 J·3.2e6) ≈ 0.5 kN, so σ_nom ≈ 24 MPa and peak ≈ 58 MPa. The stops are hit on the first wrong pulse-table or sign mapping, which the README itself warns about (180° vs 270° unit, 'sign depends on which way the servo faces').
findings.required_change: Raise both webs to Z54, which is 2 mm under the crank underside at Z56 and outside the servo footprint (Y132-152). This cuts the free length to 7 mm. Enlarge the posts to Ø22 and put an R4 fillet at the web-to-post junction. Fit a 3 mm TPU 95A bumper sleeve (print with GR-03) on each post. Resulting σ_nom = 147·7/1045 ≈ 1.0 MPa, SF > 10 static. Correct load_cases.py to include Kt and an impact case.

findings.title: Front-row countersunk arm bolts must cut into the borrowed SO-101 base, and engage only 1.2 mm of the T-nut
findings.evidence: README rows 37-42 say to 'Let the 90° head cut its own seat in the PLA boss ... or countersink lightly first'. That modifies the borrowed arm, which the BRIEF forbids ('Don't drill or modify them'). Geometry: an ISO 10642 M4 head (dk 8.96) in a Ø5.0 through-hole with its top at Z37.0 cuts a cone 1.2 mm deep into the boss, and the 90° wedge puts hoop stress on the PLA boss as it is torqued. meshes.json: the CSK M4x20 runs Z17-37, and the T-nut M4 occupies Z14.4-18.2, so engagement is 1.2 mm (1.7 threads). The back-row SHCS M4x20 (tip Z16.2) engages 2.0 mm. The arm-base load case assumes full T-nut strength.
findings.required_change: Replace the front row with ISO 7380 M4 x 22 button heads (head height 2.2 mm, dk 7.6). They seat on the existing boss at Z36.2 without modifying it, and the head top is at Z38.4. Add a shoulder soft limit so the shoulder link stays ≥3 mm above Z38.4, and check it in plan3. Lengthen the back row to M4 x 22: tip at Z14.2, 4.0 mm engagement, 0.3 mm above the 2020 core at Z13.9. Remove the countersink instruction from the README and update the BOM (8 x M4 x 22).

findings.title: AG-01 135 mm post: no real base fillet is possible, the gusset ends abruptly, and the stand rocks about the 20 x 12 bar
findings.evidence: auger_west.py: foot box(40,250,0 -> 70,312,12), post box(40,250,12 -> 70,275,135), gusset box(40,275,12 -> 46,300,70). The post is flush with the foot on the -X, +X and -Y faces, so its 'root' is a straight wall down to the bed. The only re-entrant root is the +Y face, at R≈2 (STL: post-only section 778 mm² at Z12.1 → 754 at Z13.5 → 747 mm² above). The 6 mm gusset terminates at Z70, where the section steps from 897 to 747 mm², a notch with an R1.2 top edge. The stand is held only by a 20 x 12 bar to the saddle 170 mm away (X70 → X240); the foot just rests on the table. A 20 N push in -X at the hopper (Z180) gives M = 3.6 N·m on the bar: σ = 3600/480 = 7.5 MPa (x Kt≈1.8 at the saddle junction) and θ = ML/EI = 3600·170/(3500·2880) = 0.061 rad (3.5°), so the hopper top moves about 11 mm. The layer-bonded area of this 123 mm-tall pillar is 747 mm² everywhere. It is printed upright on the A1 bed-slinger tonight.
findings.required_change: Grow the foot to 80 x 80 (X20-100, Y235-315; it is under the deck at Z<54.6, clear of TT-01 at X≥120) so the post has a true root on all four sides. Put an R8 base fillet at the post-to-foot junction, giving ~+300 mm² of bonded area within 2 mm of the root and Kt ≈1.25 instead of ~1.9. Replace the 6 mm gusset with two 8 mm gussets on the +X and +Y faces, 40 mm long at the root and tapering to zero at Z100, with R5 fillets at both ends. Thicken the bar to 30 x 16 (3.6x stiffer). Print AG-01 on the H2D or X2 (core-XY), not the A1.

findings.title: AG-01 front saddle T-nut hangs 4.5 mm off the end of the left Y-rail
findings.evidence: agfix.py moved the AG-01 bolts to Y291/Y309. meshes.json: the left Y-rail starts at Y290 (min [245,290,0]), and the AG-01 'T-nut 2020 drop-in M5' spans Y285.5-296.5. Only 6.5 of its 11 mm sit under the slot lips. Under preload the T-nut tilts out of the open end, and the AG-01 saddle (Y283-321) also overhangs the rail end by 7 mm. The original 297/307 spacing failed for a different reason: two 11 mm T-nuts on 10 mm centres overlap.
findings.required_change: Put the AG-01 saddle bolts at Y297 and Y310. That gives T-nuts at 291.5-302.5 and 304.5-315.5, fully on the rail with a 2 mm gap and clear of TT-01's T-nut at Y349.5. Shorten the saddle to Y290-321. Fix this in the same reprint as M-01/M-06.

findings.title: Fillets were applied by a blanket script, not sized to load paths; structural roots are R0-R2
findings.evidence: fillet_lib.process4 applies one r_in (1.5-2.0) to every concave edge. On failure it retries at 0.6r and then 0.35r, and it rejects any fillet that changes volume by more than 1.5% (guarded_add), so large roots are systematically refused. design_data fillet_r: ST-01 [0.7,...], DH-01 [0.35,1.0,1.5], TT-04 [0.8,1.5], RK-02 [1.0,1.5]; GR-01, GR-02, GR-03 and DH-02 have none. Measured: ST-04 Ø20 tray posts, 31 mm tall above their boss, have a root fillet of ≤0.5 mm (area 318 mm² at local Z18.5 vs 313.6). Under a stall load of 29 N at 37 mm: σ_nom 1.4 MPa, Kt ≈ 2.7. TT-04 pocket walls are 2.4 mm thick x 16 tall with R0.8 roots: a 10 N side load from a beaker dragged by the arm gives σ ≈ 160/19.2 = 8.3 MPa x 1.5 ≈ 12.5 MPa across layers (SF 1.6). The GR-01/GR-02 tongue roots (5 x 20 mm tongue, 10.5 mm projection) are sharp.
findings.required_change: Replace the blanket pass with explicit root fillets: ST-04 tray posts R4; ST-01 idler post (Ø24) R4; ST-01 stop posts per M-04; AG-01 per M-06; WS-01 pedestal-to-saddle R4; TT-04 pocket walls thickened to 3.2 mm with R1.5 inside and outside roots; RK-02 pocket walls R1.5; GR-01/GR-02 tongue roots R1.5, with a 1.5 x 45° chamfer on the GR-03 slot mouth so the fillet still seats; DH-02 collar R2 (M-09); DH-01 joints R3 (M-02). Add a fillet check to the export: list every concave edge on a load path with its radius and fail anything below its spec instead of silently accepting 0.35r.

findings.title: DH-02 auger screw shears at the collar step on a jam, and its flights are too thin to print
findings.evidence: aug2.py: collar r=4.5 for z=0-7, D-bore 8 mm deep, hub r=2.6, two flights from a 12 x 2 rectangle twisted to a 16 mm lead, no fillets. STL: section 62.9 mm² up to z=6.9, then 28.3 mm² at z=7.1-7.9, where the Ø3.1 D-bore runs past the collar into the Ø5.1 hub (1.0 mm wall), with a sharp step. N20 6 V 60 rpm stall ≈ 0.2-0.35 N·m. Software §6 runs the TB6612 at 100% PWM from the 2S pack (8.4 V), adding ~40%. Hub annulus J = π(5.1⁴-3.1⁴)/32 = 57 mm⁴, so τ = 250·2.55/57 ≈ 11 MPa nominal at 0.25 N·m, about 22 MPa with Kt≈2. That is torsional shear on the layer planes of an upright print, whose interlayer shear strength is ~10-20 MPa. Flight normal thickness at the tip = 2·sin(atan(16/2π·6)) = 0.78 mm (two lines), printed as a 67° overhang on tree supports.
findings.required_change: Extend the Ø9 collar to z=12 so the 8 mm D-bore sits wholly inside it with 4 mm of margin. Add an R2 fillet from collar to hub and grow the hub to Ø7. Make the flights ≥1.6 mm normal thickness with a 45° underside flank (buttress profile), so the screw prints upright without supports. Cap the motor at 70% PWM (≈6 V) and add stall detection (no speed change within 300 ms → stop and reverse), which the software plan must state. Add an 'auger jam at stall torque' row to load_cases.

findings.title: Auger bore printed horizontally on tree supports with 0.42 mm radial clearance; screw has no tip support
findings.evidence: auger_west.py: bore Ø13 along +Y. The DH-01 STL is exported Z-up, so the bore axis is horizontal, and the README says 'Print with tree supports'. The DH-02 STL envelope is Ø12.16 (rectangle corners at r=6.08), so radial clearance is 0.42 mm. A horizontal Ø13 FDM bore sags 0.2-0.4 mm at the crown, and support scars inside it add 0.2-0.5 mm of roughness: interference with the flight tips is likely. Dry yeast granules (0.3-1.5 mm) wedge into a 0.4 mm gap. The 62 mm screw is cantilevered from the N20 shaft with its free end at Y365.
findings.required_change: Open the bore to Ø14.0 (0.9 mm radial clearance) or cut the flight OD to Ø11.2. Model the bore with a 45° teardrop crown and put a support blocker over the bore volume. After printing, ream with a 14 mm drill by hand. Add a Ø3 x 6 printed pin on the screw tip that runs in a Ø3.4 bushing in the tube end cap (Y375-378). Spin the screw at full speed with yeast for 2 minutes during Wednesday's fit check.

findings.title: Fin-ray grip force from a 4° position squeeze is about 2-5x too low to hold a full reagent beaker
findings.evidence: The README gripper table and software §3 command contact plus 4°. gripper_design.json: beaker centre at |c| = 67 mm, so the contact is ~60 mm from the hinge and 4° gives 4.2 mm of total interference, shared by two fin-rays in series. At an estimated 0.3-0.8 N/mm per 65 mm TPU 95A fin-ray (1.6/1.8 mm skins), N ≈ 0.6-1.7 N per finger. Demand in the upright carry, where the full weight shears the contact: 100 mL PP beaker (~25 g) + 80 mL developer (1.04 g/mL) = 108 g, W = 1.06 N. TPU on wet PP (peroxide or dish soap) μ ≈ 0.3. N ≥ SF·W/(2μ) = 2·1.06/0.6 = 3.5 N per finger, and 5.3 N with the ±1 g shake the README uses. The soap/dye beaker is the worst case, with a slick outside.
findings.required_change: Close the gripper by force, not by angle: drive to contact, then hold a measured STS3215 load (current) that gives N ≥ 5 N, found on Wednesday with a luggage scale on TC fingers. Add 1 mm silicone (Dragon Skin 20) or grip tape to the contact face to get μ ≥ 0.6. Add a lift-5-mm slip check (position drift < 1 mm) before any transfer. Add a grip-friction row to load_cases.

findings.title: A level-gripper roll pour puts the pour lip at a finger, and beaker spouts are not indexed
findings.evidence: plan3.pour: qt[4] += ±100° is a wrist-roll about the approach axis e1 with the hinge vertical. After the roll, gravity in the gripper frame lies along ±e2, the closing direction. The contacts sit at normals (0.42,-0.91) on the fixed finger and (0,1) on the moving one, so the lowest rim point is next to a finger. GRIP_H puts the finger top (grip +17 mm) at 62 mm on a 61 mm-tall 50 mL beaker and 69 mm on a 74 mm 100 mL beaker. The stream leaves the rim right at the TPU finger and runs down the finger, wrist and scale. The EISCO PP beakers have spouts, but the TT-04, RK-02 and WS-02 pockets are plain rings, so the spout lands at a random angle.
findings.required_change: Lower the grasp so the finger top is ≥10 mm below the rim: GRIP_H 50 mL 45 → 34 (finger spans 17-51, 1.6 mm above the TT-04 wall top) and 100 mL 52 → 40. Re-run plan3. Add a 6 mm wide x 3 mm deep spout key notch to every TT-04, RK-02 and WS-02 pocket, oriented so the spout faces the downhill side of that station's fixed roll direction.

findings.title: Approach clearance is ±2.6 mm and the pockets have no lead-ins, below SO-101 repeatability
findings.evidence: plan3: OPEN = contact + 5° (the README's -55° for 43 mm). At ~60 mm radius that is 5.2 mm of total opening, ±2.6 mm, while the V-tips are narrower than the beaker, so a vertical approach is mandatory. gripper_design.json itself specifies q_open = contact + 14°. STL pocket IDs: TT-04 46.0 (43 mm beaker, ±1.5), RK-02 59.0 (56 mm, ±1.5), WS-02 ring Ø46. TT-04 ID measures 46.0 at z=8 and 45.8 at z=15.5, so there is no lead-in. A real SO-101 (STS3215 backlash ~0.5-1°, calibration offsets) is accurate to about ±3-5 mm at 250 mm reach, and the planner's '<0.5 mm' is FK vs CAD, not vs the hardware.
findings.required_change: Approach and release at contact + 14° and confirm with the plan3 audit that the 100 mm fingers clear the neighbours (67.4 mm pocket pitch). Add a 3 x 45° lead-in chamfer to every TT-04, RK-02 and WS-02 pocket rim. Add a teach step (software tools/teach.py) that jogs and stores every pick, place and pour pose on the real bench on Friday, replacing CAD poses.

findings.title: GR-03 TPU slot will not accept the tongue; GR-01/02 tongues are unfilleted; GR-02 print orientation loads layers
findings.evidence: gripper_ops.py: slot = tongue(SL=0.15) is 5.3 mm high and 20.3 mm wide (v 1.85-22.15), open only at u=-12. The finger prints lying on its profile (STL Z=34 is the hinge axis), so the slot roof is a 20.3 mm TPU bridge with 0.15 mm/side clearance. TPU sags 0.5-1.5 mm over that span, against a 5.0 mm PLA tongue. The side walls next to the slot are 1.85 mm. The M3 clamp goes through a base block printed at 30% infill, which creeps. design_data: GR-01, GR-02 and GR-03 have no fillets at all. GR-02's STL bbox (48.1,75.7,35.8) against its world bbox (49.7,35.4,75.8) shows the hinge axis horizontal in print, unlike GR-01, so tongue bending acts across layers.
findings.required_change: Give the slot a 45° gabled roof and chamfer the GR-01/02 tongue top edges 2 x 45° to match. Raise SL to 0.25 mm/side. Print the GR-03 base block (u<0) at 100% infill with a modifier. Use M3 nylon-insert locknuts. Add R1.5 at the tongue roots per M-08. Re-export GR-02 with the hinge axis vertical, as GR-01 is. Print one finger on Wednesday and test-fit it before printing four.

findings.title: The 1 kg load cell has no overload stop and no splash protection
findings.evidence: meshes.json: WS-01 supports the cell at X403.5-426.9 and WS-02 bears on its free end at X457.9-478.5. The gap under the pan is 12.7 mm and nothing limits deflection. Safe overload for a 1 kg bar cell is ~150% (14.7 N). An arm placing a beaker with 2-5 mm Z error into a stiff scale easily applies 20-30 N (STS3215 shoulder ~3 N·m at ~150-250 mm), which risks a permanent zero shift that the closed-loop pour depends on. Arm B pours 12% H2O2 with phosphoric acid onto a 74 mm pan directly above an unsealed aluminium cell and HX711 wiring.
findings.required_change: Add a stop post on WS-01 under the WS-02 rim opposite the cell, at (468,505), with a 0.4 mm gap. That limits pan travel to ≈1.3x full-scale deflection; check that the cell deflects less than 0.4 mm at 1 kg. Enlarge WS-02 to Ø90 with a 3 mm raised lip and an 8 mm downward skirt over the cell. Add 'arm place force vs cell overload' to load_cases.

findings.title: PLA tray, collar and catch well sit under a reaction that reaches 60-70 °C; the load case compares against PETG
findings.evidence: The BRIEF requires PLA. README line 66 says 'Everything is printed in PLA', but load_cases row 'Foam temperature vs PETG softening 55 vs 70 °C, SF 1.3' and the STL names (ST-04/05/07 _PETG) assume PETG. design_data has ST-04, ST-05 and REF-WELL as PLA. Adiabatic estimate for 50 mL of 40-vol developer: 6.24 g H2O2 = 0.184 mol x 98.2 kJ/mol = 18.0 kJ, into ~110 g of liquid (440 J/K) plus a ~110 g flask (90 J/K), gives ΔT ≈ 34 K. From a ~28 °C mix that is about 62 °C; the README's 75 mL option gives ~72 °C. PLA HDT is ≈55 °C. The ST-05 socket wall is 2.4 mm (86.6 ID) and the ST-07 wall is 2.0 mm, both in contact with hot glass and foam, for ~10 runs.
findings.required_change: Put a 3 mm silicone or cork pad (add to BOM) between the flask and ST-05. Cap the charge at 50 mL in the README and recipe. Thicken ST-07 walls to 3.2 mm. Rename the STLs to drop _PETG. Replace the thermal row in load_cases with PLA (HDT 55 °C) and the computed 62 °C, or move hot-wetted containment to the bought PP basin of M-17 (HDT ~100 °C).

findings.title: Catch well holds about a third of the foam
findings.evidence: By definition 40-vol developer releases 40 mL O2 per mL, so 50 mL gives ~2.0 L at STP, ~2.2-2.5 L at 25-60 °C. With soap, foam volume is about the gas volume. ST-07 STL: ID 126, 88 mm deep, 1.10 L gross. The annulus around the 85 mm flask is ≈0.6-0.7 L. The overflow, ~1.5 L of hot foam that still contains peroxide, runs onto the PLA tray, the PTFE glides, the four-bar and the ST-01 servo and wiring, which are 150-250 mm away. REF-BIN (110 x 80 x 100, X835-945) is off the bench and not in the BOM.
findings.required_change: Buy a PP basin of at least 6 L (e.g. ≥350 x 250 x 100 mm dish tub) and place it under the ERUPT position (flask at (450,102)). Either have the tray carry the flask over the basin rim, or stand ST-07 inside the basin, with the table edge at Y-60 still 160 mm away. Add it to the BOM with source and quantity. Route the stage servo wiring above Z60 and away from the -Y side.

findings.title: The funnel rides loose in the flask neck through the eruption, and the reaction starts at WORK under the pouring arm
findings.evidence: ST-04 payload: REF-FUNNEL-EISCO4 (102 mouth, 20 OD stem, about 40-60 g) sits in the neck at Z129-233 and translates with the tray. The run sequence is: arm pours the activated yeast into the flask at WORK, the arm withdraws, then the stage moves (1 s in load_cases, 3 s in the animation). With 12% peroxide and pre-activated yeast, foam reaches the neck within seconds. It is forced through the ~15 mm stem bore and the stem-neck annulus, can lift the loose funnel, and erupts at WORK beneath the borrowed arm's pour pose (funnel rim Z233, grasp ~Z260-300).
findings.required_change: Mount the funnel on a fixed printed arm from ST-01 or the right rail, with the stem cut to 15 mm and its tip 5 mm above the neck (Z167). The flask then leaves the funnel behind and nothing sits on the neck at ERUPT. Sequence the run so the arm retracts at least 100 mm above Z233 and the stage starts within 1 s of the pour ending. Measure the induction time on Friday's test run and record it in the README.

findings.title: CAD physical materials are wrong on many components, so the mass properties are meaningless
findings.evidence: review/design_data.json: RK-02 reagent rack = Steel (133.6 cm³ → 1.05 kg phantom; it is PLA). TT-04 = Polypropylene (it is PLA). ST-08 bearing race spacer = Steel and filed under 'HARDWARE (bought)' (it is printed PLA). REF-ROD = 'Plastic' (the BOM buys glass stir rods → Glass). REF-GLIDE-1..4 = 'Plastic' (PTFE). 'FlashHobby M45CHW + 25T disc horn' = Aluminum 6061 for the whole servo (the README says the cases are ABS). ANIM-foam is Steel, visible, 3.76e6 mm³ → 29.5 kg in the assembly. ANIM-beaker50/100 are Steel+PP. AR-01, EL-01 and REF-BOTTLE are hidden Steel leftovers. The 100 mL beakers are modelled as solid PP cylinders (546,788 mm³ ≈ 0.5 kg) and REF-BEAKER-MIX is solid too (77,585 mm³). STL filenames still say _PETG.
findings.required_change: Set RK-02, TT-04 and ST-08 to PLA (FDM), and move ST-08 out of HARDWARE into PRINT. Set REF-ROD to Glass (borosilicate), the glides to PTFE, the servo to ABS case + steel. Confirm the flask is borosilicate glass and the beakers and funnel PP. Shell the 100 mL beakers and the mix beaker (1.0 mm wall). Delete or exclude the ANIM-*, AR-01, EL-01 and REF-BOTTLE bodies. Re-export design_data.json and check that assembly mass is within 10% of the BOM-weighted mass.

findings.title: The BOM is spread over three README tables and is missing CAD and bench items
findings.evidence: Missing or unquantified: PLA filament (≈555 g tonight plus Wednesday parts plus reprints), TPU 95A filament (4 x 17.1 cm³ ≈ 85 g), PETG (listed, but the parts are PLA). The 8 x M3 x 16 SHCS and 8 x M3 hex nuts for GR-03 appear only in the gripper table: they are not in the buy list or the CAD hardware (no M3x16 or nut in design_data), and the M3 kit B0FG2BRXL3 has washers, not nuts. M1.6 x 4 motor screws are 'motor kit', unverified. M4 x 12 for the load cell is 'any M4 kit, search-only', no qty. defense.argument: Verified. auger_west.py: the DH-01 bridge is box(40,250,135 -> 100,299,148), 13.0 mm thick, with Ø3.4 clearance holes from Z148 to Z134. meshes.json, 'Measuring + auger station': both M3x12 heads sit at Z148-151 and the shanks end at Z136.0. The BOM has no M3 inserts (only ruthex M5), and a self-tapped M3 is adequate: 7 mm in Ø2.5 PLA pulls out at about π·3·7·10 MPa·0.6 ≈ 400 N, against <30 N of service load (hopper and motor ~0.1 kg plus hand loads). I also do not agree with M3x22. M3 x 22 is not in the 6-30 mm kit we already bought (B0FG2BRXL3), and M3x20 is.
defense.proposed_change: DH-01/AG-01, before tonight's print: keep the Ø2.5 x 10 pilots (Z125-135) and use SHCS M3 x 20 from the existing kit. The tip lands at Z128: 7.0 mm engagement (2.3d), 3.0 mm above the pilot bottom. Torque to snug (≤0.5 N·m), because the pilots are self-tapped PLA. Update the two CAD occurrences (M3x12 → M3x20 at (48/62, 262.5)), README fastener rows 388/513 and bom/BOM.csv. Systemic fix: add a fastener-reach check to the export. For every screw occurrence, compute the overlap length between the shank and the mating threaded feature (pilot, T-nut, insert, tapped horn) from meshes.json, and fail anything under 1.5d in PLA or 1.0d in steel or aluminium. Publish the check output in analysis/.

defense.argument: Verified by slicing exports/prints/DH-01 along Y (STL offset (40,250,135)). At Y298.95 the section is bridge only: 714 mm², X41-99, Z135.5-149.1. At Y299.00 it is tube only: 275 mm², Z144.0-164.2. The only material crossing the Y=299 plane is where the tube end disc overlaps the bridge end face, a chord segment under Z148-149 of about 22 mm² before fillets and about 45-57 mm² with them, as the reviewer found. Tube, hopper, yeast, DH-02 and the N20 torque reaction all pass through it. One correction to the mechanism: in the Z-up print, the Y=299 plane cuts across every layer, so the bending stress is along the layers, not across them. The torsional shear on the 4 mm strip acts mainly on vertical planes. The conclusion still holds. A ~50 mm² notched strip carrying ~26 cm³ of cantilevered part plus 0.25-0.35 N·m of motor stall torque, and printed on tree supports, is not acceptable. DH-01 prints tonight, so the fix costs only CAD time.
defense.proposed_change: auger_west.py: add dh.box(79,299,135, 95,350,152) (JOIN) before the bore and slot cuts, so the Ø13/Ø14 bore re-cuts its top. Add R3 fillets on the web-to-bridge, web-to-tube and web-to-hopper re-entrant edges, applied explicitly and not through process4. Stop at Y350 so the Ø10 outlet (Y365-375) stays open. The web bottom at Z135 clears the carousel beaker rims (Z121.2) by 13.8 mm. Acceptance before slicing: the Y=299.0 section must be ≥700 mm² continuous (the bridge face is now fully joined), and the Y=320 section (web 16 x 13.5 below the bore + tube ring + hopper walls) must be ≥600 mm². Record both values in analysis/load_cases.md. The motor-face M1.6 holes (Y292-308) are unaffected.

defense.argument: The over-constraint is real. The deck is located radially by the 25T spline and is also VHB-bonded to the lazy Susan top plate, while the bottom plate is VHB-bonded to TT-01 with no locating feature. Any offset between the lazy-Susan axis and the spline axis must be taken up by shearing the 2 x 1.1 mm of VHB. I think the magnitude is overstated. 4950 is viscoelastic, with a quasi-static shear modulus nearer 0.1-0.3 MPa than 0.5, and a stamped lazy Susan has some radial play (not yet measured), so the realistic load is a few hundred N, not 0.8-2.5 kN. That is still enough to load the servo output bearing and peel the tape, so it gets fixed. I reject the specific fix. A Ø53 spigot on TT-01 means reprinting a part that is already done (4 h 31, 200 g), and the PTFE sheet is a new purchase. Neither is needed. Removing one of the two bonds removes the redundant constraint at zero cost and with zero change to the stack height. Floating the bottom plate is better than floating the deck: the lazy Susan stays captive under the deck, and the only radial force the servo can see is friction, μ·N ≈ 0.3 x ~6 N ≈ 2 N. If the bottom plate turns with the deck instead of rolling, the friction torque is ≈0.3·6 N·0.04 m = 0.07 N·m against 3.4 N·m available (SF ~48).
defense.proposed_change: No reprint and no new parts. Stack and assembly: (1) Stick the lower VHB layer to the TT-01 corner pads and leave its red liner on, so the lazy Susan bottom plate rests on the liner and is NOT bonded. (2) Bond the lazy Susan top plate to the deck underside with the upper VHB layer. Centre it by eye on the Ø9 deck hole; concentricity no longer matters. (3) Bolt the deck to the horn as before. The stack height is unchanged: 43.0 → VHB 1.1 + 0.1 liner → lazy Susan 44.2-53.6 → VHB 1.1 → deck 54.6. The extra 0.1 mm liner compresses into the foam, so the horn shim stays at 0.5 mm. Update the README turntable stack line and fastener row 520 to 'VHB 1 layer, top plate → deck; lower layer liner-on, not bonded (bottom plate floats)'. Add a Friday check: rotate the deck by hand through ±70° with the servo unpowered; it must turn with less than ~0.1 N·m and no tape shear visible.

defense.argument: I agree that load_cases.py has no Kt and no impact case. Neither the claimed Kt nor the proposed fix survives measurement, though. (a) Geometry: I sliced ST-01 around (653,112) and (653,172). The Ø18 posts are freestanding from Z~5 to Z66. The web is on one side only, a ~120° sector facing the servo, and ends at Z35.3. The fillet there is not R0.7: the radial excess is 1.5 mm at 0.1 mm above the web, 0.8 at 0.5, 0.4 at 1.0 and 0.15 at 1.7, which fits R≈2-2.5. The crank load at the stop is tangential (±X), which puts that web and fillet on the neutral axis. The peak fibres at ±X run straight past Z35.3 with no shoulder. This is not a full shoulder with r/d=0.04, and Kt ≈1.2, not 2.4. At static stall (147 N at Z61, 25.7 mm lever, Z=573 mm³): σ_nom 6.6 MPa, peak ≈7.9 MPa, SF 2.5 against 20 MPa and 1.26 against the reviewer's 10 MPa. This is a two-fault accident case: the firmware clamp and the soft limit both have to fail. (b) Impact: k_post = 3.2 kN/mm ignores the series compliance of the 150 mm PLA crank, which has k ≈ 3EI/L³ = 34 N/mm for the 127 mm beyond the contact. Using that, a 1 s move hitting the stop gives F_post ≈250 N and σ ≈11 MPa. A 3 s move gives ≈83 N and 3.7 MPa, not 0.5 kN and 58 MPa. (c) The required change would break the stage. The crank (20 wide) meets a post 30.15 mm from the pivot at α = 84.3° − asin((10+r+t)/30.15). As built that is 45.2°. A Ø22 post with a 3 mm sleeve gives 31.5°, below the 36.87° that WORK and ERUPT need, so the stage could never reach either station. A 3 mm sleeve on Ø18 gives 37.4°, a 0.5° margin. This is not a blocker and does not justify an ST-01 reprint. The real control is not letting the servo be commanded past ±40°.
defense.proposed_change: 1) Firmware (software plan §7): a hard pulse clamp derived from the no-linkage sweep that the README already requires (measure µs/deg), set so that |α| ≤ 40°. The Mega refuses any stage pulse outside it, whichever pulse table is loaded. Stage moves take ≥3 s with the smoothstep profile, which makes the worst-case impact load 83 N. 2) Bumper: print 2 x ST-09 TPU 95A sleeves (ID 18.3, wall 1.2 mm = 3 perimeters, 14 mm tall, covering Z54-68) on the GR-03 TPU plate. The stop moves to α ≈42.2°, which keeps 2.2° beyond the ±40° soft limit and 5.3° beyond 36.87°. Never use a sleeve thicker than 1.5 mm (41.5°). 3) load_cases.py: post row with Kt=1.2 (σ_peak 7.9 MPa), classed as an accident case (criterion SF ≥1.0 against 10 MPa, ≥2 against 20 MPa), plus an impact row with the crank compliance for 1 s and 3 s moves. 4) Optional, not gating: if the H2D is idle for 4 h after the Wednesday plates, print an ST-01 v2 with the webs raised from Z35.3 to Z54 (2 mm under the crank at Z56; free length 25.7 → 7 mm), the same Ø18 posts at the same positions (so the stop angle is unchanged), and R3 at the web-to-post junction. Keep the current ST-01 as a spare.

defense.argument: Correct on both counts. An ISO 10642 head (dk ≈8.96) in a Ø5.0 hole, with its top at Z37.0 and the boss at Z36.2, cuts a ~1.2 mm cone into the borrowed Base_SO101. That violates the BRIEF's 'don't drill or modify', and the 90° wedge also puts hoop stress on the PLA boss. meshes.json gives the CSK M4x20 tip at Z17.0 against T-nuts at Z14.4-18.2: 1.2 mm of engagement (~1.7 threads). The CSK row goes. I reject the M4 x 22 lengths. The T-nut ends at Z14.4 and the 2020 core is at Z13.9, so full engagement without bottoming needs the tip in a 0.5 mm window. ISO 4762/7380 length tolerance at 22 mm is js15, ±0.42 mm, so a 22 mm screw ends between Z13.78 and Z14.62. Some screws will bottom on the core and leave the arm unclamped. 22 is also not a standard ISO 7380 length and is not in the M4 x 20 pack we bought. 2.0 mm (2.9 threads) is enough because the borrowed PLA boss limits the preload anyway. Head bearing for dk 7.0-7.6 on a Ø5 hole is 19-26 mm² x ~50 MPa ≈ 0.9-1.3 kN, which is a ≈0.6 N·m torque ceiling. Thread strip in a steel T-nut at 2.0 mm is ≈1.8 kN with a 0.5 knock-down, so SF ≈2.4 at installation and ≈45 against the 38 N service load.
defense.proposed_change: Front row: ISO 7380 M4 x 20 button heads (dk 7.6, k 2.2). They seat on the unmodified boss at Z36.2, the head top is at Z38.4, and the tip is at Z16.2 (2.0 mm engagement, same as the back row). Back row: unchanged, SHCS M4 x 20. Install all 8 arm screws at 0.6 N·m with medium threadlock. Delete README lines 37-42 about the countersink seat and the BOM row for B082PZY652. Add 4 x ISO 7380 M4x20 to bom/BOM.csv. Planner: the button head leaves 0.4 mm under the 38.8 shoulder-link sweep. Add a shoulder soft limit so the shoulder link stays ≥ Z41.4 within 10 mm (XY) of the front-row holes, update the screw meshes, and re-run the plan3 audit to confirm no planned pose violates it. Update the arm-base row in load_cases.py: 2.0 mm engagement and the PLA-limited preload.

defense.argument: AG-01 has not been printed yet, so I'll take the geometry changes. They cost CAD time only, and they apply the large-base-fillet rule the review is right to enforce on a 123 mm pillar. Two of the numbers are wrong, though. (1) Stress: the post is 30 x 25 (747 mm², Z_x 3750 mm³, Z_y 3125 mm³). A 20 N push at Z180 gives a root moment of 3.36 N·m and σ = 0.9-1.1 MPa across layers. That is SF ~9 even against 10 MPa with Kt 1.9, so the post is not near failure. (2) Rocking: the foot bears on the table, so a −X push pivots about the foot's X40 edge, and the bar end both lifts 30θ and rotates. Beam-matrix stiffness: k_θ = 3.85e5 N·mm/rad, θ = 0.54° and 1.9 mm at the hopper, not 3.5° and 11 mm. The soft direction is a −Y push (pivot at Y250): bending plus torsion of the bar give k_θ = 1.21e5 N·mm/rad, θ = 1.7° and 6.1 mm at Z205. That is worth fixing, and 30 x 16 brings it to 0.46° and 1.7 mm. I reject moving the print off the A1. With an 80 x 80 foot plus a 230 mm bar footprint, a 135 mm post is stable on a bed-slinger, and moving it adds schedule risk for no structural gain.
defense.proposed_change: auger_west.py, AG-01 v2 (tonight's A1 plate): foot box(20,235,0 → 100,315,12). It sits under the deck (Z<54.6), clear of TT-01 (X≥120), and the post's nearest corner is 141.6 mm from the turntable axis against a 118 mm deck radius. Add an R8 fillet at the post-to-foot junction on all four sides, applied explicitly. Replace the 6 x 25 x 58 gusset with two 8 mm gussets on the +X and +Y faces, 40 mm along the foot at the root and tapering to zero at Z100, with R5 at both ends and R3 at the gusset-to-post edges. Bar: 30 wide x 16 tall (Y282-312, Z0-16), still 3 mm clear of TT-01 at Y315. Saddle per M-07. Keep the A1, oriented with the bar along the A1's Y (bed) axis. Add an 'AG-01 hand load, 20 N at Z180, ±X and ±Y' row to load_cases with the corrected stiffness model (≤0.5° required).

defense.argument: Verified. In meshes.json the left Y-rail starts at Y290.0, and the AG-01 T-nut at Y291 spans Y285.5-296.5, so 4.5 of its 11 mm hang past the open rail end. The saddle (Y283-321, from agfix.py) overhangs the rail by 7 mm. A T-nut that half-overhangs an open slot tips out under preload. TT-01's saddle on this rail occupies Y340-400 (sliced from the TT-01 STL) and its T-nut is at Y349.5-360.5, so there is room to do better than the reviewer's 13 mm bolt spacing.
defense.proposed_change: In the same AG-01 v2 as M-01/M-06: saddle Y290-335 (45 mm of rail, 5 mm short of TT-01's saddle at Y340), channel cut Y289-336. Bolts at (255, 300) and (255, 322), giving T-nuts at Y294.5-305.5 and Y316.5-327.5: fully under the lips, 11 mm apart, 22 mm clear of TT-01's T-nut. defense.argument: The process criticism stands. fillet_lib.process4/iterative_g applies one r_in (1.5-2.0) to every concave edge, falls back to 0.6r and then 0.35r without reporting, and nothing checks the result against a load path. That is how DH-01 ended up with 0.35 mm and the DH-02, GR-01, GR-02 and GR-03 roots ended up with none. It needs fixing. I won't reprint parts that are already printed just for fillets when the numbers don't call for it. ST-04 tray posts (printed Tuesday): stall load 29.4 N at 49 mm on Ø20 (Z = 785 mm³) gives σ_nom 1.8 MPa. With the reviewer's Kt 2.7, peak 4.9 MPa, SF 2.0 against 10 MPa and 4.1 against 20. This is reached only at servo stall, since the tray weight rides on the glides. The ST-01 idler post (Ø24) carries the same 29 N, with lower stress. ST-01 stop posts: see M-04 (measured R≈2, Kt ≈1.2). TT-04 wall side load: the 10 N drag case goes away once M-13 makes the approach vertical with lead-ins, and the wall is a ring, not the flat 20 mm strip the 8.3 MPa estimate assumes.
defense.proposed_change: 1) Replace the blanket pass with an explicit fillet spec table in each part script (edge → radius), applied before process4. process4 then handles only cosmetic edges and must log every fallback. 2) Add an export gate: list every concave edge within a load-path box, with its as-built radius, and FAIL below spec instead of silently accepting 0.35r. Publish it as analysis/fillet_report.md. 3) Unprinted parts (AG-01, WS-01, DH-01, DH-02 tonight; RK-02, TT-04, WS-02 and GR-01/02/03 if not yet started): AG-01 R8/R5/R3 (M-06); WS-01 pedestal-to-saddle R4; DH-01 web joints R3 (M-02); DH-02 collar-to-hub R2 (M-09); TT-04 pocket roots R1.5 inside and outside; RK-02 pocket-wall roots R1.5; GR-01/GR-02 tongue roots R1.5, with a matching 1.5 x 45° chamfer on the GR-03 slot mouth (M-14). 4) Printed parts (ST-01, ST-04, TT-01 etc.): no reprint for fillets. Record the as-built roots and their Kt-adjusted SF in load_cases (ST-04 tray post SF 2.0 accident / 4.1 conservative).

defense.argument: Verified on exports/prints/DH-02. The section is 62.9 mm² up to z=6.9, 28.3 mm² at z=7.1-7.9 (the D-bore runs 1 mm past the r4.5 collar into the r2.6 hub, leaving a ~1 mm wall with a sharp step), and 35.0 mm² beyond z=8. The part prints upright, so torsion puts its shear on the layer planes. The flight geometry is also as stated. A 2 mm-wide blade with a 16 mm lead has a normal thickness of 2·sin(atan(16/(2π·6))) = 0.78 mm at the tip and 1.4 mm at the hub, with a ~67° overhang printed on tree supports inside a helix. There is also a real contradiction: docs/software_architecture.md §6 says 100 % PWM, while README line 429 says ~70 %. On stall detection: the plain N20 has no encoder and the TB6612 has no current sense, so 'no speed change in 300 ms' cannot be measured as specified. Either buy the $3 encoder N20 or rely on the redesigned screw surviving a stall. With the fixes below it does: at 70 % PWM, ~0.25 N·m stall on a Ø7 solid hub gives τ = 3.7 MPa x 1.3 ≈ 4.8 MPa, SF ~2 against 10 MPa, and the flights carry more on top of that.
defense.proposed_change: aug2.py, DH-02 v2 (tonight): Ø9 collar to z=12 (the 8 mm D-bore then has 4 mm of solid beyond it). R2 fillet from collar to hub. Hub Ø7. Flights in a buttress profile, ≥1.6 mm normal thickness, flat on the pushing (outlet) side, 45° underside flank. OD Ø12.0 (see M-10). Prints upright with no supports. Firmware/software: cap TB6612 PWM at 70 % (≈5.9 V from 8.4 V) and correct §6. Add the encoder N20 (6 V 60 rpm, magnetic 7 PPR) to bom/BOM.csv as the auger motor. Stall detection: encoder count unchanged for 300 ms → stop, reverse ½ rev, retry once, then fault 'auger jam'. Without the encoder, rely on the VERIFY_YEAST weight check. Add the row 'Auger jam at stall, 0.25 N·m at 70 % PWM, collar and hub torsion with Kt' to load_cases.

defense.argument: Agreed on clearance. The flight rectangle's corners sit at r = √(6²+1²) = 6.08, so the radial clearance in the Ø13 bore is 0.42 mm. A horizontal FDM bore sags at the crown, the tree supports the README calls for would scar the inside, and granules of 0.3-1.5 mm would wedge in the gap. DH-01 and DH-02 print tonight, so the fix is free. I reject the tip pin and bushing. A Ø3 pin in a Ø3.4 bushing is a 0.2 mm journal right next to the outlet. Yeast packs into it and it becomes the jam point, which is worse than the problem it solves. Tip runout from the N20 shaft and D-bore play (~0.1-0.2 mm at the motor end, ≤0.5 mm at the free end of the 62 mm screw) fits inside the 0.95-1.0 mm clearance below, and the screw carries almost no radial load (2.4 g plus loose granules).
defense.proposed_change: auger_west.py, DH-01: bore Ø14.0 with a 45° teardrop crown (the peak sits 0.9 mm above the circle, so it prints without supports). In Bambu Studio, put a support blocker over the bore and slot volume; tree supports only under the hopper overhangs. After printing, ream by hand with a 14 mm drill. DH-02: flight OD Ø12.0, giving 1.0 mm radial clearance. No tip support. Before packing on Thursday morning: run the assembled auger 2 min at 70 % PWM with real instant yeast. Pass criteria: no squeal or rub, dose repeatability within ±0.3 g over 3 x 10 revolutions (this feeds calibrate_auger.py).

defense.argument: The finding is right, though the fin-ray stiffness (0.3-0.8 N/mm) is an unmeasured estimate, as is any number I would give. That uncertainty is the reason to close on force rather than position. With position control, grip force = k_series x 4.2 mm, so it depends entirely on a stiffness nobody has measured. The demand is well established. For a 100 mL beaker with 80 mL developer, W = 1.06 N, and in the upright carry gravity shears the contact. Wet PP on TPU gives μ ≈0.3, so N ≥ 2·1.06/(2·0.3) = 3.5 N per finger, or 5.3 N with the ±1 g shake. The V-tips do not help against axial slip. The software plan already allows gripper load up to 85 %, so a torque-limited close fits the existing architecture.
defense.proposed_change: Gripper control: command q = −70° (the existing hard limit; the fingers touch at −75°) with the STS3215 torque limit set to a calibrated value, so the jaw stalls on the beaker at the target normal force. Calibrate on the first printed GR-03 set on Wednesday or Thursday. Pull a water-filled 100 mL beaker axially out of the grip with a luggage scale, and set the torque limit to the lowest value that gives a pull-out ≥ 2.2 N (SF 2 at 1 g, wet). Record the torque limit and the end angle in config.yaml. Grasp-miss threshold moves from ≤−68° to ≤−69.5°. Add 1 mm self-adhesive silicone rubber strip (20 x 30 mm per finger, 4 fingers) to the contact faces for μ ≥0.6, and add it to bom/BOM.csv. Software: after every grasp, lift 5 mm, hold 0.5 s and check that the scale or present-position shows < 1 mm drift before transferring. Add a 'Grip friction vs. beaker + liquid at 1 g shake' row to load_cases.

defense.argument: Correct that the plan3 roll pour (qt[4] += ±100° about e1, hinge vertical) points the lowest rim point along the closing direction e2, so it lands at a finger. GRIP_H puts the finger top 1 mm above the 50 mL rim (45 + 17 = 62 vs 61) and 5 mm below the 100 mL rim (52 + 17 = 69 vs 74). Lowering the grasp fixes this: the stream then leaves the lip ≥7-10 mm beyond the finger along the now-horizontal beaker axis and falls clear. The 50 mL change has a constraint the reviewer skipped. With the 34 mm finger, GRIP_H 34 puts the finger bottom at 17 mm, only 1 mm above the 16 mm TT-04 walls, which is less than arm Z error. I reject the spout key notch. The EISCO spout is a pinched lip at the rim, 45-60 mm above any pocket wall, and the beaker body is round where it sits in the 12-16 mm pockets. A notch there engages nothing and cannot index the spout.
defense.proposed_change: plan3.py GRIP_H: 100 mL 52 → 40. The finger spans 23-57 mm: 17 mm under the 74 mm rim, 13 mm over the RK-02 10 mm walls. 50 mL: if TT-04 has not been printed, cut its pocket walls 16 → 12 mm and use GRIP_H 34 (finger 17-51: 10 mm under the rim, 5 mm over the wall). If TT-04 is already printed, use GRIP_H 37 (finger 20-54: 7 mm under the rim, 4 mm over the wall). Spout orientation: engrave a 0.6 mm-deep arrow at every TT-04, RK-02 and WS-02 pocket. The operator places each beaker spout-to-arrow, and each arrow points to the downhill side for that station's fixed roll sign in plan3. Re-run plan3 for all pick, place and pour poses with the new GRIP_H and commit the audit (M-29).

defense.argument: Verified. plan3.py line 19 opens to contact + 5°, while gripper_design.json specifies q_open = contact + 14° (−46° for 43 mm, −33.3° for 56 mm). At ~60 mm that is ±2.6 mm, below real SO-101 accuracy. The pockets have no lead-in. I accept the larger opening and the lead-ins, with one caveat. The README rejected wide opening because the 100 mm fingers can swing into neighbouring carousel beakers, which leave a 24.4 mm gap at the 67.4 mm pitch. So +14° must be confirmed by the audit, not assumed. The teach step is not new: docs/software_architecture.md §3 already specifies teach.py, which jogs each arm to each pick and place, records the joint vectors, and blends the last 60 mm of the approach toward the taught pose (corrections capped at 15 mm/8°). What is missing is making it mandatory (see M-29).
defense.proposed_change: plan3.py: OPEN = contact + 14°. Run the audit against the TT-04 neighbours, the RK-02 beakers and the WS-02 ring. If any move collides, use the largest opening that clears, but not less than contact + 9° (±4.7 mm at 60 mm), and record the per-station value. Add a 3 x 45° lead-in chamfer to the rim of every pocket on parts not yet printed (TT-04, RK-02, WS-02 ring). If TT-04 is already printed, cut the chamfer by hand with a countersink bit or deburring tool. Software: PRECHECK refuses to run unless config.yaml has a taught pose for every pick, place and pour target (M-29).

defense.argument: Verified in gripper_ops.py. The slot is tongue(SL=0.15): v 1.85-22.15 (20.3 wide), z −21.65 to −16.35 (5.3 high), open only at u = −12. The finger prints lying on its profile (z vertical), so the slot roof is a 20.3 mm TPU bridge, and TPU sags 0.5-1.5 mm over that span. design_data shows no fillets on GR-01, GR-02 or GR-03. None of the gripper parts are printed yet, so every change here is free. A full 45° gable over a 20.3 mm slot would rise ~10 mm into the finger, so the practical version is edge chamfers plus more clearance, then trimming whatever droops.
defense.proposed_change: gripper_ops.py: SL 0.15 → 0.25 per side (slot 5.5 x 20.5). Add 2 x 45° chamfers along both long roof edges of the slot, which cuts the bridge to 16.5 mm, and matching 2 x 45° chamfers on the top long edges of the GR-01/GR-02 tongues. Add a 1 x 45° lead-in at the tongue tip (u = −1.5) and R1.5 at the tongue roots (M-08). Slice GR-03 with a height-range modifier at 100 % infill for the base block (u < 0), bridge fan 100 %, bridge speed ≤15 mm/s. Use M3 nylon-insert locknuts (DIN 985) in place of plain hex nuts, 8 pcs, in bom/BOM.csv. Re-export GR-02 with the hinge axis vertical, like GR-01. Print one GR-03 plus one GR-01 first and test-fit the tongue (slides in by hand, no visible gap at the clamp) before printing the other three fingers.

defense.argument: I agree there is no overload stop. WS-01 is printing tonight, so adding one is free. I also agree that splash protection is cheap insurance over an aluminium cell and the HX711. The overload mechanism is overstated. The arm presses the scale beaker down through the TPU fingers, and the beaker slides in the grip once the axial force exceeds the friction 2μN ≈ 2·0.5·5 N ≈ 5 N (with the M-11 grip force). With the finger bottom ≥17 mm above the beaker base, the fingers cannot reach the pan. A Z error in placement therefore puts about 6 N plus the beaker weight on the cell, not 20-30 N, unless something jams. Those 20-30 N do arise from a hand leaning on the pan, a dropped beaker, or transport. A fixed 0.4 mm printed gap is not a precise stop: a 1 kg bar cell deflects only ~0.2-0.3 mm at full scale, and the print tolerance on a 0.4 mm gap is ±0.2 mm. On the skirt: anything hanging from the pan that touches WS-01 or the cell's fixed end shunts the load path and silently corrupts every pour, so its clearance must be verified.
defense.proposed_change: WS-01 (tonight): add a Ø10 boss under the WS-02 rim on the far side from the cell's fixed end, at (490, 475) or wherever the CAD shows a free spot ≥15 mm from the cell. Give it an M3 heat-free pilot (Ø2.5) for an M3 x 12 set screw that acts as an adjustable stop. At assembly, set the gap with two sheets of printer paper (~0.2 mm) under a 1 kg calibration load, which gives overload protection at ~1.5-2x FS. WS-02 (if not printed): grow to Ø90 with a 3 mm raised rim lip (holds ~19 mL of spill). Skirt 6 mm down only if the interference check shows ≥2 mm clearance from WS-01 (top Z45) and the cell's fixed end at every point; otherwise no skirt. Wrap the cell body and the HX711 board in cling film (consumable, in the BOM). Add an 'Arm place force vs cell overload (grip-slip limited 6 N; stop at 1.5-2x FS)' row to load_cases.

defense.argument: The documentation is inconsistent and I accept the fixes. README line 66 says PLA, but the load-case row, the print schedule and the STL names say PETG, and the BRIEF mandates PLA. I agree with the adiabatic bound. 50 mL of 12 % (6.27 g, 0.184 mol x 98.2 kJ/mol = 18.1 kJ) into ~111 g of liquid (445 J/K) plus a ~115 g flask (95 J/K) gives ΔT ≈ 34 K. From a ~29 °C mix (developer and soap at room temperature, yeast water at 40 °C) that is ≈62 °C. In practice it will be lower, because most of the heat leaves in the foam. 62 °C is above PLA's ~55 °C HDT, but the collar and well carry almost no stress (flask ~0.3 kg on hundreds of mm²: kPa) and see a few minutes per run, so creep is negligible. Warping of the thin well wall over ~10 runs is the plausible failure. I reject reprinting ST-07 to 3.2 mm walls. It is printed and unloaded, and under M-17 it stops being the primary containment.
defense.proposed_change: 1) Put a 3 mm cork pad, cut to Ø80, under the flask in the ST-05 socket (cork trivet or coaster sheet, in bom/BOM.csv). The flask rises 3 mm, so the neck goes to Z165; update the funnel-tip height in M-18. 2) Cap the developer charge at 40 mL in the README and recipe (adiabatic ≈56 °C; also sizes the foam for M-17) and delete 'go up to 75 mL'. 3) Rename ST-04/05/07 *_PETG → plain names, set the print table to PLA and delete the 'PETG' sentence at line 93. 4) load_cases: replace the PETG row with 'Hot-wetted PLA: adiabatic 56 °C (40 mL) / 62 °C (50 mL) vs PLA HDT 55 °C, near-zero stress; check ST-07 roundness after each test run'. 5) Rinse the parts with cold water right after each run (already in README).

defense.argument: Correct on volume. 40-vol means 40 mL O2 per mL, so 50 mL gives ~2.0 L at STP and ~2.3 L warm. ST-07 is Ø126 ID x 88 deep (1.10 L gross), leaving ~0.65 L of annulus around the flask, so ~1.5 L of warm, peroxide-bearing foam overflows. I reject the required change because it is incompatible with the stage. The tray (ST-04, Z6-55) rides on PTFE glides on the table at Z0, translating 180 mm from WORK (Y214-420) to ERUPT (Y34-240). A ≥6 L basin with 100 mm walls under the ERUPT position sits directly in the tray's path, so the tray cannot 'carry the flask over the basin rim'. Putting ST-07 inside a basin is the same problem, because ST-07 rides on the tray. What actually protects the hardware is a smaller charge plus a disposable surface and protected wiring.
defense.proposed_change: 1) Live demo charge 40 mL of developer (≈1.6 L O2 at STP, ≈1.9 L warm), per M-16. 2) Lay a 1.2 x 2.4 m plastic drop cloth under the whole bench before clamping (the frame clamps over it), and ring the ERUPT footprint (X330-570, Y−60 to 250) with absorbent pads. 3) Cover the ST-01 servo with cling film and route the stage servo lead up along the right rail above Z60 and away from −Y. 4) Optional upgrade if a teammate finds one by Thursday morning: replace ST-07 with a bought clear PP round container, OD ≤150 mm (1 mm clear of the tray posts at X526), height ≤150 mm (rim ≤Z160, under the funnel), floor ID ≥127 so ST-05 sits in it. That holds ≈2.3 L. 5) Add drop cloth, absorbent pads, cling film and the optional container to bom/BOM.csv with quantities. Add a 'Foam volume vs containment' row to load_cases (40 mL: 1.9 L vs 0.65 L well + cloth).

defense.argument: The safety part is right and is the more important half. With pre-activated yeast, foaming starts within seconds, and the current plan has the arm pour at WORK, withdraw, and only then start the stage (1 s in load_cases, 3 s in the animation). That lets the reaction begin under a borrowed arm. A loose PP funnel (40-60 g, 20 mm stem in a ~30 mm neck) will be lifted and tipped by foam forced through the neck. At ERUPT that happens 180 mm in front of the arms and is mostly a mess and cosmetic problem, but at WORK it is not. A fixed funnel is the right end state. It is a new printed part with a ~230 mm cantilever across the arm workspace, though, so it can only ship if plan3 shows it is clear. That cannot be assumed the night before the flight.
defense.proposed_change: 1) Sequence (software plan §4, mandatory): A_YEAST_TO_FLASK ends with arm A retracting ≥100 mm above the funnel rim (above Z333). STAGE_OUT starts ≤1 s after the pour cut-off and the move takes 3 s (M-04). On Friday's test run, measure the time from pour to first foam at the neck and record it in the README. If it is under 6 s, reduce the yeast pre-activation wait in WAIT_ACTIVATE. 2) Funnel: design FN-01, a saddle on the right Y-rail at Y318-372 (between ST-01 and RK-02), a post to Z200 and a beam to a ring holding the funnel cone at (450,282). Cut the stem to 15 mm with the tip at Z170 (5 mm above the neck at Z165 with the M-16 cork pad), so the flask leaves the funnel behind. Ship it only if a plan3 re-run with FN-01 in the scene shows zero collisions and ≥10 mm clearance for both arms by Thursday 06:00. 3) Fallback if FN-01 does not clear: the funnel rides in the neck as now. Accept that it may tip at ERUPT, and put it on the absorbent pads of M-17.

defense.argument: Verified in review/design_data.json. RK-02 = Steel (133.6 cm³ → ~1.05 kg phantom). TT-04 = Polypropylene. ST-08 = Steel and filed under HARDWARE (q7). REF-ROD = 'Plastic'. REF-GLIDE-1..4 = 'Plastic'. 'FlashHobby M45CHW + 25T disc horn' = Aluminum 6061 for the whole servo. ANIM-foam = Steel at 3.76e6 mm³ and visible (~29.5 kg). ANIM-beaker50/100 = PP+Steel. AR-01, EL-01 and REF-BOTTLE are hidden Steel leftovers. 'EISCO 100 mL PP beaker x3' is one solid body of 546,788 mm³, and REF-BEAKER-MIX is solid (77,585 mm³). REF-FLASK-250 is correctly Glass and the funnel correctly PP. These are CAD-only fixes with no print impact.
defense.proposed_change: Run a matfix3.py pass. RK-02, TT-04 and ST-08 → PLA (FDM); move ST-08 from HARDWARE (bought) to PRINT. REF-ROD → Glass (borosilicate; custom material ρ 2.23). REF-GLIDE-1..4 → PTFE (custom, ρ 2.2). M45CHW → ABS case body plus a steel gear/output proxy, with the Treedix horn kept as Al 6061. REF-LAZY-SUSAN stays Steel. Confirm REF-FLASK-250 Glass, and beakers and funnel PP. Shell REF-BEAKER-MIX, the scale 50 mL beaker and the three 100 mL beakers to 1.0 mm walls and split the x3 body into three bodies. Exclude ANIM-*, AR-01, EL-01, REF-BOTTLE and REF-TABLE from the mass roll-up (move them to a hidden 'NON-BOM' component). Re-export review/design_data.json and add a check that the assembly mass (excluding arms and table) is within 10 % of the BOM-weighted mass from bom/BOM.csv.

defense.argument: Verified. The T-nut count is wrong. Saddle positions are TT-01 2, ST-01 2, AG-01 2, RK-02 2 and WS-01 2 = 10, plus 8 bracket = 18 M5 T-nuts, against the README's 12. The 120-pack covers it, so there is no extra purchase, only a wrong count. design_data quantities are inflated by one by the HW-LIB masters (M45CHW q3, clamps q3, inserts q4, M5x20 q4, ST-08 q7). The GR-03 M3x16 screws and nuts are missing from the CAD hardware and the buy list, and the M3 kit has washers, not nuts. The rack screw appears as both M5x10 and M5x12. Glassware is split between the Amazon and Boston tables, and filament and tools are absent. One machine-readable BOM is the right answer.
defense.proposed_change: Create bom/BOM.csv with columns: id, cad_component, description, material, qty_required, qty_to_buy, pack_size, source_link, status, notes. Rows: every printed part with filament grams (PLA and TPU 95A totals, including tonight's reprints); every bought part from design_data with the masters excluded; fasteners at the corrected lengths (M3x20 for DH-01 per M-01; ISO 7380 M4x20 x4 and SHCS M4x20 x4 per M-05; M3x12 x4 for the deck per M-21; M3x16 x8 plus M3 nylon locknuts x8 for GR-03; M5x12 everywhere for saddles and rack); 18 M5 T-nuts and 8 M4 T-nuts; M5 inserts x3; F625ZZ x6; glassware (2 x Karter 250 mL borosilicate Erlenmeyer, 4 x glass stir rods 6.35 x 150, 100 mL graduated cylinder); PP beakers (50 mL qty = 7 TT-04 + 1 scale + 1 mix + 2 spare = 11; 100 mL qty 3 + spares); funnel; consumables (3M 4950 VHB, cork pad, silicone grip strip, cling film, drop cloth, absorbent pads, medium threadlock); encoder N20; tools (soldering iron/Pinecil for inserts, hex keys 2.0/2.5/3/4 ≤7 in, 14 mm drill for reaming, countersink bit, feeler paper, luggage scale, kitchen thermometer); safety (glasses, gloves). Generate the hardware rows from design_data by script. Replace the README buy tables with a short summary and a link to bom/BOM.csv.

defense.argument: The numbers are right. Saddle M5x12: head at Z28, tip at Z16, T-nut Z14.4-18.2, so 2.2 mm (2.75 threads). Carousel M3x10: tip Z48.6 in the Z48-50 horn flange, 1.4 mm. The adequacy is overstated for the printed saddles. M5 strip in a steel T-nut at 2.2 mm is ≈π·5·2.2·0.58·250 MPa·0.5 ≈ 2.5 kN with a 0.5 knock-down. Preload is capped by the PLA roof under the head: (8.5² − 5.5²)·π/4 = 33 mm² x 50 MPa ≈ 1.65 kN, i.e. ≈1.65 N·m. So SF ≈1.5 at installation and >40 against the <50 N service loads. That does not justify reprinting TT-01 or ST-01 (8 h 49 of printing). Where the part is unprinted (AG-01, WS-01 tonight), the counterbore is free and I'll take it. The deck screw is worth fixing: M3x12 is in the kit, gives the full 2.0 mm flange, and its tip at Z46.6 is 4.1 mm above the servo case (Z42.5) and clear of the Ø8 spline hub (screws at r = 7 ± 1.5 vs hub r = 4).
defense.proposed_change: Carousel deck: SHCS M3 x 12 (kit), 4 pcs, replacing M3x10. Update the CAD occurrence and README row 519. AG-01 and WS-01 saddle roofs: Ø10 x 2 mm counterbores, so the M5x12 heads sit at Z26 with the tip at Z14.0: 4.2 mm, past the full 3.8 mm T-nut and 0.1 mm above the 2020 core at 13.9 (if that margin is too tight in CAD, make the counterbore 1.5 mm deep: tip 14.5, 3.7 mm engagement). TT-01/ST-01: no reprint. Torque spec M5 into PLA saddle 1.5 N·m, M4 arm bolts 0.6 N·m (M-05). Add an engagement column (mm and threads) to the README fastener table, generated by the M-01 reach check.

defense.argument: Correct. The ST-05 disc OD (126.0) equals the ST-07 ID (126.0), a line-to-line fit. With elephant's foot on the ST-05 bed edge and any inward lean of the 2 mm ST-07 wall, it becomes an interference fit. Both parts are printed, so the fix is to sand the collar, not reprint.
defense.proposed_change: Thursday fit check: drop ST-05 into ST-07. If it does not seat freely, sand the ST-05 outer edge to ≈124.8-125.0 OD (0.5-0.6 mm/side), mainly the bottom 1 mm (elephant's foot), with 120-grit on a flat block. Update the CAD: ST-05 disc OD 124.8 for future exports. Add 'ST-05 ↔ ST-07: 0.6 mm/side' to the README verification table and to the clearance check, which must flag zero-gap contacts between parts that are supposed to slide.

defense.argument: The shield contact is plausible: the F625ZZ inner-ring land is ~7.5 mm, and a Ø8 spacer can reach the shield, so I accept reducing the OD. Two parts of the required change are wrong. (1) DIN 988 shims for d=5 are 5 x 10, which is bigger still and definitely on the shield; '5 x 7 x 1 DIN 988' is not a standard size. (2) Torquing to 1.5 N·m makes the crushing worse. M5 preload is F ≈ T/(0.2d) = 1.5 kN, and on a Ø7/Ø5.3 annulus (16.4 mm²) that is ~90 MPa, which crushes any PLA spacer and approaches the pull-out of a 9.5 mm heat-set insert in PLA. This is a pivot pin and needs no preload. The inner races only need to be located axially; if they creep on the screw, nothing is lost.
defense.proposed_change: Reprint 6 x ST-08 at Ø7.2/Ø5.3 x 1.0, 100 % infill (~10 min, any printer). Torque the three pivot M5x20 screws to snug, ≤0.5 N·m (≈0.5 kN, ~28 MPa on the 18 mm² annulus, under PLA compressive yield), with medium threadlock. Check that each link spins freely with no axial play after tightening. Update the README pivot-stack row and the BOM; also move ST-08 to PRINT per M-19.

defense.argument: Verified in rk3.py: Z0, PT = 20.2, 6.0 and rk.box(690,470,Z0 → 740,476,Z0+PT). The 'rib' lies entirely inside the plate. The reviewer's own check shows the plate is adequate without it (20 N at X717: σ ≈1 MPa, δ ≈0.04 mm). A foot that reaches down to the table would also have to match the table height under the rail exactly (Z0-20.2) and would rock if it is off. Deleting the rib is the correct fix.
defense.proposed_change: rk3.py: delete line 33 (the rib box) and replace the comment with '# no rib: 6 mm plate overhang 68 mm, 20 N place load → σ≈1 MPa, δ≈0.04 mm (CDR M-24)'. If RK-02 is already printed, there is no reprint because the geometry is identical. If not, export from the updated script.

defense.argument: Verified. The cavity box(69,312,162 → 105,348,206) is 36 x 36 x 43 mm ≈ 56 mL with a flat floor and a 10 mm slot, not '70 mL'. The choke from the slot end (Y348) to the screw end (Y365) is 17 mm, about one 16 mm lead, which allows flood-through when the bench is bumped. 56 mL of instant yeast (~0.65 g/mL) is ~36 g, about 5 runs at 7 g, so capacity is fine. DH-01 and DH-02 print tonight, so the geometry changes are free.
defense.proposed_change: auger_west.py: replace the flat floor with two 60°-from-horizontal walls on the ±X sides converging to a 12 mm slot (X81-93). Shorten the slot to Y312-344. aug2.py: lengthen the screw so it ends at Y368 (choke 24 mm ≥1.5 leads; the outlet Ø10 stays at Y365-375). README: replace '70 mL' with the measured live volume after the redesign (≈45-50 mL; compute from the CAD and state it) and say 'refill every 4 runs'.

defense.argument: Agreed. analysis/load_cases.py has no Kt, no impact case and no thermal row against PLA. It models the ear screws as pull-out when the load is in-plane shear and bearing, and it lacks the cases that actually govern. One adjustment to the criteria. A flat 10 MPa across-layer allowable used for every case, including two-fault accident cases (stall into a stop), would condemn parts that are fine, as shown in M-04 and M-08. Use limit/accident categories, as any structural code does.
defense.proposed_change: Rewrite analysis/load_cases.py and regenerate load_cases.md. Allowables: PLA across layers 10 MPa (scatter-adjusted), along layers 30 MPa, PLA bearing 50 MPa, TPU 95A, VHB 4950 shear 0.3 MPa sustained. Criteria: operational SF ≥2.0 against these; accident (two-fault, e.g. stall into a stop) SF ≥1.0 against these and ≥2.0 against 20/40 MPa. Apply Peterson Kt with the measured as-built root radii (fillet_report from M-08). New rows: DH-01 bridge joint (M-02); AG-01 20 N hand load, stress and rocking ±X/±Y (M-06); DH-02 auger jam at 70 % PWM (M-09); grip friction vs beaker and 1 g shake (M-11); arm place force vs cell overload (M-15); hot-wetted PLA 56/62 °C (M-16); foam volume vs containment (M-17); stop post static (Kt 1.2) and impact at 1 s/3 s with crank compliance (M-04); thread engagement for every fastener group (M-01/M-05/M-21); carousel radial constraint after the M-03 fix (friction-limited 2 N); TT-04 wall side load; ear screws in shear/bearing.

defense.argument: All verified. Line 66 says PLA while the table, schedule and filenames say PETG. The stock-jaw section (lines 480-498) contradicts the fin-ray section, as does the joints table ('−58° closes it'). RK-02 has 3 pockets at (670,414)/(717,495)/(707,587) per rk3.py and plan3.py, but the table lists 4 at Y392/456/520/584. M5x10 and M5x12 are both given for the rack. The README run step 1 has arm B carry the measuring beaker to the funnel, but plan3 and software §4 (A_DEV_TO_FLASK) use arm A. Step 3 says the auger doses 'to 7.0 g' with pulses on the scale, when the auger is over the carousel and is open-loop by revolutions (software §6).
defense.proposed_change: Do a single README consistency pass in the same commit as the BOM. Say PLA everywhere (and TPU 95A for GR-03 and ST-09). final.argument:
I concede the force and dispute the governing section. That changes what is mandatory.

(1) FORCE: conceded. The crank edge contacts the post at sqrt(30.15^2 - 19^2) = 23.4 mm along the crank, so F = 4.41/0.0234 = 188 N (146 N in X, 119 N in -Y). load_cases.py line 43 (STALL/0.030) is wrong. With the 1.2 mm ST-09 sleeve the contact offset becomes 20.2, the lever 22.4 mm and F 197 N. That is the number to design to.

(2) THE Z5 ROOT CLAIM IS WRONG. The web is not stranded behind an air gap. I re-sliced exports/prints/ST-01_stage-base_qty1.stl, a clean single-shell union. Scanning along Y at local x = -8, -2.98 and +2 for Z = 10, 20 and 34, there are exactly two boundary crossings: y = -38.8 (post outer face) and y = -10.3 (servo pocket wall). The material is continuous from the post through the 12-wide web and the 4 mm cradle front wall (y -10.3 to -14.5, which runs the full 70 mm X width) into the cradle box. The +Y post mirrors this (y 10.4 to 38.7). The reviewer's 287 mm^2 section is the post plus the stub alone, which leaves out material that is physically there. If the slices showed a 6-8 mm gap, either the wrong y-range was sliced or the even-odd fill was misread; the crossing list settles it. My measured section at Z7.3 is a lower bound, because it counts only the post, web and front-wall strip and not the side walls: A 662 mm^2, Z 4008 mm^3 for the X load and 2580 mm^3 for the Y load. Under 188 N at Z61 (lever 53.7 mm), that gives 1.96 + 2.48 = 4.4 MPa nominal at the worst corner, and 6.6 MPa with the reviewer's Kt of 1.5. The Z5 root does not govern and does not fail. Neither the R5 base fillet nor the plate extension is needed for strength.

(3) Z35.3 IS THE GOVERNING SECTION, AND ITS MARGIN IS THIN. This is where the reviewer is right in substance. The cradle wall and web both end at Z35.3: the section drops from 616 to 268 mm^2 between Z35.0 and Z35.5. The section at Z36 is A 260 mm^2, Z about 579 to 604 mm^3, with a lever of 25.5 mm. At 188 N, sigma_nom = 4.79 N*m / 577 = 8.3 MPa, matching the reviewer's 8.4. The resultant points 39 deg off X. The -Y component puts the web-side face in tension, which is the R2 fillet edge, so Kt is about 1.2 and sigma_peak is about 10.0 MPa. With the sleeve (197 N) it is about 10.4 MPa. Against the accident criterion I proposed, that is SF 0.96-1.0 against 10 MPa and 1.92-2.0 against 20 MPa. That is a pass on a knife edge, not the 3.0 claimed in print_manifest.md. A post failure lets the tray overtravel next to a flask of 12% H2O2, so I will not defend a 1.0 margin for the demo.

(4) THE PROPOSED v2 GEOMETRY. Tying each post to the cradle wall from Z5 to Z54 is the wrong description: it is already tied from Z5 to Z35.3, and the cradle wall stops at Z35.3. The fix that works is my optional v2 made mandatory for the demo. Extend the existing 12-wide web upward from Z35.3 to Z54 as a fin on the post's servo-facing side, spanning y -14.5 to -20.9 (mirrored on +Y). The servo body sits at |y| <= 10.3 with its ears along X, so the fin clears it by 4.2 mm. The crank underside at Z56 leaves 2 mm of clearance. The free lever then drops from 25.5 to 7 mm. At 197 N that is sigma = 197 x 0.007 / 577 = 2.4 MPa, or 3.1 MPa with Kt 1.3. At Z35.3 the post-plus-fin section carries 197 N x 25.7 mm on more than 330 mm^2 with no notch, because the fin runs continuously into the wall. The stop angles do not change (45.2 deg bare, 42.2 deg with the sleeve). This easily meets the reviewer's acceptance criterion of sigma_peak <= 10 MPa at every section.

(5) GATING. v1 stays safe for bench bring-up and rehearsal behind the clamp. To reach the post at all, the servo must be commanded past 40 deg (blocked by the hard pulse clamp), or the horn must slip or the calibration drift by more than 2.2 deg. Even then, the static stall stress is 10 MPa, at or under the conservative across-layer criterion, and the 3 s smoothstep plus TPU sleeve keep the impact load below static stall. So v2 should gate the live demo, not powered bring-up.
final.last_offer: 1) Fix analysis/load_cases.py line 43: F_stop = STALL / sqrt(r_c^2 - (10 + r_post + t_sleeve)^2), which gives 188 N bare and 197 N sleeved, applied at 39 deg to tangential at Z61. Check three sections: the Z7.3 composite (post + web + cradle front wall, measured A 662 mm^2, Z 4008/2580 mm^3, lever 53.7 mm, Kt 1.5), the Z35.5 post top (Z 577 mm^3, lever 25.5 mm, Kt 1.2) and, for v2, the Z54 fin top. Report v1 honestly as SF 0.96-1.0 against 10 MPa, and correct the 'SF 3.0' claim in exports/print_manifest.md line 28 and the README. 2) ST-01 v2 is MANDATORY before the live demo, not before powered bring-up. Keep the same Ø18 posts at the same positions, so the stop stays at 45.2 deg and 42.2 deg with the sleeve. Extend the existing 12-wide web from Z35.3 up to Z54 (y -14.5 to -20.9, mirrored on +Y), with an R3 fillet where the fin meets the post along its full height. Where the geometry allows, add R5 to the free sides of the Z5 post-plate root. Grow the plate outline locally on -Y/+Y so the post face sits at least 2 mm inboard of the plate edge; v1 overhangs by 0.7-0.9 mm. I accept the reviewer's 6 mm if it clears RK-02 and the saddle. Acceptance: slice the v2 STL and show sigma_peak <= 10 MPa at every Z from 5 to 66 under 197 N at Z61. Expected result: about 3 MPa at the fin top, worst case. Reprint: ST-01 only, about 4 h 18 on the H2D and 235 g PLA. Keep v1 as the spare. 3) Firmware: hard pulse clamp |alpha| <= 40 deg, derived from the no-linkage µs/deg sweep and enforced on the Mega whichever pulse table is loaded. Stage moves take at least 3 s with smoothstep. Fit 2 x ST-09 TPU 95A sleeves (ID 18.3, 1.2 mm wall, Z54-68). Sleeve wall must not exceed 1.5 mm. 4) If v2 is not fitted by Thursday, the lead signs an accepted-risk entry that names the correct section: 'stop post may fracture at the Z35.3 web top (SF approx 1.0 vs 10 MPa) under a servo stall at the stop; protection is the firmware clamp plus the TPU sleeve.' I do not accept the Z5-root wording or the 26 MPa figure, because the slice data disproves them.

findings.title: The M45CHW servo leads have no exit path from the TT-01 and ST-01 servo pockets. Both pockets are closed cups with 0.3 mm clearance.
findings.evidence: I sliced the STLs with numpy ray-parity in exports/prints. TT-01_turntable-base_qty1.stl, in local coordinates (origin at the turntable axis (175,370)): the pocket is X -30.3..+10.3, Y +/-10.3. It is closed by a floor at Z 0-1 and by a continuous 2 mm sleeve on all four faces from Z 1 to 29.3, which is the ear ledge. I mapped the walls at x=-31.3, x=+11.3 and y=+11.3 and found no opening below Z 29. West of the sleeve there is solid PLA out to x=-53.5 up to Z 28. The only opening in the outer box is a window in the west wall at local Y +13..+24, Z 15-43. It connects to the cavity north of the sleeve, not to the pocket. ST-01_stage-base_qty1.stl, in local coordinates (origin at the driven pivot (656,142)): the pocket is X -10.3..+30.3, Y +/-10.3, Z 5-35.3, walled by solid PLA of 14.7 mm at -X, 14.7 mm at +X and about 3.5 mm at +/-Y over its full height. Pocket size is 40.6 x 20.6 mm against a 40 x 20 case (39.9 x 20.1 per servodatabase), which leaves 0.3 mm per side. A standard-size servo brings its lead out through a grommet in the lower case below the mounting ears. The CAD servo model, hw_funcs.py servo() lines 106-125, models no lead or grommet at all, so the interference check in README 'Verification' could not catch this. Both parts were on Tuesday's plates and are already printed. As built, either the lead is crushed between case and wall (8.4 V, up to 6.8 A conductors) or the servo cannot be seated.
findings.required_change: Before assembly on Friday, fit each servo dry and mark the grommet position. TT-01: cut a 7 mm wide notch through the sleeve's +Y wall (local Y +10.3..+12.3) at the lead end, running from the ledge (Z 29.3) down to 2 mm below the grommet. Route the lead through the cavity and out of the existing west window (local Y 13-24, world X 120, Y 383-394). ST-01: cut a 7 W x 12 H mm notch through the 3.5 mm side wall that faces away from the tray sweep (+X / rail side), from the ledge (Z 35.3) down past the grommet. Deburr both notches and line them with 1 layer of electrical tape. Add the lead and grommet to servo() in hw_funcs.py and the slot to the TT-01/ST-01 generators so any reprint is correct. Add a zip-tie anchor (a 4 x 2 mm slot) 15 mm outside each exit for strain relief. Add 'cut lead notch' as step 0 of the servo install in README 'Assembly and every fastener'.

findings.title: Opening the serial port, a reset, a firmware upload or plugging in the LiPo snaps the carousel and stage to 1500 us at full servo speed, with peroxide on board.
findings.evidence: docs/software_architecture.md section 1 and README line 215: the Mega Pro is on USB serial (a CH340-class bridge with DTR auto-reset), and the laptop's Python process opens the port. Every open, which includes each restart of a crashed script, toggles DTR and resets the AVR. The AVR Servo constructor sets ticks to DEFAULT_PULSE_WIDTH (1500 us), and attach(pin,500,2500) starts emitting that pulse immediately. The firmware has no idea where the servos are (there is no feedback), so the ramp in README line 426 and the S-curve in section 7 cannot apply to the first command. Stage: from WORK (alpha +36.87 deg) to alpha 0 is a 90 mm tray jump. Torque-limited, that is 4.4 N*m / 0.150 m = 29 N on a 0.69 kg payload (load_cases.py m_payload), about 40 m/s^2 = 4 g. That is 27x the 0.15 g flask slosh limit in analysis/load_cases.md, with 50-75 mL of 12 % H2O2 in an open flask carrying a loose funnel. Carousel: station 3 (22.5 deg) to home (90 deg) is 67.5 deg in about 0.12 s (0.11 s/60 deg at 8.4 V). That gives alpha = 4*1.178/0.12^2 = 327 rad/s^2 and 2.9 g at r = 88 mm, which is 12x the 0.25 g beaker limit. The same snap happens whenever the LiPo is plugged in after the Mega is running and someone has moved a servo by hand. The section 7 watchdog cannot help, because a reset happens before the firmware runs.
findings.required_change: (1) Gate servo power: put a 10 A relay module (e.g. SRD-05VDC-SL-C) or a logic-driven high-side P-FET (Vds >= 20 V, Rds(on) < 20 mOhm) between the fuse/e-stop and the servo bus. Drive it from D25. It must be OFF when the pin is high-Z (at reset, during the bootloader, when USB is disconnected). (2) Firmware: do not attach() in setup(). Wait for host 'INIT <tt_us> <st_us>' carrying the last commanded pulses (the host persists them to disk after every move; the Mega mirrors them to EEPROM). Call writeMicroseconds() before attach(), then close the relay, then accept moves. (3) After flashing, fit 10 uF from RESET to GND (remove it to re-flash), and in pyserial set dtr=False and rts=False before open(). (4) Bring-up rule in the README: the flask stays empty until the INIT handshake is proven. (5) Enable the AVR WDT (250 ms) only after confirming the Mega Pro bootloader survives a WDT reset; a WDT reset must leave the relay open.

findings.title: The 10 A fuse cannot protect the M45CHWs from a stall. A one-spline horn error drives the stage into its +/-45 deg stop and holds it there.
findings.evidence: servodatabase M45CHW: stall 4.5-6.8 A, 'running' 7.0 A at 8.4 V, idle 0.6 A. README line 216 uses 9-14 A for two stalled servos, but those are 6 V figures; at 8.4 V one stall is 6.8 A, and 9.5 A if the 6.8 A figure is a 6 V value scaled by 8.4/6. ATO/ATC fuse curve (SAE J1284): 135 % opens in 0.75-600 s, 200 % in 0.15-5 s. One stall at 68-95 % of 10 A never opens the 10 A fuse, so the motor dissipates 8.4 V x 6.8 A = 57 W until it burns, and there is no spare servo in the BOM. Two stalls (13.6-19 A) open the fuse in about 0.2-600 s and kill the whole bench. Realistic stall: the horn goes on in 14.4 deg steps (README line 465). One spline of trim error puts the ERUPT command (-36.87 deg) at -51.3 deg, past the -45 deg stop posts, so the servo stalls continuously. The '+/-40 deg soft limit' (README item 9) is on the commanded angle and gives no protection against a mis-trimmed horn. The Mega has no current sense.
findings.required_change: Keep the 10 A main fuse for the wiring. Add a 3 A ATO fuse per servo branch: at 6.8 A (227 %) it opens in 0.15-5 s, while the computed demand (carousel 0.06 N*m and stage 0.33 N*m out of 3.4-4.4 N*m, i.e. <10 % of stall, about 1 A) never reaches it. Add bus current sensing: an INA226 with a 10 mOhm shunt, or INA219 breakouts per branch, on I2C (D20/D21). Firmware opens the servo relay (E-02) if a branch draws > 3 A for 300 ms, and reports 'F STALL'. Commissioning: before the crank is fitted, jog the stage servo to +/-36.87 deg and check the crank clears the stops by >= 8 deg with a printed angle gauge. Buy 1 spare M45CHW.

findings.title: HX711 reads disable interrupts and jitter the Servo-library pulses by up to 300 us. The timers themselves do not conflict on the Mega.
findings.evidence: Pins: README line 425 and software section 1 assign carousel D9, stage D10, PWMA D11, HX711 D3/D4. ATmega2560 ServoTimers.h uses Timer5 first for up to 12 servos, so only analogWrite on D44/45/46 is lost. D9/D10 (Timer2) and D11 (OC1A, Timer1, 490 Hz) are unaffected, and the D9/D10/D11 conflict exists only on an Uno or Nano. The real conflict is timing. The bogde HX711 library wraps each 25-27-clock shiftIn in noInterrupts(); with digitalWrite/digitalRead on AVR that is about 11 us per bit, roughly 300 us blocked per read.
