At 80 reads/s that is 24 ms/s, or 2.4 % of the time. There are 100 servo pulse-end ISR events per second (2 servos x 50 Hz), so about 2.4 pulses/s get stretched by up to 300 us. At 7.4 us/deg (270 deg unit, README line 220) that is a command spike of up to 40 deg. The servos twitch visibly with beakers and the peroxide flask on board, and the pulse table accuracy in README lines 456-476 becomes meaningless.
findings.required_change: Drop the Servo library. Generate both servo pulses in hardware on Timer4: mode 14 Fast PWM, prescaler 8, ICR4 = 39999 (50 Hz, 0.5 us resolution). Carousel on D6 (OC4A), stage on D7 (OC4B), and the firmware S-curve writes OCR4A/OCR4B. Leave PWMA on D11 (OC1A) and move Timer1 to 20 kHz (mode 14, ICR1 = 799, prescaler 1) so the N20 is silent and above the TB6612's 100 kHz limit with margin. Alternatively, keep the Servo library and replace the HX711 read with a direct-port bit-bang (PORTG/PINE, about 1 us/bit, < 35 us with interrupts off). Update the pin table in README and in software section 1.

findings.title: The pour controller assumes an 80 Hz HX711 the module does not provide, and the HX711 and load-cell wiring have no mount, routing or spill protection.
findings.evidence: Software section 5.1 and section 7 assume 'HX711 runs at 80 Hz' and stream W at 80 Hz. The ShangHJ green HX711 module (B09K7G51KJ) ties RATE (pin 15) to GND, which gives 10 SPS. At 10 SPS the 4-sample median spans 0.4 s, so effective lag is about 0.2 s + tau 0.1 s = 0.3 s instead of about 0.14 s. At the planned peak flow q = 8 g/s the cut-off predictor in section 5.4, which budgets only q*(T_air + 0.1 s), under-predicts by about 8 x 0.2 = 1.6 g. That exceeds every tolerance in section 5.6 (water +/-0.5 g, developer +/-1.0 g). Noise at 80 SPS is about 90 nV rms against 4.3 uV/g (1 mV/V x 4.3 V AVDD over 1 kg), about 0.02 g. That is fine, so 80 Hz is worth getting. There is no HX711 mount on WS-01 (no part in review/design_data.json other than the load cell, item 138, at X 403.5-478.5, Y 468.6-481.3, Z 45-57.7). The scale sits directly under every pour (WS-02 at (468,475)), so drips of 12 % H2O2 and soap land on the load cell lead exit and on any HX711 left nearby.
findings.required_change: Convert the module to 80 SPS: lift HX711 pin 15 (RATE) from the GND trace and tie it to DVDD. Verify the rate by timing DOUT falling edges, which should be 12.5 ms apart. If that fails, re-tune the software for 10 SPS: median-3, tau 0.05 s, cut-off lead q*(T_air + 0.35 s), q* capped at 3 g/s. Mount the HX711 on WS-01, on the -Y face away from the pour, within the 200 mm load-cell lead, with 2 x M2 into 1.8 mm pilots, or 3M VHB plus a printed cover. Run the 4 load-cell wires as a twisted bundle and keep DT/SCK/VCC/GND to the Mega at least 50 mm from the servo and N20 leads, crossing them at 90 deg. Add a drip skirt to WS-02: a 2 mm overhang beyond the load cell, 5 mm down. Give the load-cell lead exit a dab of silicone or Kapton.

findings.title: There is no hardware emergency stop. The only stop is a laptop spacebar, which depends on the Python loop being alive.
findings.evidence: Software section 8: 'E-stop: spacebar ... A hardware e-stop isn't feasible on borrowed arms; operator can pull the arm barrel jacks'. The spacebar path needs the asyncio loop, the USB link and the Mega firmware all to be healthy. The barrel-jack pull is a hidden, two-handed action at the back of the frame (the Waveshare plates sit at world Y 587-595 behind each base), done while the arm may be holding 12 % peroxide over the funnel at Z about 260. The M45CHW bus (up to 2 x 7 A) and the N20 have no way to be cut by hand except unplugging the XT60.
findings.required_change: Fit a red latching mushroom e-stop (2 NC poles, >= 10 A at 12 VDC, e.g. 22 mm panel type in a yellow box) at the front edge of the table within the operator's reach. Pole 1 sits in series in LiPo+ after the 10 A fuse and before the servo relay (E-02), which cuts carousel, stage and auger (stop category 0). Pole 2 feeds D2 (INT4) with INPUT_PULLUP, so firmware latches 'F ESTOP' and refuses to re-arm until the host sends 'RESET' after the button is released. For the arms, put both arm adapters on a switched power strip labelled 'ARMS OFF'. Document that the arms go limp and drop what they hold, and that the spacebar (torque-hold) is the first action, with the strip only for a pinch or collision. Update software section 8 and the README accordingly.

findings.title: The pour interlock and the low-battery stop rely on signals that do not exist: stage position is inferred from the command, and the LiPo monitor is not wired.
findings.evidence: Software section 8: 'pour states refuse to start unless ... the flask collar is detected (stage servo at its WORK angle)'. That is the commanded angle, not a sensor. If the servo relay is open, the fuse has blown, the LiPo is flat or the horn has slipped, the stage can sit at ERUPT (flask at (450,102)) while arm B pours 40 g of 12 % developer at the fixed funnel position (flask at (450,282)), onto the table. Same section: 'Battery: A0 divider (OPEN: not yet wired — add 10 k / 4.7 k)'. With 10k/4.7k, 8.4 V gives 2.686 V. That exceeds the 2.56 V internal reference, so it must use AVcc, which is laptop VBUS at 4.75-5.25 V, a +/-5 % error. At the 7.0 V cutoff the reading spans 6.65-7.35 V. A dead or unplugged LiPo is also invisible: the servos go limp silently and the host keeps commanding carousel stations.
findings.required_change: Add 2 lever microswitches (Omron D2F-L class) on ST-01, actuated by the crank at WORK (+36.87 deg) and ERUPT (-36.87 deg), wired to D26/D27 with INPUT_PULLUP. Pours and auger runs require WORK closed. Add a deck-home Hall sensor (A3144 plus a 6 x 2 mm magnet in TT-02) on D28 for carousel indexing confirmation. Battery: use a 33k/10k divider (8.4 V gives 1.953 V) with 100 nF at A0 and INTERNAL2V56, calibrated once against a multimeter (resolution 10.7 mV). Measure the servo bus downstream of the relay as well (second divider on A1), so 'relay closed but bus < 6.0 V' raises 'F SERVO_PWR'. Thresholds: warn at 7.2 V, refuse moves below 7.0 V under no load. Remove the 'OPEN' from software section 8.

findings.title: Ground topology, wire gauge, connector ratings and servo extension drops are unspecified. 'All grounds common' invites returning motor current through the Mega and its USB link.
findings.evidence: README line 215: 'Tie Mega GND to the LiPo −'. README line 429: 'All grounds are common'. No topology, gauges or connector types are given anywhere. The TB6612 breakout shares one GND for VM and logic, so if it is wired to the Mega header, N20 current (about 1.1 A stall at 8.4 V) returns through Dupont jumpers (28 AWG, about 0.2 Ohm per 1 m loop) and the Mega ground plane. That shifts the HX711 ground and pushes noise into the CH340/USB ground, a classic cause of mid-demo USB disconnects. Laptop USB ground is also common to both arm bus boards (Waveshare) and their adapters, so a grounded (3-prong) arm adapter plus a grounded laptop charger forms a mains-earth loop. Extension drop: with electronics at the rear-left (E-09), the stage servo (ST-01, about (666,142)) needs a lead routed about 1.07 m along the X-back and Y-right rails, i.e. a 300 mm stock lead plus 0.8-1.0 m extension. A 26 AWG extension (133.9 mOhm/m) plus a 22 AWG stock lead gives a loop of 2 x (1.0 x 0.134 + 0.3 x 0.053) = 0.30 Ohm, a 2.0 V drop at a 6.8 A stall and 0.36 V at 1.2 A idle. At a 7.0 V pack that leaves 5.0 V at the servo, below its 6.0 V minimum, so it browns out and resets. JR servo crimp contacts are rated about 3 A against 7 A running and 6.8 A stall peaks.
findings.required_change: Draw and follow a star ground. One star point is a Wago 221-415 or brass terminal block at the bulk capacitor, where these all land: LiPo−, both servo grounds, TB6612 GND (its own 22 AWG wire) and ONE 22 AWG wire to Mega GND. The HX711 GND goes only to the Mega GND. Wire gauges: XT60 to fuse to e-stop to relay to bus in 16 AWG silicone. Servo branches use 20 AWG (stage extension 1.0 m, carousel 0.3 m) with a 2-pin power connector (XT30) for + and −; the JR plug carries signal only, or use 20 AWG 'HD' extensions. Target < 0.7 V drop at 6.8 A, which 20 AWG gives: 2 x (1.0 x 0.0333 + 0.3 x 0.053) = 0.098 Ohm. Twist each signal with its ground. TB6612 VM uses 22 AWG. Use 2-prong (Class II) arm adapters, or confirm the laptop charger is ungrounded. Add the drawing to README (see E-12).

findings.title: There is no defined location, enclosure or spill protection for the Mega, LiPo, TB6612, fuse and relay. The old EL-01 envelope sits under the arms' swept volume.
findings.evidence: review/design_data.json item 96 'EL-01' is hidden, with bbox 184 x 84 x 58 at world (18..202, 506..590, 0..58). No other electrical part is modelled. Using the planner sweep (C:/Users/User/fusion_bridge/sweep.npy, 2.5 mm voxels, LO (-10,40,-20)), 11 % of the EL-01 footprint is overflown by arms or beakers at Z 77-262. The zone behind the arms (X 265-665, Y 600-700) is 31 % overflown. Zones with 0 % overflight: X 0-240, Y 600-700 (left rear) and X 700-900, Y 40-300. Pours of 12 % H2O2 happen over the scale at (468,475) and the funnel at (450,282). The LiPo is a fire risk next to an oxidiser.
findings.required_change: Put a printed or bought electronics box with a lid in the left-rear 0 % zone, X 20-235, Y 600-695, about 2-30 mm in from the table's back edge (Y 702). It holds the Mega Pro on M3 standoffs, the TB6612, the relay, the fuse holder and the star terminal block. The LiPo goes in a LiPo-safe bag, strapped with Velcro, on the floor of the box or beside it, at least 600 mm from the eruption point (450,102); (130,650) is 630 mm away. Mount the e-stop separately at the front edge. Re-run plan3.py with the box as a scene obstacle to confirm zero hits. Cable exits face +Y or −X, away from the arms. Add the box to the CAD as EL-02 (visible) and to the print plan or BOM.

findings.title: The auger drive is under-specified and contradictory: 70 % vs 100 % PWM, speed that varies with battery voltage, no stall detection, an unfused TB6612 branch and no dead time on reversal.
findings.evidence: README line 429: 'PWM limited to about 70 % so the 6 V motor sees about 6 V'. Software section 6: 'TB6612, 100 % PWM forward', which is 8.4 V (140 %) on a 6 V N20. With a fixed 70 % duty the motor sees 5.9 V at 8.4 V and 4.9 V at 7.0 V, a 17 % rpm swing. Revolutions are counted as time x calibrated rpm (section 6), so the dose shifts about 17 % over one pack (7 g gives 5.8-7 g). README step 3 'reversing 0.3 s if it stalls' has no stall sensor: no encoder and no current sense. A yeast jam at 100 % PWM holds the N20 in stall (about 1.1 A at 8.4 V, near the TB6612's 1.2 A continuous rating) while time-based counting reports success. Instant reversal from full forward to reverse roughly doubles the current transient. The TB6612 VM lead is protected only by the 10 A main fuse. I checked the DH-01 STL: the region behind the motor face (local X 30-67, Y 0-48, Z 12-28) is empty. The motor is cantilevered from the face at local Y 49.5, so an encoder N20 (about +8 mm at the back) fits with no change to DH-01, which prints tonight.
findings.required_change: Buy the encoder N20 (6 V, 60 rpm, magnetic 7 PPR, same 12 x 10 gearbox) and wire encoder A/B to D18/D19 (INT3/INT2), VCC 5 V. Count real revolutions and flag a stall when there are 0 edges in 150 ms at duty > 30 %. Duty = min(1, 6.0 V / V_bus) using the A0 reading from E-07, so the motor always sees 6.0 V. Reverse sequence: coast 30 ms, brake 20 ms, then reverse. Fuse the TB6612 VM branch with 1 A (polyfuse or ATO). Solder 100 nF ceramic across the N20 tabs, plus 2 x 47 nF tab to can. Resolve the README and software contradiction in favour of voltage-compensated 6.0 V.

findings.title: The arm supply sizing has zero margin, and identical 5.5 x 2.1 barrels on 5 V, 6 V and 12 V supplies invite a motor-killing mis-plug.
findings.evidence: README lines 186-191: the 7.4 V variant uses '5 V, >=4 A' while expected draw is '4–5 A peaks', so peaks reach 100-125 % of the adapter rating. The 12 V variant uses 12 V 5 A for 4-5 A peaks, 0 % margin. The README itself says supply sag causes 'servo resets and bus errors' (line 192). An STS3215 reset mid-pour drops a beaker of 12 % developer. Every candidate supply on the bench uses the same 5.5/2.1 barrel: Facmogu 12 V 5 A (B0711Q5B49), Facmogu 5 V 4 A (B087LY41PV), inShareplus 6 V 10 A (B01GHN2S7Q) and the 2 A bench supply. README line 184 warns that 'the wrong one can burn the motors out'.
findings.required_change: Size each arm supply at >= 1.3 x the 5 A peak, i.e. >= 6.5 A: 5 V 8 A for C001/C044/C046 arms, 12 V 8 A for C018/C047 arms. If the lender's adapters are smaller, buy these. Label each adapter and each arm's jack with its voltage and variant using coloured heat-shrink (red for 12 V, blue for 5 V). Bring only one voltage family to the venue. Before the first power-on, check with a multimeter at the barrel that the voltage matches the sticker. Add these to README 'SO-101 arms' and the BOM.

findings.title: The README contradicts itself on power and control (legacy PCA9685 / 6 V text) and has no wiring diagram, pin table or harness list.
findings.evidence: README lines 223-234, 'M45CHW servos (turntable + stage)', still say 'Power: 6 V 10 A supply wired straight to the servos', 'Signal: PCA9685 channels, or Arduino ... or ESP32', 'Tie all grounds together (supply, controller, PCA9685)' and 'A wall supply is simpler'. Lines 208-216 say the LiPo and Mega 'replace the 6 V 10 A wall supply and the PCA9685 below'. Line 224 quotes 6 V currents while the pack is 8.4 V. Line 216 says '9–14 A' for two stalled servos; at 8.4 V running is 7 A each. Lines 214 and 428/443 give the capacitor as '1000–2200 µF' and '2200 µF'. Line 429 says 70 % PWM where software section 6 says 100 %. README line 215 and software section 1 say 'USB-C' for a Mega 2560 Pro, which is usually micro-USB with CH340G. Software section 5 assumes 80 Hz HX711 (see E-05). The repository layout (lines 663-676) omits docs/. The only wiring description is one prose paragraph (lines 425-430): no schematic, no connector list, no wire gauges or lengths, no fuse ratings per branch. Teammates assemble on Friday with the author unavailable.
findings.required_change: Delete lines 223-234 and replace them with one 'Electrical' section containing: (a) a block schematic (SVG or PNG in docs/) of LiPo -> XT60 -> 10 A fuse -> e-stop -> relay -> 2200 uF + star terminal -> 3 A per-servo fuses -> M45CHWs, plus the 1 A TB6612 branch, the dividers and the Mega/USB. (b) A pin table: D2 e-stop sense, D3/D4 HX711, D6/D7 servos (Timer4), D11 PWMA (Timer1 20 kHz), D18/D19 encoder, D20/D21 INA226, D22/D23/D24 AIN1/AIN2/STBY, D25 relay, D26/D27 stage limit switches, D28 deck Hall, A0/A1 dividers. (c) A harness table: from/to, gauge, length, connector. (d) Current figures at 8.4 V. Make the software doc reference the same table. Correct the USB connector type after inspecting the board.

findings.title: The electrical BOM is missing parts needed to build and run the bench, including a USB hub for 3 serial devices.
findings.evidence: README 'What you buy' (lines 140-166, 434-443) lists only the XT60 fuse lead, the 2200 uF capacitor, HX711 x2, TB6612 x3 and N20 x3. Mentioned or needed but not listed: the 2S LiPo itself (capacity, C rating and connector unstated; line 233 only mentions 5000 mAh as an option), the LiPo charger, LiPo bag and voltage alarm (all required by README item 10 and line 214), a USB hub (arm A, arm B and Mega are 3 serial ports, and most current laptops have 2 USB-C), USB cables for the Mega, servo extensions, hookup wire, a terminal or star block, per-branch fuses, the e-stop, the servo relay, divider resistors (software section 8 'OPEN'), a perfboard or screw-terminal shield for the Mega Pro, heat-shrink, zip ties and adhesive tie mounts, solder, a multimeter, a power strip (2 arm adapters + laptop + charger), and a spare M45CHW (single point of failure, $44.99). Runtime: at the listed 0.6 A idle per servo (servodatabase), the bus idles at 1.2 A. A 2200 mAh pack gives about 1.5 h at 80 % usable and a 5000 mAh pack about 3.3 h. The pack capacity matters for a full expo session.
findings.required_change: Add these lines to the README BOM: 2S 5000 mAh 30C LiPo with XT60, 37 Wh (or confirm the owned pack is >= 4000 mAh); a 2S balance charger with its own supply; a LiPo-safe bag; a 1-8S cell checker/alarm set to 3.5 V/cell; a powered 4-port USB 3 hub; a micro-USB (or USB-C) data cable, 1 m; 2 x 20 AWG servo extensions, 1.0 m and 0.3 m; 16/20/22 AWG silicone wire, 2 m each; 2 x XT30 pairs; a Wago 221-415 pack; ATO fuse holders x3 with 3 A x4 and 1 A x2 fuses plus spare 10 A x2; a 22 mm latching NC e-stop with box; a 5 V 10 A relay module; resistors 33k/10k x2 and 100 nF x4; an INA226 breakout; 2 x D2F-L microswitches; an A3144 Hall sensor and a 6 x 2 mm magnet; an encoder N20; a screw-terminal shield or perfboard for the Mega Pro; heat-shrink, zip ties and 3M tie mounts; a 4-outlet switched power strip; 1 spare M45CHW.

findings.title: A full 2S charge sits at or above the M45CHW's 8.4 V maximum. The XT60 sparks into 2200 uF, and the single bulk capacitor is far from both servos.
findings.evidence: M45CHW rating is 6.0-8.4 V (servodatabase). Charger tolerance is 4.20 +/- 0.05 V/cell, so a pack can reach 8.5 V, above the maximum before any regenerative bump. Plugging 8.4 V into 2200 uF through about 30 mOhm gives a peak of roughly 280 A and arcs on every connect. One capacitor at the battery is 0.3-1.3 m of lead away from the servos (E-08), so local transients are not decoupled.
findings.required_change: Charge to 4.15 V/cell (8.30 V), or discharge for 1 min before running. Keep the 2200 uF upstream of the relay, which also stops relay-contact inrush, and add 470 uF 16 V low-ESR at each servo's power connector. Use an XT60 anti-spark lead or a 10 Ohm pre-charge resistor for the first 1 s, or connect the LiPo with the relay open (E-02) so the arc happens only at the battery-side capacitor.

findings.title: Cable routing and strain relief: the N20 leads hang near the deck rim, there is no tie point on DH-01/AG-01, and the arm cables and load-cell lead are unmanaged.
findings.evidence: The N20 sits at world X 81-93, Y 271.5-299, Z 149-161 (design_data item 142), cantilevered from 2 x M1.6. Its tabs are fragile. Its horizontal distance from the turntable axis (175,370) is 122-132 mm against the deck radius of 118 mm, so a drooping lead brushes the rotating deck and TT-04 rim. Neither DH-01 nor AG-01 has a cable-tie feature. The carousel and stage servos are stationary, so no slip ring is needed, which is good. The Waveshare boards (Y 587-595, Z 62-104) exit their USB and barrel cables into the zone behind the arms, which the sweep shows is 31 % overflown at Z 27-267 (E-09). The load-cell lead (about 200 mm) runs from the fixed end on WS-01 under the scale, inside the scale-placement path.
findings.required_change: Pot the N20 tabs with hot glue after soldering 22 AWG leads. Zip-tie the leads to the AG-01 post (X 40-70) at Z 140 and Z 20, and run them along the AG-01 bar and the Y-left rail slot under a 2020 slot cover strip to the box (about 600 mm). Run every bench cable in rail slots: the stage lead along the Y-right and X-back rails, the HX711 bundle along the X-front then X-back rails. Clip the arm USB and barrel cables flat in the X-back rail slot and route them straight back (+Y) to the table edge. Keep a 100 mm service loop at each arm base so pan rotation never tensions the cable. Dress the load-cell lead along the WS-01 underside with 2 adhesive tie mounts.

findings.title: Servo idle current and heat inside the closed PLA pockets have not been measured, and USB host robustness items are not covered.
findings.evidence: servodatabase lists 0.6 A idle at 6-8.4 V, i.e. up to 5 W per servo held continuously inside a fully enclosed PLA cup (E-01). That is close to PLA's 55-60 deg C softening point around the self-tapping ear pilots (load_cases.md assumes about 300 N pull-out). Windows USB selective suspend and laptop sleep drop CH340 and Waveshare ports. Three USB-serial devices enumerate in an unpredictable order (software section 2 config.yaml 'ports').
findings.required_change: Friday bring-up: measure idle current per servo with the 2 A bench supply at 8.4 V. Run 30 min holding, then check the case and pocket are below 45 deg C with the kitchen thermometer. If the idle current is above 0.3 A, open the relay (E-02) between runs. In software, select ports by USB serial number or VID:PID, not COM index. Disable USB selective suspend and sleep on the demo laptop, and install the CH340 driver before Thursday.

defense.argument: I checked this and the reviewer is right. It is a real BLOCKER. I sliced exports/prints/TT-01_turntable-base_qty1.stl with ray parity. The pocket is local X -30.3..+10.3, Y +/-10.3 inside a 2 mm sleeve (x -32.3/+12.3, y +/-12.3) from Z 1 up to the ear ledge at Z 29.3. West of it the block is solid PLA from x -32 to -54 at Z < 28. The only opening is the cavity north of y = +12.3, which is open down to Z ~1 between x -52 and +20, and it leads to the west-wall window. ST-01_stage-base_qty1.stl: the pocket is X -10.3..+30.3, Y +/-10.3. It is walled by 14.7 mm of solid at -X (x -25..-10.3) and +X (30.3..45), and about 4 mm at +/-Y (y 10.3..14.5), up to the ledge at Z 35.3. hw_funcs.py servo() lines 106-125 model only a 40 x 20 x 40.5 box, ears and spline, with no lead. The reference Sandard-Servo.stl in the repo root has no lead either: all its geometry sits inside X +/-10, Z +/-20, except the ears. So the interference check could never have caught this. design_data puts the seated servo bottom at world Z 2.0, so a lead grommet sitting 5-8 mm above the case bottom lands at pocket Z ~7-10, deep inside the closed sleeve. One amendment to the cut. On 40 x 20 metal-gear servos of this family, the grommet usually leaves the END face opposite the spline and stands 2-3 mm proud. With 0.3 mm clearance, a notch only in the +/-Y side wall (the reviewer's ST-01 cut) still leaves the grommet hitting the end wall, so the servo will not seat. The lead also cannot climb the end face, because the ear (it extends to x -37.5, Y +/-9.35) sits over it. The relief therefore has to be L-shaped: end-wall relief plus a side break-out below the ear.
defense.proposed_change: Friday, step 0 of the servo install (add to README 'Assembly and every fastener'): dry-fit each M45CHW and mark the grommet centre (face, Y and height from the case bottom). TT-01 (lead end = local -X): (a) end-wall relief at local X -34.3..-30.3, Y from (grommet Y - 5) to +12.3, Z from (grommet bottom - 2, expected about Z 4) to 29.3; (b) break through the +Y sleeve wall at X -32.3..-24, Y +10.3..+12.3, over the same Z. The lead then lies in the north cavity and leaves through the existing west window (local Y 13..24, Z 15..43; world X ~121, Y 383..394). ST-01 (lead end = local +X): an 8 mm wide slot centred on the grommet Y, straight through the 14.7 mm +X wall (x 30.3 to 45, exiting at world X 701, away from the crank, which swings on the -X side), from Z 35.3 down to 2 mm below the grommet. Cut both with a hacksaw (two kerfs) plus flush cutters or a knife-tip soldering iron. Deburr and line with one wrap of Kapton or electrical tape. Strain relief: a 3M adhesive tie mount (in the BOM, E-13) 15 mm outside each exit, used instead of printed slots, since both parts are already printed. CAD: add to servo() a lead grommet of 8 (Y) x 3 (protrusion) x 6 (Z) mm on the far end face, at the measured height, plus a 3 x 1.2 mm lead. Add the L-relief to the TT-01 generator and the +X slot to the ST-01 generator, so a reprint is correct, then re-run the interference check.

defense.argument: I accept the hazard and the numbers. The AVR Servo constructor loads 1500 us and attach() starts emitting it. The Mega 2560 Pro's CH340G resets on DTR, and nothing knows the servo position at boot. Stage: WORK to alpha 0 moves the tray 150*sin(36.87 deg) = 90 mm. Torque-limited, F = 4.41/0.150 = 29 N on m_payload = 0.686 kg (load_cases.py line 33), about 42 m/s^2 = 4.3 g, against the 0.15 g limit. Speed-limited would be worse: 90 mm in 0.068 s needs 78 m/s^2, so torque governs. Carousel: 67.5 deg in about 0.12 s gives 327 rad/s^2 and 2.9 g at r = 88 mm. Both are confirmed. I accept (1), (2) and (4), with corrections. (1) An SRD relay module is fine (10 A/28 VDC contacts, about 75 mA coil from USB 5 V), but many modules are active-LOW or have an H/L jumper, and a high-level-trigger input left floating is not guaranteed OFF. I specify the H jumper plus a 10 k pull-down. (2) The sequence is wrong in one respect. 'writeMicroseconds, attach, then close relay' drives 5 V pulses into an unpowered servo and back-powers its MCU through the signal pin's input clamp. The correct order is: relay closed with the signal held LOW, a 200 ms wait (digital servos stay limp with no pulse), then enable the PWM output at the stored pulse. Also, a stored pulse is wrong if the reset happened mid-move. So the Mega also stores a MOVING flag and refuses auto-arm if it is set. (3) I reject the 10 uF RESET capacitor. Once (1) and (2) are in place, a reset only drops servo power: the stage is limp on PTFE glides with no horizontal load, and the carousel coasts on the lazy Susan. So a reset is no longer a hazard. A cap that must be removed to re-flash is a trap for teammates working on Friday without the author. Keep dtr=False/rts=False in pyserial. (5) I accept a conditional WDT.
defense.proposed_change: Hardware: a 5 V 1-channel SRD-05VDC-SL-C relay module with the trigger jumper set to H, IN wired to D25 with a 10 kOhm resistor D25 to GND at the module. COM goes from the e-stop output and NO goes to the servo + bus. Relay is OFF at reset, in the bootloader and with USB unplugged (coil powered from USB 5 V). Firmware (no Servo library, see E-04): at boot, D6/D7 are driven LOW with Timer4 COM bits off and the relay is off. On host 'INIT <tt_us> <st_us>', compare with the EEPROM copy (EEPROM written at the end of every move with MOVING=0, and MOVING=1 written at move start). If MOVING=1 or the two disagree by more than 20 us, answer 'ERR POS_UNKNOWN', and the operator must jog the servos at low speed with the flask empty. Otherwise: close the relay, wait 200 ms, load OCR4A/OCR4B, enable COM4A1/COM4B1, then accept moves. Shutdown is the reverse order (PWM off, then relay open). If A1 reads > 2 V while the relay is commanded off, report 'F RELAY_WELD' and refuse to arm. Host: create serial.Serial() without a port, set dtr=False and rts=False, then set the port and open(). Persist the last pulses to JSON after every OK. README bring-up rule: the flask stays empty and the tray carries no payload until INIT and re-arm after a forced reset are demonstrated twice. WDT 250 ms only after a test 'WDT reset -> bootloader exits -> sketch runs' passes on this board (some clone stk500v2 bootloaders hang). The WDT ISR or boot path leaves the relay open. No RESET capacitor.

defense.argument: I accept the core point. 6.8 A on a 10 A ATO is 68 % of rating and never opens, so a single stall dissipates about 57 W indefinitely. One spline of horn error takes ERUPT to -36.87 - 14.4 = -51.3 deg, past the -45 deg stop, and the +/-40 deg soft limit on the command cannot see that. The 3 A per-branch ATO is right. At 227 % it opens in 0.15-5 s per SAE J1284. Normal demand is far below it: stage 0.33 N*m and carousel 0.06 N*m out of 4.4 N*m stall (analysis/load_cases.md rows 3 and 7), so about 0.6 A idle plus about 0.5 A. A 5 A fuse would sit at 136 % and could take 600 s, so 3 A is the correct value. I modify the sensing. Per-branch INA219s are unnecessary, because the bus sum identifies a stall. Two legitimate concurrent moves stay under about 2.2 A, and one stall alone pushes the sum above 7 A. One INA226 upstream of the relay also gives the pack voltage, which replaces the A0 divider in E-07. Watch the shunt on the common CJMCU-226 module: it is R100 = 0.1 Ohm, and with the 81.92 mV shunt range it saturates at 0.82 A, i.e. on every servo move. It must be changed to 10 mOhm. Commissioning tolerance: the design clearance at the stops is exactly 45 - 36.87 = 8.13 deg. Requiring 'clears by >= 8 deg' would fail any real assembly, so the check is +/-2 deg on the WORK/ERUPT angles, i.e. >= 6 deg clear.
defense.proposed_change: Keep the 10 A main fuse (16 AWG). Add inline ATO holders with 3 A fuses on the carousel and stage + branches, downstream of the relay. Add one INA226 breakout with its R100 shunt replaced by a 10 mOhm 2512 2 W resistor (full scale 8.19 A, LSB 0.25 mA), placed in LiPo+ between the 10 A fuse and the e-stop. Address 0x40 on D20/D21. Firmware polls it at 50 Hz. If the sum is > 2.5 A for 300 ms, it disables PWM, opens the relay and reports 'F STALL <A>'. Any reading over 8 A (saturated) trips immediately. Commissioning, before the crank is bolted on: put the horn on at the spline nearest alpha 0, jog to the +/-36.87 deg pulses and check with a printed 36.87 / 45 deg angle gauge that the crank is within +/-2 deg of +/-36.87 deg, i.e. >= 6 deg from each stop post. Record the trim in config.yaml. Buy 1 spare M45CHW (B09VBFZ9KW, $44.99).

defense.argument: I verified this. ServoTimers.h for the ATmega2560 allocates _timer5 first, so D9/D10 (Timer2) and D11 (OC1A) do not conflict, as the reviewer says. bogde HX711::read() wraps the shiftIn calls in ATOMIC_BLOCK on AVR. Arduino shiftIn on a Mega costs 2 x digitalWrite + 1 x digitalRead, about 10-11 us per bit, so 25-27 clocks block for about 270-300 us. At 80 SPS that is 2.4 % of the time, so about 2.4 of the 100 pulse-end interrupts per second are stretched by up to 300 us. At 7.4 us/deg that is up to 40 deg of single-frame command error, and a digital servo acts on a single frame. The reviewer missed a second casualty of the same 300 us blackout: USART0 RX. At 115200 baud a character takes 86.8 us, so 300 us brings 3.5 characters into a 2-deep RX buffer, which means overrun and lost host-command bytes (and dropped 'STOP'/'HB' lines). That is why I adopt BOTH remedies, not either one. Timer4 hardware PWM makes servo pulses immune to any interrupt latency. The direct-port HX711 read cuts the blackout to under 35 us, less than half a UART character. D6 = PH3/OC4A, D7 = PH4/OC4B, D3 = PE5 (read PINE), D4 = PG5 (write PORTG): all correct on the Mega 2560.
defense.proposed_change: Firmware: no Servo library. Timer4 in mode 14 (WGM4 = 1110), prescaler 8 (2 MHz), ICR4 = 39999 (50.000 Hz), OCR4A/OCR4B = 2 x pulse_us (0.5 us = 0.068 deg resolution on the 270 deg unit). Carousel on D6 (OC4A), stage on D7 (OC4B). The S-curve updates OCR4x in the TOV4 ISR so the update is glitch-free at the period boundary. Timer1 in mode 14, prescaler 1, ICR1 = 799 gives 20.0 kHz PWMA on D11 (OC1A), below the TB6612's 100 kHz maximum and inaudible. HX711: custom read with DT on PE5 and SCK on PG5 via direct PORTG/PINE access, with 4 NOP cycles (250 ns) per SCK half-period to meet the 0.2 us minimum. Interrupts are off for the 25-27 clocks only, about 30 us total, and the read is only attempted after DOUT goes LOW (polled, never waiting with interrupts off). Update the pin table in README and in software section 1 (see E-12).

defense.argument: I accept the rate. The green HX711 boards in kit B09K7G51KJ tie RATE (pin 15) to GND, which gives 10 SPS. At 10 SPS the 4-sample median spans 0.4 s and the effective lag is about 0.3 s. At q = 8 g/s the section 5.4 predictor (T_air + 0.1 s) under-calls by about 1.6 g, outside the +/-0.5 g water and +/-1.0 g developer tolerances. 80 SPS noise is 90 nV rms against 1 mV/V x 4.3 V / 1000 g = 4.3 uV/g, about 0.02 g, which is acceptable. Note that 80 SPS loses the HX711's 50/60 Hz rejection. 60 Hz pickup aliases to 20 Hz, which the tau = 0.1 s low-pass (fc 1.6 Hz) attenuates about 12x, so this is acceptable with the twisted bundle. I partly reject the mount location. I sliced WS-01_scale-base_qty1.stl: it is a 33 x 39 x 45 mm pillar at local X 0..33, Y 0..39 (world X 395..428, Y 455..494), plus two low cross-bars. The arm-A shoulder sweep (sweep.npy, pan axis (330,525)) is occupied at Z 30-50 right up to X ~390, so a module on the pillar's -X face would sit within about 5 mm of the arm base. The -Y face (world Y 455) is clear in the sweep at Z 0-45. It is also not under the pan: WS-02 spans X 431..505, so the pillar (X 395..428) is entirely west of it, 36 mm from the pour column at (468,475). I also prefer VHB to M2 pilots, because WS-01 then needs no generator change before tonight's print. The drip skirt is a WS-02 change (mechanical owner). Liquid can only reach the load cell where it runs off the pan's west edge between Y 468.6 and 481.3 (a 13 mm stretch), so a tape drip edge does the job without a reprint.
defense.proposed_change: Convert both HX711 boards (the kit has 2, one becomes a spare) to 80 SPS: cut the pin-15-to-GND trace (or lift pin 15) and bridge pin 15 to pin 16 (DVDD) with a solder blob. Verify by scoping DOUT or by firmware timing: 12.5 +/- 1 ms between ready edges. If that fails, re-tune the software to 10 SPS: median-3, tau 0.05 s, cut-off lead q*(T_air + 0.35 s), q* capped at 3 g/s. Mount the HX711 on the WS-01 pillar -Y face (world Y 455, X 397..426, Z 4..38), vertical, component side out, with 3M 4950 VHB (already in the BOM). Solder wires directly instead of fitting headers, then cover with Kapton tape. Twist the 4 load-cell wires and dress them down the -X/-Y corner. Run DT/SCK/VCC/GND as one twisted 4-core along the X-front rail slot, then the Y-left rail slot, to the box. Keep it >= 50 mm from the servo and N20 leads and cross them at 90 deg. Put a dab of neutral-cure silicone (or a Kapton wrap) on the load-cell lead exit and on the strain-gauge potting. WS-02: add a Kapton/PTFE tape drip edge folded 5 mm down along the west edge (world X 431, Y 460..490). A printed skirt is optional and is for the mechanical owner to decide.

defense.argument: Correct. The spacebar path depends on the asyncio loop, the USB link and the firmware all being healthy, and the barrel-jack pull is a two-handed reach to the Waveshare boards at world Y ~600 behind the arms. A latching NC mushroom in the bench power path is cheap and independent of software. Stop category 0 is acceptable for both bench actuators. The stage tray rides on PTFE glides with no horizontal gravity load, so it stays put when limp. The carousel only coasts briefly on the lazy Susan. The auger stops. At 8.4 V DC the break arc barely sustains (under about 12 V), so a standard 22 mm 10 A (Ith) NC block can break the normal 1-2 A running current, and the 3 A branch fuses cap the worst case. The arms cannot get a hardware stop without modifying borrowed hardware, so the switched strip is the right level, with the operator rule that torque-hold (spacebar) comes first because cutting arm power drops the beaker.
defense.proposed_change: Fit a 22 mm red latching mushroom e-stop with 2 x NC contact blocks in a yellow 1-hole box, at the front table edge within reach of the operator (front strip Y -60..40, near X 300). Wiring order: LiPo -> XT60 -> 10 A ATO -> INA226 10 mOhm shunt -> 2200 uF bulk cap -> e-stop pole 1 (16 AWG) -> relay COM/NO -> + bus -> 3 A carousel, 3 A stage and 1 A TB6612 VM branches. Pole 2: D2 (INT4) with INPUT_PULLUP, NC to GND, so pressing the button OR breaking a wire reads HIGH, which latches 'F ESTOP', disables PWM and opens the relay. Re-arm requires the button released (D2 LOW for 500 ms) AND host 'RESET', then INIT (E-02). Put both arm adapters (and nothing else) on a 4-outlet switched strip labelled 'ARMS OFF'. Software section 8 and README: first action is spacebar (torque-hold). Use ARMS OFF only for a pinch or collision, knowing the arms go limp and drop what they hold. Delete the sentence 'A hardware e-stop isn't feasible'.

defense.argument: I accept the interlock gap. The 'collar detected' check in section 8 is the commanded angle, and an open relay, a blown 3 A fuse, a flat pack or a slipped horn would leave the flask at ERUPT (450,102) while arm B pours at the funnel position (450,282). I accept the battery gap too: the 10k/4.7k divider gives 2.686 V at 8.4 V, which forces AVcc as reference, and USB VBUS of 4.75-5.25 V is a +/-5 % error. I modify both fixes. (a) Lever microswitches on the crank have an overtravel problem. The stop post is only 8.13 deg beyond WORK/ERUPT, i.e. 4.3 mm of arc at 30 mm radius, which is more than the D2F-L hinge-lever overtravel, so a crank driven into a stop (the E-03 scenario) would crush the switch. They also need mounting features on the already-printed ST-01. A non-contact Hall sensor plus a magnet on the TRAY senses what actually matters, the flask position, and is immune to horn slip. Near WORK the tray moves dY/dalpha = 150*cos(36.87 deg) = 120 mm/rad = 2.1 mm/deg. An A3144 with a 6 x 2 mm N52 magnet switches within about +/-4 mm, i.e. a +/-2 deg window, while one spline of slip (14.4 deg, 30 mm) reads definitively 'not at WORK'. (b) I reject the deck-home Hall. A carousel mis-index is not a hazard (it carries empty beakers or 7 g of yeast), and the grasp check in software section 3 (jaw at <= -68 deg means a miss, retry, then fault) already catches it. (c) Battery: the INTERNAL 2.56 V reference is specified at 2.33-2.79 V (+/-9 %), worse than AVcc, so it only works after calibration. The INA226 added in E-03 measures pack voltage directly (VBUS, 1.25 mV LSB, +/-0.1 % gain) with no divider or calibration. A divider is still needed downstream of the relay to detect 'relay or e-stop open'.
defense.proposed_change: Stage position: 2 x A3144 Hall sensors in heat-shrink (open-collector, 5 V, INPUT_PULLUP), fixed with VHB to the table or ST-01 under the tray's WORK and ERUPT positions. 2 x 6 x 2 mm N52 magnets (south face down) on the ST-04 underside, aligned at the WORK and ERUPT poses. WORK goes to D26 and ERUPT to D27. Before the flask goes on, set the sensor position so it switches within +/-2 deg of +/-36.87 deg. Pours, A_DEV_TO_FLASK and auger runs require D26 = WORK. STAGE_OUT requires the D27 transition within the move time + 0.5 s, else 'F STAGE_POS'. Pack voltage: from the INA226 VBUS (E-03). Warn at 7.2 V, refuse moves below 7.0 V measured with the relay open, and report 'F NO_PACK' below 5 V. Servo bus: a 33k/10k divider plus 100 nF on A1 downstream of the relay (8.4 V gives 1.953 V) with the AVcc reference. That is adequate for a presence check: relay closed and bus < 6.0 V gives 'F SERVO_PWR', relay open and bus > 2 V gives 'F RELAY_WELD'. Remove 'OPEN' and the 10k/4.7k text from software section 8. No deck Hall sensor.

defense.argument: I accept the star ground, the gauges and the drop calculation. 26 AWG is 133.9 mOhm/m, 22 AWG 52.9 mOhm/m and 20 AWG 33.3 mOhm/m. The routed stage path from the box at about (130,650) is |666-130| + |650-142| = 1.04 m. 2 x (1.0 x 0.134 + 0.3 x 0.053) = 0.30 Ohm, which is a 2.0 V drop at a 6.8 A stall and puts a 7.0 V pack below the servo's 6.0 V minimum. With 20 AWG it is 0.098 Ohm: 0.67 V at stall and 0.1 V at 1 A. I reject the XT30 power split. The JR crimp's roughly 3 A rating has to cover only the running current (under 1.2 A per servo, from the E-03 torques). A stall now lasts at most 300 ms (INA226 trip) before the relay opens, and 3-5 s at most on the 3 A fuse, which JR contacts tolerate easily. Adding a second connector per servo doubles the mis-mate and assembly risk for teammates working alone on Friday. The reviewer's own alternative, 20 AWG 'heavy-duty' JR extensions, is the right fix. Ground loop: this is real only if both a grounded laptop charger and a 3-prong arm adapter are plugged in. The simplest guarantee is to run the laptop on battery during runs, plus Class II arm adapters.
defense.proposed_change: Add a ground drawing to README 'Electrical' (E-12). The minus star is 2 x Wago 221-415 joined by a 50 mm 16 AWG jumper, mounted beside the bulk capacitor in the box. Landing there: LiPo- (16 AWG), the 2200 uF cap -, carousel servo - (20 AWG), stage servo - (20 AWG), TB6612 GND (its own 22 AWG, NOT via the Mega header), and ONE 22 AWG to Mega GND. HX711 GND, INA226 GND, relay-module GND and the A1 divider bottom go to Mega GND only. The + bus is 1 x Wago 221-415 after the relay. Gauges: 16 AWG silicone from XT60 through the fuse, shunt, e-stop and relay to the + Wago. 20 AWG HD JR extensions: stage 1.0 m, carousel 0.3 m. 22 AWG for TB6612 VM/GND and the N20. Twist every servo signal with its ground. Target drop < 0.7 V at 6.8 A (20 AWG gives 0.67 V). Arm adapters: 2-prong (Class II) only. Run the laptop on battery during demo runs (charge between runs).

defense.argument: Confirmed. EL-01 (design_data item 96) is hidden at world 18..202, 506..590. My own query of sweep.npy (2.5 mm voxels, LO (-10,40,-20)) gives 11.0 % of its footprint overflown between Z 57.5 and 242.5. Behind the arms (X 265-665, Y 600-700) it is 31.1 %. X 20-235, Y 600-695 is 0.0 % at every Z. The candidate centre (130,650) is sqrt(320^2 + 548^2) = 635 mm from the eruption point (450,102). It also clears the BESSEY clamp at X 246-264, Y 650+. One amendment: the sweep is a column test over all Z (the 'any over Z' footprint is 0 %), so a plan3.py re-run cannot find a hit there. I keep it only as a cheap confirmation once the EL-02 body exists in the scene.
defense.proposed_change: Model EL-02 (visible) as an electronics box with a lid, outer size 200 x 90 x 60 mm, at world X 25..225, Y 602..692, Z 0..60. Make it printed PLA (1 print, fits the A1) or a bought ABS project box of 200 x 120 x 75 mm max. It holds the Mega 2560 Pro on 4 x M3 x 8 standoffs, the TB6612, the relay module, the INA226, the 3 inline ATO holders, the Wago star/bus and the 2200 uF cap, with cable exits on the +Y and -X faces only. The LiPo goes in its LiPo bag, Velcro-strapped beside the box at about (130,650), >= 600 mm from (450,102). The e-stop is separate, at the front edge (E-06). Add EL-02 to the print plan/BOM and to the plan3 scene as an obstacle for a confirmation run.

defense.argument: The contradiction is real: README line 429 says 70 % and software section 6 says 100 % (8.4 V on a 6 V motor). A fixed duty gives 5.9 V at 8.4 V and 4.9 V at 7.0 V. Time-based counting therefore drifts about 17 % over a pack, and nothing detects a yeast-jam stall. The weigh-back in VERIFY_YEAST does catch a short dose, but only after the beaker has travelled to the scale, and a persistent jam would then loop through correction doses. I verified the encoder fit. In DH-01_yeast-auger-head_qty1_SUPPORTS.stl the N20 occupies local X 41-53, Y 21.5-49, Z 14-26 (world 81-93, 271.5-299, 149-161), cantilevered from the face at Y 49-52. Slices at Z 15/20/25 show local X 30-67, Y 0-48 empty, so a +8-10 mm encoder can extends into Y 11.5-21.5 with no change to DH-01 tonight. Encoder rate: a 60 rpm N20 has a gearbox of about 1:250, so a 7 PPR magnetic encoder gives about 1750 rising edges per output rev on channel A. At 1 rev/s that is about 1750 ISR/s at 3-4 us each, about 0.6 % CPU. Timer4 PWM (E-04) is unaffected, and a 30 us HX711 blackout cannot lose an edge (period about 570 us). The reversal transient at the compensated 6 V is about 2 x stall, about 1.6 A, inside the TB6612's 3.2 A pulse rating, but coast plus brake costs nothing.
defense.proposed_change: Buy the encoder N20, 6 V 60 rpm, 3 mm D-shaft, same 12 x 10 gearbox, 7 PPR magnetic Hall encoder. Encoder A goes to D18 (INT3) and B to D19 (INT2), VCC 5 V, GND to Mega GND. Count A rising edges, using B for direction. Calibrate edges/rev on Friday. Stall: fewer than 10 % of the expected edges in 100 ms at duty > 30 % gives coast 30 ms, brake 20 ms, reverse 1/4 rev, retry. 3 stalls give 'F AUGER_JAM'. Duty = min(1, 6.0 V / V_pack) using the INA226 VBUS (E-07), so the motor always averages 6.0 V. PWM is 20 kHz on D11 (E-04). Fuse the TB6612 VM branch with a 1 A ATO inline holder. Solder 100 nF ceramic across the N20 tabs plus 2 x 47 nF tab to can. Correct README line 429 and software section 6 to 'voltage-compensated 6.0 V, encoder-counted', and close the section 6/10 OPEN items. If the encoder N20 cannot arrive by Friday, the fallback is the voltage-compensated duty plus a stall check on the INA226 sum (a step of more than 0.4 A above the pre-run baseline for 200 ms during an auger run), with the README stating that dose accuracy then relies on the VERIFY_YEAST weigh-back.

defense.argument: Agreed. README lines 186-192 size the 7.4 V variant at '5 V, >= 4 A' against its own estimate of 4-5 A peaks, and the 12 V variant at 12 V 5 A against 4-5 A, i.e. 0-25 % over the rating. The README itself says sag causes servo resets, and an STS3215 under-voltage unload mid-pour drops a beaker of 12 % developer. All four candidate supplies use the same 5.5 x 2.1 barrel. One addition: many 8 A adapters ship with 5.5 x 2.5 mm plugs. A 2.5 plug goes into the Waveshare 2.1 jack but makes an intermittent centre contact, which is exactly the brown-out we are trying to remove. Another addition: the STS3215 present-voltage register (0.1 V) gives free in-run supply monitoring, so we can verify the margin instead of trusting it.
defense.proposed_change: As soon as SIGRobotics confirms the variant, buy 2 adapters of >= 6.5 A: 5 V 8 A for C001/C044/C046 or 12 V 8 A for C018/C047, with a 5.5 x 2.1 mm centre-positive plug stated in the listing. Bring only that voltage family. Use coloured heat-shrink bands on each adapter plug and each arm's jack (red = 12 V, blue = 5 V) plus a label 'ARM A/B, 12 V' (or 5 V). Before first power-on, measure each barrel with a multimeter against its label. Software: the guard reads present_voltage on all 6 servos at 10 Hz. Warn below 0.92 x nominal, and torque-hold plus fault 'F ARM_SUPPLY' below 0.85 x nominal for 100 ms. Add this to README 'SO-101 arms' and to the BOM (E-13).

defense.argument: Confirmed line by line. Lines 223-234 still describe a 6 V 10 A supply, PCA9685/ESP32, 'all grounds together' and 'a wall supply is simpler', while lines 208-216 say the LiPo and Mega replace those. Line 224 quotes 6 V currents, line 216 says '9-14 A' and line 214 says '1000-2200 uF' while line 443 says 2200 uF. Line 429 (70 %) contradicts software section 6 (100 %). Lines 215 and software section 1 say USB-C, but the common Mega 2560 Pro (Embed) has micro-USB with a CH340G. The repository layout (lines 663-676) omits docs/. The only wiring description is the prose at lines 425-430. The pin table below is the final one after E-02..E-10 (it differs from the reviewer's: no microswitches and no deck Hall, and pack voltage comes from the INA226, not an A0 divider).
defense.proposed_change: Delete README lines 223-234 and the wiring prose at lines 425-430. Replace them with one 'Electrical' section: (a) docs/electrical_block.svg: LiPo 2S -> XT60 -> 10 A ATO -> INA226 10 mOhm shunt -> 2200 uF 16 V -> e-stop pole 1 -> relay (D25) -> + bus Wago -> 3 A carousel, 3 A stage (+ 470 uF at the stage end), 1 A TB6612 VM; minus star per E-08; Mega on USB; HX711 at WS-01. (b) Pin table: D2 e-stop sense (NC to GND, PULLUP); D3 HX711 DT (PE5); D4 HX711 SCK (PG5); D6 carousel OC4A; D7 stage OC4B; D11 PWMA OC1A 20 kHz; D18/D19 encoder A/B; D20/D21 INA226 SDA/SCL (0x40); D22 AIN1; D23 AIN2; D24 STBY; D25 relay IN (10k pull-down); D26 stage WORK Hall; D27 stage ERUPT Hall; A1 servo-bus divider 33k/10k + 100 nF. (c) A harness table (from, to, gauge, length, connector) per E-08. (d) Currents at 8.4 V: idle about 0.6 A/servo (to be measured, E-16), working < 1.2 A/servo, stall 6.8 A/servo (cut by 3 A fuse and 300 ms INA trip), N20 < 0.8 A. Make software section 1 reference this table instead of its own pin list. Replace 'USB-C' with the connector found on inspecting the board. Add docs/ to the repository layout.

defense.argument: I accept the gap: the BOM lists only the fuse lead, the cap, HX711, TB6612 and N20. I adjust the list to the design as resolved above: no D2F-L or deck Hall (E-07), one INA226 with the shunt replaced (E-03), and HD 20 AWG JR extensions instead of XT30 (E-08). I relax the pack-capacity requirement. The relay is open between runs (E-16), so idle draw between runs is zero. A run is about 10 min at about 1.5 A average, about 250 mAh, so a 2200 mAh pack at 80 % usable covers about 7 runs. 4000-5000 mAh is preferred but not mandatory. Charger and bag: the owner has the pack, so confirm a balance charger is owned before buying one. A powered hub is needed: 3 USB-serial devices, and laptops commonly have 2 ports.
defense.proposed_change: Add to the README BOM: 2S LiPo >= 2200 mAh (preferred 5000 mAh 30C, 37 Wh) with XT60 (confirm owned); 2S balance charger (confirm owned); LiPo-safe bag; 1-8S cell checker/alarm set to 3.5 V/cell; powered 4-port USB 3 hub; 1 m data cable for the Mega (micro-USB or USB-C after inspection); 20 AWG HD JR servo extensions 1.0 m x1 and 0.3 m x1 (+1 spare); 16/20/22 AWG silicone wire, 2 m each; Wago 221-415 x4 (one spare); inline ATO fuse holders x3 with 3 A x4, 1 A x2 and spare 10 A x2; 22 mm latching NC mushroom e-stop (2 NC blocks) with yellow box; 5 V 1-channel relay module with H/L jumper; INA226 breakout plus a 10 mOhm 2512 2 W shunt resistor; resistors 33k and 10k (x2 each), 10k pull-down x2, 100 nF ceramics x6, 47 nF x2, 470 uF 16 V low-ESR x2; A3144 Hall sensors x3 (one spare); 6 x 2 mm N52 magnets x4; encoder N20 6 V 60 rpm 7 PPR; screw-terminal shield or perfboard for the Mega 2560 Pro; heat-shrink assortment; zip ties; 3M adhesive tie mounts x10; 4-outlet switched power strip; Kapton tape; neutral-cure silicone; multimeter (borrow if owned); 1 spare M45CHW; 2 arm adapters per E-11.

defense.argument: I partly reject the voltage concern. The M45CHW's 6.0-8.4 V 'HV' rating exists precisely to cover a full 2S pack. Common balance chargers terminate at 4.20 V/cell within about 10-20 mV. A fresh pack sags below 8.4 V within seconds at the 1-1.5 A load. So charging to 4.15 V/cell is not needed, but a firmware check costs nothing. I accept the capacitor points with one correction. The bulk cap must be upstream of the relay AND the e-stop, so that neither contact ever switches the 2200 uF inrush. 2200 uF x 8.4 V = 18.5 mC (78 mJ) through about 30 mOhm is a 280 A peak, which can weld a 10 A relay. With the cap upstream, a weld would also silently defeat the E-02 gating, hence the weld check. That inrush lands on the XT60 instead, which is designed for it: 78 mJ at 2S is a minor spark, unlike 6S, where anti-spark plugs matter. Local decoupling only matters at the 1.0 m stage run (about 1 uH plus 0.07 Ohm). The carousel's 0.3 m lead does not need it. A 470 uF cap at the stage end adds just 17 mJ of relay inrush.
defense.proposed_change: Charge on a balance charger at the standard 4.20 V/cell, never in LiHV mode. Firmware warns if INA226 VBUS > 8.50 V at arm time. Put the 2200 uF 16 V directly after the INA226 shunt, upstream of the e-stop and relay. Add one 470 uF 16 V low-ESR cap at the stage servo end of the 1.0 m extension (soldered across +/- at the JR plug and heat-shrunk). Accept the XT60 connect spark, and plug the pack in with the relay open (it is always open at boot per E-02). A1 > 2 V with the relay off reports 'F RELAY_WELD' (E-02).

defense.argument: Agreed, with one correction to the geometry. The N20 bbox (design_data item 142, world X 81-93, Y 271.5-299, Z 149-161) has corners 108.5-136 mm from the turntable axis (175,370). So part of the motor is already inside the 118 mm deck radius in plan, which is necessary because it doses into a pocket at r = 88 mm. It sits about 90 mm above the deck (Z 54.6-61.6) and about 27 mm above the beaker rims (about Z 122), so a drooping lead would hang into the beakers and onto the TT-04 rim. The carousel and stage servos are stationary, so no slip ring is needed. The arm cables need a service loop for pan rotation.
defense.proposed_change: Solder 22 AWG leads to the N20 tabs and pot the tabs and caps (E-10) in hot glue. Zip-tie the N20 and encoder leads to the AG-01 post (world X 40-70) at Z 140 and Z 20 using adhesive tie mounts, then run them along the AG-01 bar and the Y-left rail slot under a 2020 slot-cover strip to EL-02 (about 600 mm). Stage lead: along the Y-right rail slot (X 675), then the X-back rail slot, to EL-02. Carousel lead: from the TT-01 west window (world X ~121, Y 383..394) north along the table to EL-02. HX711 bundle: per E-05. Clip the arm USB and barrel cables flat in the X-back rail slot and run them straight +Y to the table edge, with a 100 mm service loop at each arm base. Dress the load-cell lead along the WS-01 underside with 2 adhesive tie mounts.

defense.argument: I accept measuring idle current and temperature. The servodatabase 0.6 A figure is a no-load running figure, and true holding draw is likely 0.1-0.3 A, but the pocket is closed PLA with a 55-60 deg C softening point, so it must be measured. Opening the relay between runs (E-02) removes standby heat and battery drain regardless. Both TT-01 and ST-01 also gain a lead opening (E-01), which vents the pocket slightly. I accept the USB power settings. I reject the port-selection method as written. The CH340G (Mega) reports no USB serial number (iSerial = 0), and the Waveshare bus boards use CH340/CH343-family bridges that can share VID:PID 1A86:7523 or 55D3. So 'select by serial number or VID:PID' cannot tell the three devices apart. The robust method is the physical hub port (pyserial ListPortInfo.location) plus an identity probe.
defense.proposed_change: Friday bring-up: power each servo from the 2 A bench supply at 8.4 V, holding at the WORK/station angles, and measure the current. Hold for 30 min in its pocket and check the case and pocket wall with the kitchen thermometer. The limit is < 45 deg C. Firmware opens the relay after 60 s idle between runs regardless of the measurement, and re-arms via INIT. Software: config.yaml maps devices by hub port (ListPortInfo.location, ports labelled A/B/MEGA on the powered hub). At startup the Mega must answer '<seq> ID' with 'OK <seq> WLB-MEGA v1', and each arm bus must answer a Feetech ping on IDs 1-6 with the stored calibration homing offsets matching that arm, otherwise refuse to start. Demo laptop: disable USB selective suspend (Power Options), sleep and lid-close actions on battery and AC, and install the CH340 (and CH343, if the Waveshare boards use it) drivers before Thursday.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the owner's amendment. The L-relief is better than my side-only notch. In local coordinates the spline sits at the origin, so the TT-01 pocket (X -30.3..+10.3) puts the far, lead end at -X, and the ST-01 pocket (X -10.3..+30.3) puts it at +X. With 0.3 mm per side, a grommet standing 2-3 mm proud on the end face will not seat unless the end wall is relieved. On TT-01 the 4 mm channel (X -34.3..-30.3) runs from the grommet up into the north cavity, which is open from x -52 to +20 north of y +12.3. That cavity connects to the existing west window (11 x 28 mm), which is big enough to pass the JR plug. On ST-01, the +X exit at world X 701, Y about 142 is south of RAIL-Y-RIGHT (rails.py: X 665-685, Y 270-670), so the lead can run north along X about 700 and enter the rail slot at Y 270. Adhesive tie mounts instead of printed slots are acceptable because both parts are already printed.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Servo install step 0 (README 'Assembly and every fastener'): dry-fit each M45CHW and record which face the grommet is on, its Y and its height. TT-01: end-wall relief at local X -34.3..-30.3, Y from (grommet Y - 5) to +12.3, Z from (grommet bottom - 2) to 29.3, plus a break-out in the +Y sleeve at X -32.3..-24, Y +10.3..+12.3 over the same Z. Exit through the west window (world X about 121, Y 383-394). ST-01: an 8 mm slot centred on the grommet Y, through the full 14.7 mm +X wall (local x 30.3-45, world X 701), from Z 35.3 down to 2 mm below the grommet. Deburr the cuts and line them with Kapton. Put a 3M tie mount 15 mm outside each exit. Pass criterion: the servo seats flush on its ears with no force, and the lead moves freely 2 mm in and out. CAD: add the grommet (8 x 3 x 6 mm) and the lead to hw_funcs.servo(), add the relief and slot to the TT-01 and ST-01 generators, and re-run the interference check before any reprint.

rebuttal.argument: Two of the owner's corrections are right. Power the bus first with the signal held LOW, then start the pulses; this avoids back-powering the servo MCU through the signal pin clamp. The MOVING flag is also needed, because a reset mid-move leaves the stored pulse wrong. I withdraw the 10 uF RESET cap. With the relay off at reset, in the bootloader and with USB unplugged (coil on USB 5 V, H-trigger jumper and a 10 k pull-down), a reset only makes the servos go limp. The tray carries no horizontal gravity load on its PTFE glides, so it stays put. A cap that teammates must remove before re-flashing is a real trap. One gap remains in the recovery path. 'Jog the servos at low speed' cannot work when the position is unknown, because the first pulse still steps straight to its target at full speed. Recovery has to put the mechanism in a known pose by hand with the relay open. The E-07 Hall sensors give a hardware cross-check on the stage at no extra cost. Also, the 'F RELAY_WELD' check must allow time for the 470 uF stage cap to bleed down.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Implement as the owner proposed. SRD-05VDC-SL-C module with the H jumper, IN on D25 with 10 kOhm to GND at the module, coil on USB 5 V. Boot state: relay off, D6/D7 driven LOW, COM4A/B off. Arm sequence on 'INIT <tt_us> <st_us>': compare with the EEPROM copy (MOVING flag set at move start and cleared at move end). Mismatch > 20 us or MOVING=1 gives ERR POS_UNKNOWN. On match: close relay, wait 200 ms, load OCR4A/B, enable COM bits. Shutdown is the reverse. Added conditions: (a) INIT is also refused unless the stage Hall state agrees with st_us: D26 active for the WORK pulse, D27 active for the ERUPT pulse, otherwise ERR POS_UNKNOWN. (b) POS_UNKNOWN recovery, written in the README: relay open, flask empty; by hand, push the tray to WORK until D26 reads active and turn the carousel to the painted home mark; then send 'INIT FORCE', which loads the WORK and home pulses. No other recovery path. (c) RELAY_WELD is evaluated 1.5 s after the relay is commanded open (A1 > 2 V). (d) pyserial: dtr=False and rts=False before open(). Persist pulses to JSON after every OK. (e) Bring-up rule: flask empty and no payload until a forced reset followed by re-arm has been shown twice with no motion at arm. Confirm at bring-up that the M45CHW stays limp when powered with no pulse; if it moves, stop and re-review. (f) Enable the 250 ms WDT only after a WDT reset on this board's bootloader is shown to work; the relay stays open through it. No RESET capacitor.

rebuttal.argument: The owner's corrections are valid. I accept them on these grounds. (1) 45 - 36.87 = 8.13 deg of design clearance makes my '>= 8 deg' test impossible to pass, so a +/-2 deg check (>= 6 deg clear) is right. (2) One INA226 on the bus sum is enough, because a single 6.8 A stall is more than 3x every legitimate sum. (3) The R100 shunt on the CJMCU-226 saturates at 81.92 mV / 0.1 Ohm = 0.82 A, so it must be replaced; with 10 mOhm, full scale is 8.19 A. One residual risk is in the trip threshold. The INA226 sits upstream of everything, so it also sees the TB6612. Two servos idling at the listed 0.6 A (1.2 A), the N20 at up to 0.8 A and one servo moving (about 1 A) add to about 3.0 A, which would false-trip a fixed 2.5 A threshold. The threshold must be set from measurement, and auger runs must not overlap servo moves. Inrush check: plugging in charges the 2200 uF downstream of the shunt. The pulse is 280 A peak with tau about 66 us, so I^2*t is about 2.6 A^2*s, under a 10 A ATO's melting I^2*t, and about 20 mJ lands in the 2512 shunt. That is acceptable for a metal-strip 2 W part, so use metal-strip and not thick-film.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Keep the 10 A main ATO on 16 AWG. Add inline 3 A ATO holders on the carousel and stage + branches, downstream of the relay. Fit one INA226 with a 10 mOhm 2512 2 W metal-strip shunt replacing R100, at address 0x40 on D20/D21, placed after the 10 A fuse and before the 2200 uF cap, the e-stop and the relay. Sample at 50 Hz. Trip (PWM off, relay open, 'F STALL <A>'): sum > I_trip for 300 ms, or any saturated reading (>= 8.0 A) immediately. I_trip defaults to 2.5 A. On Friday, set it to 1.3 x the largest 300 ms-average sum seen over one full dry run, clamped to 2.0-4.0 A, and store it in config.yaml. The sequencer must never run the auger at the same time as a servo move. Commissioning before the crank is bolted: horn on the spline nearest alpha 0, jog to the +/-36.87 deg pulses with no load, and confirm with a printed 36.87/45 deg gauge that the crank is within +/-2 deg (>= 6 deg from each stop post). Record the trim in config.yaml. Add 1 spare M45CHW (B09VBFZ9KW) to the BOM.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted in full. The owner's added USART0 RX overrun argument is correct: 300 us / 86.8 us is 3.5 characters at 115200 baud, against a 2-byte RX FIFO. That justifies doing both remedies. The pin mappings check out on the ATmega2560: D6 = PH3/OC4A, D7 = PH4/OC4B, D3 = PE5, D4 = PG5, D11 = PB5/OC1A, D2 = PE4/INT4, D18/D19 = INT3/INT2 and D20/D21 = SDA/SCL. One technical note: in mode 14 Fast PWM, OCR4A/B are double-buffered and latch at TOP. Writes are therefore already glitch-free, so the TOV4 ISR is optional; it is fine as the place where the S-curve steps once per frame.
rebuttal.final_requirement: No Servo library. Timer4 mode 14, prescaler 8, ICR4 = 39999 (50 Hz), OCR4x = 2 x pulse_us. Carousel on D6 (OC4A), stage on D7 (OC4B). S-curve set-points written once per frame (TOV4). Timer1 mode 14, prescaler 1, ICR1 = 799 for 20 kHz PWMA on D11. HX711 read: direct PINE5 (DT, D3) and PORTG5 (SCK, D4), >= 250 ns per SCK half-period, interrupts disabled only for the 25-27 clocks (< 35 us total, SCK high always < 50 us), started only after DOUT is seen LOW. The pin table in README 'Electrical' is the single source; software section 1 references it.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the counter on mounting location. WS-01 is a pillar at world X 395-428, Y 455-494, which is entirely west of WS-02 (X 431-505) and 36 mm from the pour column. Its -X face is about 5 mm from the arm-A shoulder sweep, so the -Y face (Y 455) is the correct choice. Using VHB avoids changing tonight's print. The tape drip edge is sound for the exposed 13 mm stretch of load cell (Y 468.6-481.3) west of the pan edge at X 431. The 80 SPS conversion (pin 15 RATE to pin 16 DVDD) is correct. Aliasing of 60 Hz to 20 Hz, attenuated about 12x by the tau = 0.1 s filter, is acceptable with twisted leads.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Convert both HX711 boards to 80 SPS: cut the pin 15 to GND trace and bridge pin 15 to pin 16. Pass: ready edges 12.5 +/- 1 ms apart, logged by firmware. If that fails, use the 10 SPS software set: median-3, tau 0.05 s, lead q*(T_air + 0.35 s), q* capped at 3 g/s. Mount on the WS-01 -Y face (world Y 455, X 397-426, Z 4-38), component side out, with 3M 4950 VHB. Wires soldered directly and covered with Kapton. Load-cell wires twisted. DT/SCK/VCC/GND as a twisted 4-core along the X-front then Y-left rail slots, >= 50 mm from servo and N20 leads and crossing them at 90 deg. Neutral-cure silicone on the load-cell lead exit. Kapton or PTFE tape drip edge folded 5 mm down along the WS-02 west edge (X 431, Y 460-490). Measure noise at bring-up: 100 samples at no load must give a std below 0.1 g.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted. The wiring order puts the 2200 uF upstream of both the e-stop and the relay, so neither contact switches the capacitor inrush. Pole 2 is NC to GND with a pullup, so a pressed button and a broken wire both read as a stop (fail-safe). Breaking at 8.4 V DC is within a 10 A Ith block's capability for the 1-2 A running current. A stall is limited by the 300 ms INA trip, which opens the relay first. The 'ARMS OFF' strip, with spacebar torque-hold as the first action, is the right level for borrowed arms.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Fit a 22 mm red latching mushroom e-stop with 2 NC blocks in a yellow box at the front table edge (Y -60..40, near X 300). Pole 1 in 16 AWG: LiPo, XT60, 10 A ATO, INA226 shunt, 2200 uF, pole 1, relay COM/NO, + bus Wago, then the 3 A, 3 A and 1 A branches. Pole 2: D2, INPUT_PULLUP, NC to GND. HIGH latches F ESTOP, disables PWM and opens the relay. Re-arm needs D2 LOW for 500 ms, then host RESET, then INIT (E-02). Both arm adapters, and nothing else, go on a switched strip labelled 'ARMS OFF'. Software section 8 and README: spacebar torque-hold first; ARMS OFF only for a pinch or collision, knowing the arms drop what they hold. Delete 'A hardware e-stop isn't feasible'. Test at bring-up: press the e-stop during a slow stage move, the bus must go below 1 V within 1 s and the host must show F ESTOP.

rebuttal.argument: I accept all three counters. (a) The 8.13 deg of overtravel at the stop is 4.3 mm at a 30 mm radius, which exceeds D2F-L lever overtravel. Halls on the tray sense the flask position directly and are immune to horn slip. (b) A carousel mis-index is not a hazard, and the grasp check catches it. (c) The ATmega2560 internal 2.56 V reference is specified at 2.33-2.79 V, so the INA226 VBUS reading is better. I checked the mechanical fit. The REF-GLIDE PTFE pads are 6.6 mm tall (design_data items 108-111, Z 0-6.6), and the ST-04 STL underside is flat (Z 0 face across X -79..95, Y -175..29 local). An A3144 TO-92S lying flat (1.5 mm) on VHB (1.1 mm) plus a 2 mm magnet on the tray underside uses 4.6 mm of the 6.6 mm gap, leaving 2.0 mm running clearance. At a sensor-to-magnet gap of about 2.5 mm, a 6 x 2 N52 gives about 0.14 T on axis, far above the A3144 operate point (<= 35 mT), so it will switch. But the lateral window will be wider than the claimed +/-4 mm, about +/-5-6 mm or +/-2.5-3 deg. That still rejects a 30 mm one-spline slip. The sensors sit on the table under the tray's swept path, so they must also be clear of the glides' swept tracks.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Fit 2 A3144 sensors (heat-shrunk, lying flat, VHB to the table): WORK on D26, ERUPT on D27, INPUT_PULLUP. Place each outside the four PTFE glides' swept tracks with >= 5 mm margin; check by sliding the tray WORK to ERUPT by hand with the relay open. Glue 2 6 x 2 mm N52 magnets (south face down) to the ST-04 underside at the matching poses. Running clearance must be >= 1.5 mm. Measure the switching window by hand at commissioning; it must be <= +/-3 deg about +/-36.87 deg, otherwise move the sensor out of axis. Pours, A_DEV_TO_FLASK and auger runs require D26 active. STAGE_OUT requires D27 within the move time + 0.5 s, otherwise F STAGE_POS. Pack voltage from INA226 VBUS: warn at 7.2 V, refuse moves below 7.0 V measured with the relay open, F NO_PACK below 5 V, warn above 8.50 V at arm. Servo bus: 33k/10k divider + 100 nF on A1 (AVcc reference) downstream of the relay. Relay closed and A1 below 6.0 V gives F SERVO_PWR. Relay open for more than 1.5 s and A1 above 2 V gives F RELAY_WELD. No deck Hall. Remove 'OPEN' and the 10k/4.7k text from software section 8.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the rejection of XT30. With the 300 ms INA trip and the 3 A fuse, a JR crimp only has to carry under 1.2 A continuously plus short peaks, and a second connector per servo doubles the mis-mate risk for teammates working alone. 20 AWG HD JR extensions meet the drop target: 2 x (1.0 x 0.0333 + 0.3 x 0.053) = 0.098 Ohm, or 0.67 V at a 6.8 A stall. Battery-powered laptop plus Class II arm adapters removes the mains-earth loop. There is no loop through the arm buses, because each Class II adapter connects to the USB ground at only one point.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Minus star: 2 Wago 221-415 joined by 50 mm of 16 AWG, beside the bulk cap in EL-02. Land there: LiPo-, cap-, carousel servo-, stage servo-, TB6612 GND (own 22 AWG) and ONE 22 AWG to Mega GND. HX711, INA226, relay-module and A1-divider grounds go to Mega GND only. + bus: 1 Wago 221-415 after the relay. Gauges: 16 AWG silicone XT60 through the fuse, shunt, e-stop and relay to the + Wago. 20 AWG HD JR extensions: stage 1.0 m, carousel 0.3 m. 22 AWG for TB6612 VM/GND and the N20. Every servo signal twisted with its ground. Bring-up test: at a commanded stage move, the voltage at the stage JR plug must be within 0.3 V of the pack. Arm adapters Class II (2-prong) only. Laptop on battery during runs. The ground drawing goes into README 'Electrical'.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted, and I confirmed the clearances. EL-02 at X 25-225, Y 602-692 is west of RAIL-X-BACK (which starts at X 265, rails.py line 24) and of RAIL-Y-LEFT (X 245-265). It is in the 0 % overflown zone and clears the clamp at X 246-264. The owner is right that a column-type sweep test would not catch a collision there. A plan3 run is therefore a confirmation, not a gate.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Model EL-02 (visible) at world X 25-225, Y 602-692, Z 0-60, with a lid. Printed PLA or bought ABS (max 200 x 120 x 75). It holds the Mega 2560 Pro on 4 x M3 x 8 standoffs, the TB6612, the relay, the INA226, 3 inline ATO holders, the Wagos and the 2200 uF cap. Cable exits on +Y and -X only. The LiPo goes in its LiPo bag, Velcro-strapped beside the box at about (130,650), >= 600 mm from (450,102). Add EL-02 to the print plan or BOM and to the plan3 scene for a confirmation run.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted. The owner verified the encoder fits: DH-01 local X 30-67, Y 0-48, Z 12-28 is empty, so the can extends into Y 11.5-21.5 with no reprint. The ISR load (about 1750 edges/s, about 0.6 % CPU) and the 570 us edge period are fine alongside the 35 us HX711 blackout. The INA-based fallback is a reasonable plan B.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Fit the encoder N20 (6 V, 60 rpm, 7 PPR): A on D18, B on D19, 5 V and Mega GND. Calibrate edges per output rev on Friday and store it in config.yaml. Stall: fewer than 10 % of expected edges in 100 ms at duty > 30 % gives coast 30 ms, brake 20 ms, reverse 1/4 rev, retry. 3 stalls give F AUGER_JAM. Duty = min(1, 6.0 / V_pack(INA226)), 20 kHz on D11. TB6612 VM branch on a 1 A ATO. 100 nF across the N20 tabs plus 2 x 47 nF tab to can, potted in hot glue. Fix README line 429 and software section 6 to read 'voltage-compensated 6.0 V, encoder-counted'. If the encoder N20 has not arrived by Friday: compensated duty plus an INA step > 0.4 A for 200 ms as the stall test, with the README stating that dosing then relies on the VERIFY_YEAST weigh-back.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted. The owner adds two good points: 5.5 x 2.5 plugs give intermittent contact in 2.1 jacks, and the free STS3215 present-voltage monitoring (0.1 V resolution) turns the margin from an assumption into a measurement.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Buy 2 adapters rated >= 6.5 A (5 V 8 A or 12 V 8 A to match the confirmed arm variant), with a 5.5 x 2.1 mm centre-positive plug stated in the listing. Bring one voltage family only. Colour bands (red 12 V, blue 5 V) and 'ARM A/B, <V>' labels on each plug and jack. Multimeter check at each barrel before first power-on. Guard reads present_voltage on all 6 servos at 10 Hz: warn below 0.92 x nominal; torque-hold plus F ARM_SUPPLY below 0.85 x nominal for 100 ms. Add to README 'SO-101 arms' and the BOM.

rebuttal.argument: Accepted, and I checked the owner's final pin table for conflicts. D2 INT4, D3 PE5, D4 PG5, D6/D7 OC4A/B, D11 OC1A, D18/D19 INT3/INT2, D20/D21 TWI, D22-D27 GPIO, A1. There are no timer or interrupt collisions, and Timer0 (millis) and Timer5 are untouched. The table correctly reflects the resolved design: no microswitches, no deck Hall, and pack voltage from the INA226.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Delete README lines 223-234 and the prose at 425-430. Add one 'Electrical' section with: (a) docs/electrical_block.svg showing the power chain exactly as in E-06, the minus star from E-08, the Mega on USB and the HX711 at WS-01; (b) the pin table as the owner proposed; (c) a harness table (from, to, gauge, length, connector, fuse) covering every wire in E-08, E-10 and E-15; (d) currents at 8.4 V (idle per servo to be measured per E-16, working < 1.2 A/servo, stall 6.8 A cut by the 300 ms INA trip and the 3 A fuse, N20 < 0.8 A). Software section 1 references this table and carries no pin list of its own. Replace 'USB-C' with the connector found on the board. Add docs/ to the repository layout. No remaining mention of PCA9685, a 6 V 10 A supply, '9-14 A', '1000-2200 uF' or 70 % PWM anywhere in the repo (grep must return none).

rebuttal.argument: I accept the relaxed pack capacity. With the relay open between runs, about 250 mAh per run means a 2200 mAh pack covers about 7 runs, which is enough with the charger at the venue. The list matches the resolved design. The user requires every item to be in the repository BOM, so this must be a real table in README 'What you buy' (or a bom file it links to), not prose. It also needs the few consumables the resolutions introduced.
rebuttal.final_requirement: README 'What you buy' (the repo BOM) gets one row per item with quantity, link or ASIN where available, price and 'owned / to buy'. Items: 2S LiPo >= 2200 mAh with XT60 (5000 mAh 30C preferred); 2S balance charger; LiPo bag; cell checker/alarm set to 3.5 V/cell; powered 4-port USB 3 hub; 1 m Mega data cable; 20 AWG HD JR extensions 1.0 m x1 and 0.3 m x1 (+1 spare); 16/20/22 AWG silicone wire 2 m each; Wago 221-415 x4; inline ATO holders x3 with 3 A x4, 1 A x2 and spare 10 A x2; 22 mm latching NC e-stop (2 NC) with yellow box; 5 V relay module with H/L jumper; INA226 breakout plus 10 mOhm 2512 2 W metal-strip shunt; 33k x2, 10k x4 (dividers and pull-downs), 100 nF x6, 47 nF x2, 470 uF 16 V low-ESR x2, 2200 uF 16 V x1; A3144 x3; 6 x 2 mm N52 magnets x4; encoder N20 6 V 60 rpm 7 PPR; screw-terminal shield or perfboard for the Mega 2560 Pro; heat-shrink; zip ties; 3M tie mounts x10; Kapton tape; neutral-cure silicone; 4-outlet switched strip; 2 Class II arm adapters (E-11); 1 spare M45CHW; multimeter (borrowed or owned); a printed 36.87/45 deg angle gauge added to the print plan. Mark the stage-end 470 uF in the harness table.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the counter. The 6.0-8.4 V HV rating covers a 2S pack charged to 4.20 V/cell, and the pack sags within seconds under a 1-1.5 A load. Putting the 2200 uF upstream of both the e-stop and the relay is better than my proposal (upstream of the relay only). The 78 mJ connect spark at 2S is benign on an XT60, and the inrush I^2*t (about 2.6 A^2*s) does not stress the 10 A ATO. Local decoupling only at the 1.0 m stage run is justified.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Standard 4.20 V/cell balance charge, never LiHV mode. Firmware warns if INA226 VBUS > 8.50 V at arm. 2200 uF 16 V directly after the shunt, upstream of the e-stop and relay. 470 uF 16 V low-ESR across +/- at the stage JR plug, heat-shrunk. Plug in the pack only with the relay open (the boot default). RELAY_WELD check per E-02/E-07.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the geometry correction. The N20 corners are 108.5-136 mm from the axis, partly inside the 118 mm deck radius and about 27 mm above the beaker rims. The droop hazard is into the beakers, which makes tying the leads even more important. The routing plan is consistent with EL-02's position and with the rail positions in rails.py: Y-left X 245-265 and Y-right X 665-685 for Y 270-670. The stage lead leaves ST-01 at X 701, Y about 142, so it must run north to Y 270 before it reaches the Y-right slot.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Solder 22 AWG leads to the N20 tabs and pot them. Tie mounts on the AG-01 post (X 40-70) at Z 140 and Z 20. Route along the AG-01 bar and the Y-left rail slot under a slot cover to EL-02. No lead may hang below Z 140 within 125 mm of the turntable axis (175,370). Stage lead: from the ST-01 +X exit (X 701, Y about 142) along the table edge north to Y 270, then the Y-right slot, then the X-back slot, to EL-02. Carousel lead: from the TT-01 west window north to EL-02, taped down. Arm USB and barrel cables clipped in the X-back slot and run straight +Y, with a 100 mm service loop at each arm base, checked by a full pan sweep with no tension. Load-cell lead on the WS-01 underside with 2 tie mounts.

rebuttal.argument: I accept the port-selection correction. The CH340G has iSerial = 0, and CH340/CH343 bridges can share VID:PID 1A86:7523 or 1A86:55D3, so selecting by serial number or VID:PID cannot tell the devices apart. Mapping by hub port location plus an identity probe is the correct method. Opening the relay after 60 s idle removes the standby heat and drain concern whatever the measured idle current turns out to be.
rebuttal.final_requirement: Friday: measure the holding current of each servo at 8.4 V and record it in README 'Electrical' (d) and in the E-03 I_trip calibration. Hold for 30 min in the pocket; case and pocket wall must stay below 45 deg C. Firmware opens the relay after 60 s idle and re-arms via INIT. config.yaml maps devices by ListPortInfo.location on a labelled powered hub (A/B/MEGA). Startup identity probe: Mega answers 'OK <seq> WLB-MEGA v1'; each arm bus answers a Feetech ping on IDs 1-6 with homing offsets matching that arm's stored calibration; otherwise refuse to start. Demo laptop: USB selective suspend off, sleep and lid-close actions off on AC and battery, CH340/CH343 drivers installed before Thursday.

findings.title: Offline trajectories go past the SO-101 joint ranges, so they cannot be replayed on the real arms
findings.evidence: C:\Users\User\fusion_bridge\frames.json is the planner output that export_trajectories.py would cut up, per docs/software_architecture.md §3. I measured the joint spans across all 1707 frames. Arm A wrist_flex runs from -186 deg to +198 deg, a 384 deg span. The STS3215 is a single-turn 0-4095-tick servo (360 deg), so this is physically impossible. Arm B wrist_flex spans 320 deg (-143 to +177). Arm A pan spans 269 deg (-151 to +118), against a 220 deg pan range (about ±110 deg in so101_new_calib.urdf). Arm B wrist_roll reaches +188.3 deg during the water pour (frames 1208-1232). In plan3.py and planner.py the only joint bounds are IK/RRT sampling at |q| < 2.8 rad (±160 deg). pour() adds +100 deg to q[4] with no limit check, and nothing checks the 4095/0 tick wrap. A commanded path that crosses the wrap makes the servo turn about 360 deg the long way while it holds an open beaker of 12 % peroxide.
findings.required_change: Add per-joint limits to planner.py. Use the URDF limits mapped into the CAD zero frame minus a 5 deg margin, and enforce them in ik_grasp, grasp_solutions, rrt_connect (lo/hi per joint, not ±2.8 rad) and pour(). export_trajectories.py must convert every waypoint to raw ticks with each arm's own calibration and fail the export if any value falls outside [range_min+20, range_max-20] ticks or crosses the 0/4095 wrap. Re-plan the whole storyboard under these limits before anything is exported.

findings.title: Planned moves carry filled open beakers tilted and upside down, so they spill reagent in transit
findings.evidence: Arm A, frames.json frames 541-586: the measuring beaker holding 40 g of developer is carried through tilts of 97 deg to 180 deg (fully inverted) while its lip is 270-360 mm from the funnel axis and 100-200 mm below the funnel rim. Arm B, frames 1145-1170: the water beaker tilts 35-107 deg while its lip is 66-250 mm from the scale beaker and up to 84 mm below its rim.
