In total the held beaker is tilted more than 30 deg for 14.6 s (arm A) and 10.4 s (arm B), roughly twice the planned pour time. Peak held-beaker motion is 818 mm/s and 6.0 m/s^2 (0.62 g, frame 570). go(), line_pose() and rrt_connect() in plan3.py interpolate in joint space with no constraint on the held beaker's orientation. ik_grasp only forces the hinge to be vertical at the end poses.
findings.required_change: In the planner, every segment that carries liquid (any held beaker outside a declared pour segment) must keep the beaker axis within 10 deg of +Z at every 1.5 deg collision-check sample. Enforce this as a constraint in RRT edge_free and the go() fallbacks. Limit held-liquid segments to 250 mm/s and 1.5 m/s^2 at the beaker centre. export_trajectories.py must check tilt, speed and acceleration on every exported segment and refuse to export on any violation.

findings.title: The planned pour pose puts the stream 35 mm outside the measuring beaker
findings.evidence: Developer pour, frames 336-342, computed from the held-beaker transforms in frames.json. The 100 mL beaker's lowest rim point (the lip) is at about (502, 431, 156-171). The measuring beaker axis is at (468, 475) and its rim is at Z 124.7 (rim radius 21.5 mm). So the lip is 55-58 mm off-axis horizontally for every tilt from 50 to 100 deg, and the stream lands about 35 mm outside the receiver, on WS-02/WS-01 and the load-cell area. Cause: pour_pose() models the tilt as a rotation about the horizontal radial direction f through the grasp centre. The arm actually executes q[4] += 100 deg about the real wrist-roll axis, whose direction at the IK solution is not radial: the actual tilt direction is (0.65, -0.75), about 25 deg from the assumed (0.33, -0.94). That axis also passes about 9 mm from the 43 mm grasp centre (grip_frames.json gp + centre2d gives z 181.2 vs roll axis z 172.0). pour() never checks where the lip ends up. Also, the controller pours at tilts between 50 and 82 deg (see S-09), not only at 100 deg, and the lip moves as the tilt changes.
findings.required_change: Replace the single pour pose with an offline pour manifold q(θ), θ = 40..105 deg in 1 deg steps. Each pose is solved by real-FK IK so the lip stays within 8 mm horizontally of the receiver axis and 10-20 mm above its rim. Each step is collision-checked and exported as a 1-D lookup table. The pour controller commands θ and interpolates q(θ). Do the same for the funnel pours (lip within 30 mm of the funnel axis). Add an export assertion on lip-to-receiver distance for every θ.

findings.title: E-stop and SAFE_STOP keep a pour running, and a software exit drops the held beaker
findings.evidence: In software_architecture.md §4/§8, SAFE_STOP means the arms hold their current pose. During B_POUR_* the wrist is past θ_start, so holding the pose keeps pouring until the reagent beaker is empty. An operator can fill up to about 80 mL of 12 % H2O2 (README rack table), but the 50 mL measuring beaker on the scale holds about 74 mL to the brim. The excess overflows onto WS-02, the load cell and the HX711. Separately, LeRobot SO101FollowerConfig.disable_torque_on_disconnect defaults to True. Any exception path that calls disconnect() (a context manager, atexit) makes both arms go limp while one holds a beaker of peroxide. Pulling the barrel jacks (§8) does the same.
findings.required_change: Make SAFE_STOP depend on the state. If the wrist is within 10 deg of θ_start(fill) or beyond it, first untilt along the pour manifold (S-03) to θ_start - 25 deg in ≤0.3 s, then hold. Wrap main in try/finally and add SIGINT/SIGBREAK handlers that run the same untilt-then-hold. Set disable_torque_on_disconnect=False and never call disconnect() while a beaker is held. Add a unit test: inject an exception in mid-pour in the simulator and assert that tilt < θ_start within 0.5 s.

findings.title: A Mega reset slams the carousel and the stage to 1500 µs at full speed
findings.evidence: The Mega 2560 Pro (CH340) auto-resets when DTR is asserted. pyserial asserts DTR on open by default, so every host start or crash recovery reboots the Mega. After the bootloader, Servo.attach() immediately outputs its default 1500 µs. That moves the deck from, say, -67.5 deg (yeast pocket at the pick station, README servo table) to 0 deg, and the stage crank from +36.87 deg (WORK) to α = 0, at full servo speed. The tray then jumps about 90 mm carrying the flask of 12 % peroxide. §7 specifies S-curves for commanded moves only. Nothing covers boot, and the host has no position feedback (M45CHW) to know where things are.
findings.required_change: Firmware: keep the last commanded µs per servo in EEPROM (write it on move completion). Call writeMicroseconds(last) before attach(), and attach only after an explicit `INIT` from the host that the operator confirms. Print a boot banner `I BOOT <fw> <reset_cause>` so the host can detect an unexpected reset and latch a fault. Host: open the port with DTR/RTS deasserted (construct an unopened serial.Serial, set dtr=False and rts=False, then open()). Fit a 10 µF RESET-GND capacitor after flashing as a backup.

findings.title: No valid trajectory set exists for the hardware being built, and the repo cannot regenerate one
findings.evidence: frames.json is dated 02:21. It predates gripper_design.json (02:59), the fin-ray meshes.json (03:43, data['finray']) and plan3.py (03:49), and plan3.log is 0 bytes. So the only trajectories were checked against the stock jaws, not GR-01/02/03. Their gripper values contradict the README table: arm A holds the 43 mm beaker at -71.0 deg (README says command -64 and never past -70), and arm B holds the 56 mm water beaker at -60.0 deg (frames 1202-1238; README says -51). The planner continues after failures: go() logs 'WARN no collision-free path' and plays the colliding move anyway, and pour() continues after 'WARN pour tilt touches'. The final audit checks only every 2nd frame at 12 fps, with joint steps up to 19.2 deg per frame, so up to 38 deg goes unchecked between samples. planner.py, plan3.py, kin.json, meshes.json (77 MB) and gripper_design.json are not in the wlb repo, so teammates at the venue cannot re-plan after fixing S-01 to S-03 or after re-teaching.
findings.required_change: export_trajectories.py must: (a) abort if the planner LOG contains any WARN; (b) re-audit every exported segment at ≤1 deg joint steps against the fin-ray meshes; (c) stamp each trajectory with the SHA-256 of meshes.json, plan3.py and kin.json, and have player.py refuse a mismatch; (d) strip gripper values from the trajectories, since the gripper is commanded from the README table. Commit the planner and its inputs to software/tools/ before Thursday's flight, with meshes.json either as a compressed .npz or under Git LFS.

findings.title: The cut-off law double-counts in-flight mass and ignores the untilt tail
findings.evidence: §5.1/§5.4 cut off when m_f + q·(T_air + 0.1 s) ≥ target - 0.3 g, with T_air ≈ 0.25 s. But while flowing, the scale already reads the stream's momentum force q·v/g. With v = √(2gh) ≈ 1.2 m/s for the roughly 75 mm fall from lip to liquid surface in the frames-336 geometry, that is q·0.12 s, which equals the mass in flight (the classic hourglass result). Adding q·T_air therefore cuts early by q·0.25 s: 2.0 g at 8 g/s, 0.25 g at 1 g/s. Meanwhile the real overshoot sources are not modelled: flow that continues during the 25 deg snap-back (about 0.1 s at STS3215 speed) and lip drainage. The filter lag term is right: I simulated a 0.12 s lag of m_f behind a 5 g/s ramp.
findings.required_change: Remove T_air. Use the cut law m_f ≥ target - (a + b·q̂), with a and b fitted by least squares from at least 10 logged water pours on Friday at q = 1-8 g/s. Starting values: a = 0.3 g, b = 0.15 s. Log the final settled error of every pour and refit after the first live run. Add stream momentum to the simulator (S-27).

findings.title: PI on flow cannot follow the falling liquid level without tilt feed-forward
findings.evidence: I modelled the 100 mL beaker as a tilted cylinder (Ø52 × 72 mm inner). The tilt at which liquid reaches the lip is 53 deg at 80 mL, 60 deg at 60 mL, 65 deg at 46 mL, 70 deg at 33 mL and 80 deg at 12 mL, so dθ/dV is 0.34-0.67 deg/mL. Holding 5 g/s therefore needs the tilt to advance 1.6-3.2 deg/s. Estimated plant gain dq/dθ is about 3-5 g/s per deg (weir flow ∝ head^1.5-2, head about 2-3 mm at 5 g/s). Loop delay is about 0.38 s (servo 0.1 + fall 0.12 + filters 0.14 + host 0.02). With 60 deg phase margin, an integral gain Ki·K ≤ 1.4 rad/s gives Ki ≤ about 0.35 deg/s per g/s. A type-1 loop then has a ramp-following error of rate/Ki, about 4.6-9 g/s: the PI alone would starve the flow and then overshoot when it catches up. The gain also drops to 0 below θ_start, so integrator windup during the ramp-to-first-drop is guaranteed.
findings.required_change: Command the tilt as θ = θ_ff + θ_PI. Feed-forward: dθ_ff/dt = (dθ/dV)(V_remaining)·q̂/ρ from the tilted-cylinder table, with V_remaining = V_first_flow - m_f/ρ. Starting PI gains: Kp = 0.15 deg per g/s, Ki = 0.3 deg/s per g/s, with conditional-integration anti-windup, the integrator reset to 0 at first-drop detection, and tilt rate clamped to 10 deg/s. Validate in the simulator (S-27) against flows of 1-8 g/s and fills of 46-80 mL before Friday.

findings.title: Reagent fill level is never measured, so θ_start(fill) and the PRECHECK quantity test have no input
findings.evidence: §5.2 takes the fill as 'beaker weight before pickup - tare of the empty beaker', and §4 PRECHECK requires each reagent beaker to hold at least recipe + 20 %. The 100 mL reagent beakers go rack → pour → rack and are never on the scale. The WS-02 locator ring is Ø46 and cannot seat a Ø56 beaker. The fill can be anything from 46 mL to the brim (README: 'any amount, up to about 80 mL'), which gives θ_start anywhere from about 37 deg to 65 deg. The 'one pour at each of 3 fill levels' lookup in §5.2 has no fill value to look up.
findings.required_change: Infer the fill from the tilt at first flow using the geometric table (V(θ) at 53/60/65/70 deg = 80/60/46/33 mL), corrected by one empirical offset measured Friday with water. Ramp from a fixed safe start of 40 deg at 3 deg/s, not θ_start - 8 deg. Replace the PRECHECK quantity test with a check after first flow: if θ_first > θ(1.2 × recipe volume) (65 deg for developer, 69 deg for 30 g of water), untilt and PAUSE('refill <reagent>').

findings.title: Flow estimate and first-drop detection are noise-limited, and the HX711 rate is assumed, not checked
findings.evidence: I simulated the specified pipeline (80 Hz, 4-sample median, τ = 0.1 s low-pass, finite-difference q). At σ_m = 0.05 g it gives σ_q = 0.23 g/s, and 0.47 g/s at σ_m = 0.10 g. The 0.5 g/s first-drop threshold in §5.2 is therefore 1-2σ and will false-trigger within about a second. A 0.5 s linear-regression slope gives σ_q = 0.058 g/s. Separately, most HX711 breakouts tie RATE to GND (10 SPS). At 10 SPS the 4-sample median spans 0.4 s and the loop delay roughly doubles. WS-01 also bolts to the same X-front rail as both arm bases (scale X 395-512 between the arm bases), so arm B's wrist motion during the pour couples straight into the load cell.
findings.required_change: Compute q̂ as a 0.5 s rolling least-squares slope on Mega timestamps, with an outlier gate of 5σ. Declare first drop when q̂ > 0.5 g/s for 3 consecutive samples and m_f has risen by more than 0.3 g. Firmware must measure its sample interval and report it in the banner; the host refuses pours if the rate is below 70 Hz (electrical: RATE pin to DVDD). On Friday, measure σ_m with arm B at the pour pose, still and moving at 10 deg/s. If it exceeds 0.1 g, lengthen the regression window to 0.8 s and lower the q* ceiling to 5 g/s.

findings.title: Grasp-miss detection cannot fire, and the gripper load thresholds conflict with LeRobot's gripper configuration
findings.evidence: §3: command -64 deg (contact -60 + 4 deg squeeze), and declare a miss if the jaw reaches ≤ -68 deg. A position servo stops at its goal, so a miss reads -64 deg and is classified as a grasp. A real grasp also reads -62 to -64 deg because the TPU fin-ray deforms. §8 allows gripper load up to 85 %, but LeRobot so101_follower.configure() writes Max_Torque_Limit = 500 (50 %), Protection_Current = 250 and Overload_Torque = 25 to the gripper. Present_Load can therefore never reach 85 %, and an overload trip drops the grip to 25 % torque mid-pour with the beaker at up to 100 deg tilt.
findings.required_change: Classify after the close settles (0.3 s). Grasp: Present_Load ≥ L_grip (measure Friday; expect 15-35 %) and position ≥ -63.0 deg. Miss: position ≤ -63.5 deg and load < 8 %. Cross-check every pick or place at the scale against the scale itself (Δm = beaker + contents ± 2 g). Read the STS3215 status register every 0.5 s and fault on the overload or overheat bit. Friday test: hold the 100 mL beaker with 90 g at 100 deg tilt for 30 s with no overload bit; set the squeeze from that test, not from the 4 deg default.

findings.title: A 5 deg approach opening leaves almost no clearance on the fixed finger
findings.evidence: Only the moving jaw opens. The 43 mm contact centre is about 67 mm from the hinge (gripper_design.json centre2d (65.5, 14.5)), so opening 5 deg past contact (README '-55 deg', plan3 OPEN = contact + 5) gives a 5.8 mm gap, all on the moving side. The fixed finger sits on its contact line with 0 mm clearance, so any positioning error toward it puts the TPU finger on the beaker rim during the straight-down approach. gripper_design.json q_open is -46 / -33.3 deg (14 deg), which contradicts the README and plan3 value of 5 deg. WS-02 and TT-04 locate the 43 mm beaker in Ø46 pockets, which is ±1.5 mm at placement.
findings.required_change: Aim the approach 2.9 mm toward the moving jaw. Open 12 deg (about 14 mm gap) at the scale, rack and funnel, and 5 deg only at the carousel where neighbouring beakers limit it. Re-plan with these values and keep one value set in config.yaml. Friday acceptance: 20 consecutive picks per station with no rim strike, and a repeatability of ±1.5 mm or better at the grasp centre.

findings.title: Calibration and teach plan break the collision guarantee, needs fixtures nobody has, and ignores LeRobot's normalisation
findings.evidence: §3 says 'record ticks at three known CAD poses', but there is no jig to put a real arm in a CAD pose, and eyeballing to ±3 deg means about 13 mm at 250 mm reach. LeRobot's SO-101 default is use_degrees=False, so body joints come back as RANGE_M100_100 (percent of each arm's recorded range) and the gripper as RANGE_0_100 recorded with the stock jaws. That is not degrees. The correction bounds are inconsistent: 8 deg at the shoulder is about 35 mm at the tool versus the 15 mm limit, and both exceed the planner's clearance (2.5 mm voxels, scene dilated 1 voxel). Blending the last 60 mm in joint space also curves the straight-down approach that the fin-ray V needs. Keyboard jogging 6 joints at about 8 stations on 2 arms will take hours.
findings.required_change: Bypass LeRobot normalisation and use raw ticks: q_cad = s_j·(tick - tick0_j)·2π/4096, so only sign and offset are unknown. Teach by hand-guiding with torque off: touch 2 reference features per arm for tick0, then record the 6 fixture positions (scale, funnel, carousel pick, 3 rack pockets) as Cartesian points. teach.py then updates the world model, re-runs the planner and the S-06 audit (minutes), and refuses any fixture more than 10 mm from CAD ('re-clamp'). No runtime blending.

findings.title: Arm-to-arm safety relies on zone locks, but the plan was only checked against the other arm's planned pose
findings.evidence: In plan3.py each move is collision-checked against W.other_grid(t), the other arm frozen at its planned pose at that moment. In frames.json the two arms never move at the same time (0 frames with both moving). §3's zone mutex (scale/funnel/carousel/rack) is a coarser and different guarantee. After a fault, a retry, or a hold elsewhere, the other arm is no longer where the plan assumed.
findings.required_change: Execute strictly one moving arm at a time. Before each segment starts, verify that the idle arm's Present_Position is within 2 deg on every joint of the pose it had in the plan for that segment; otherwise fault. Keep the zone locks only as a second check.

findings.title: The eruption starts at WORK under arm A before the stage moves out
findings.evidence: In plan3.py to_flask() the yeast is poured (tilt 1.2 s, dwell 2.4 s, untilt 1.0 s), then the beaker is placed back on the scale (about 4.9 s), the arm goes home (2 s), there is a 1 s camera move, and only then does the stage run its 3 s move (crank 0 → 73.74 deg). That is about 12.5 s from catalyst contact to stage start, with the flask and funnel at (450, 282) next to arm A and the scale. 12 % H2O2 with yeast foams within seconds. The §4 state order (A_YEAST_TO_FLASK → STAGE_OUT) is the same.
findings.required_change: Start STAGE_OUT no more than 1.5 s after arm A's untilt, once the gripper is above Z 300 and outside the funnel zone. Place P2 on the scale only after the stage reaches ERUPT. Measure foam onset time in Friday's first live run and encode it as a hard deadline in the state machine: fault-and-stage-out if it is exceeded.

findings.title: No e-stop independent of software, and no handling for arm power loss
findings.evidence: §8: 'A hardware e-stop isn't feasible on borrowed arms.' The only stops are the spacebar (needs terminal focus and a live Python process) and pulling the barrel jacks, which makes the arms limp so they collapse with the beaker. Nothing removes LiPo power from the M45CHWs or the auger if the host or Mega hangs. README notes the 2 A supply browns out and resets the servos, and the software has no voltage monitoring for the arms.
findings.required_change: Add a latching NC mushroom e-stop (no modification to the arms). Contact 1 is in series with LiPo+ to the servo bus and TB6612 VM, which stops the carousel, stage and auger in hardware. Contact 2 goes to a Mega input (D2, INT0, pull-up), and the firmware reports `F ESTOP`. The host then runs the S-04 untilt-and-hold on the arms. Add an inline barrel-jack switch per arm as the last resort, with a note that it drops the arm. Read Present_Voltage every 0.5 s and fault below 6.0 V (7.4 V motor variant) or 10.5 V (12 V variant). After any bus error, mark the arm state UNKNOWN and require operator recovery.

findings.title: Firmware: the HX711 read disables interrupts and jitters the servos, and a blocking read can leave the auger running
findings.evidence: The common bogde/HX711 library calls noInterrupts() around the whole 24-bit read on AVR, about 250 µs with digitalWrite/digitalRead at roughly 10 µs per bit. At 80 Hz that blocks 2.2 % of the time. Servo-library pulse ends (Timer5 ISR) that land in a blocked window are stretched by up to about 250 µs, which is about 34 deg at the 7.4 µs/deg of a 270 deg unit: about one twitch per second per servo, carrying open beakers and the peroxide flask. Separately, wait_ready() blocks forever if the HX711 disconnects, while analogWrite PWM on D11 (Timer1 hardware) keeps the auger running with nothing to stop it.
findings.required_change: Use a non-blocking HX711 read (poll is_ready()) that disables interrupts only around each SCK-high pulse (under 2 µs), or move the servos to Timer5 hardware PWM (D45/D46, OCR5B/OCR5A, 0.5 µs resolution). Enable the AVR watchdog with wdt_enable(WDTO_250MS). Put a 10 kΩ pull-down on TB6612 STBY (D24) and drive STBY low as the first instruction in setup(). Bench test: a 10-minute scope capture of D9/D10 pulse width while streaming at 80 Hz, with maximum deviation under 5 µs.

findings.title: Motion limits are not enforced in firmware and are given in degrees while the servo type (180 vs 270) is unknown
findings.evidence: README items 9 and 'Stage': soft-limit the crank to ±40 deg (stops at ±45 deg; the stop post is the load-case weak link at SF 3.0) and the carousel to servo 20-160 deg. The servo may be the 180 deg or 270 deg unit. A limit computed with the wrong µs/deg (7.4 vs 11.1) turns '40 deg' into 60 deg and stalls the crank on the stop posts. §7 does not say whether the Mega checks TT/ST arguments, durations or S-curve minimums ('≥2 s per 45 deg'), so one bad host value moves hardware.
findings.required_change: Store limits in Mega EEPROM as µs, written by calibrate tooling from the slow no-linkage sweep: carousel min/max µs, crank min/max µs (±40 deg measured), and minimum ms per 100 µs of travel. The firmware rejects any TT/ST/AUG outside them with `ERR <seq> RANGE` and never clamps silently. The host keeps its own copy of the limits, but the firmware check is authoritative.

findings.title: Mega protocol is underspecified: framing, acknowledgement semantics, watchdog latch and baud error
findings.evidence: §7 has ASCII lines with no checksum. 115200 baud on a 16 MHz AVR has +2.1 % error (UBRR = 16 gives 117 647). 'OK <seq>' does not say whether it means accepted or completed (a TT S-curve takes 2-4 s). Behaviour when a TT/ST arrives during a move is undefined. There are no messages for scale calibration factor, limits, init, version or battery voltage (§8 needs the A0 reading). The heartbeat rate is unspecified. Watchdog recovery is unspecified: is it latched, and does the auger resume?
findings.required_change: Run at 250 000 baud (0 % error). Frame as `<seq> <CMD> <args> *<CRC8>\n` and reply `ERR <seq> CRC` on mismatch. Reply `ACK <seq>` on acceptance and `DONE <seq>` on completion. Reject TT/ST during a move with `ERR <seq> BUSY` (no preemption except STOP). Add INIT, CAL <counts_per_g>, LIM ..., VER, CLR, plus unsolicited `V <mV>` at 2 Hz and `I <fw> <hx_rate_hz>` at boot. HB every 100 ms from the control tick, not from an independent timer, so a hung controller stops heartbeats. On a 500 ms watchdog trip, emit `F WDT` latched until CLR; an interrupted AUG is reported as `F WDT AUG <revs_done>` and is never resumed automatically.

findings.title: A single asyncio loop with blocking LeRobot calls cannot meet the timing budget
findings.evidence: FeetechMotorsBus sync_read/sync_write are blocking pyserial calls, about 3-5 ms each (§10's own figure). One tick needs, per arm, a position read, a load read and a goal write. Run inside coroutines on one loop, that is about 15-25 ms during which the Mega reader, the pour controller and the UI cannot run. On Windows, asyncio sleep granularity is about 15.6 ms. The rich Live dashboard redraw and per-sample CSV/JSONL writes (§2, §9.3) also run on the same loop. This answers §10's open question: no.
findings.required_change: Use one OS thread per serial port (arm A, arm B, Mega), talking to the asyncio orchestrator through queue.Queue / loop.call_soon_threadsafe. Arm threads run at 50 Hz with a position read every tick and a load/status read every 4th tick. The pour controller is triggered by each Mega W sample (80 Hz) and uses Mega millis for dt. Logging goes through a writer thread with a bounded queue. Document the budget: pour compute ≤ 2 ms, arm command latency ≤ 20 ms at the 95th percentile, and log every tick overrun.

findings.title: Arm identity is not checked at connect, so serial ports can swap and torque-enable can snap the arm
findings.evidence: Both Waveshare boards present servos with IDs 1-6, and the Mega is a third USB-serial device. COM/tty numbering can change between boots or hubs, and config.yaml maps ports by name, so arm A could run arm B's trajectories. Also, while powered, the STS3215 keeps its last Goal_Position. If the arm was hand-guided during teach or went limp, Torque_Enable = 1 makes it jump to that stale goal at full speed.
findings.required_change: At connect, read the 6 Homing_Offset EEPROM values per bus and compare them with the stored fingerprint for arm A and arm B. Refuse to enable torque on a mismatch, and identify the Mega by its `I` banner. Before every Torque_Enable = 1, write Goal_Position = Present_Position on all 6 servos. The player clamps each write to ≤5 deg from present (LeRobot max_relative_target).

findings.title: State machine: soap state missing, no pause/resume or reset, no recovery paths, tare scheme cannot work
findings.evidence: The §4 state chain has no soap pour. The §4 note pours soap into the measuring beaker, README step 2 uses a fresh beaker, README 'Running the reaction' adds 15 mL by hand, and plan3.py has no soap move at all. README promises a 'refill developer' pause, but §4 only has SAFE_STOP. The retries and corrections (grasp retry, scale → carousel for the yeast top-up, retreating from mid-segment) have no planned or checked trajectories. There is no RESET: after DONE, P2 is on the scale and the stage is at ERUPT, so the next PRECHECK fails. No timeouts are given as numbers. VERIFY_YEAST uses tare(empty P2), which is never measured, while TARE on the Mega zeroes the scale with P1 on it. The water target is a fixed 37.0 g rather than the actual yeast mass + 30 g.
findings.required_change: Settle §10's open question: soap is pre-loaded by hand in the flask. Dish soap's viscous, stringy flow and a tail lasting many seconds invalidate the pour model and the 1 s drip hold. Add PAUSE(reason) with resume-at-state, and a RESET sequence: stage to WORK, P2 back to the carousel, operator checklist. Make the universal recovery primitive 'retreat = reverse replay of the executed prefix of the current segment' (the only path known to be collision-free) and plan scale→carousel explicitly. Give every state a numeric timeout (e.g. pour 45 s, grasp 5 s, carousel = duration + 2 s, settle 5 s). Do all taring on the host: the Mega reports gross grams against an empty-pan zero taken at PRECHECK, each beaker's empty mass is recorded the first time it is placed, and all targets are relative (water = m_yeast_actual + 30.0 g).

findings.title: Open-loop auger dosing cannot meet ±0.3 g, and several planned checks are physically impossible
findings.evidence: Revolutions are counted from time × rpm at 100 % PWM (§6). That puts 8.4 V on a 6 V N20, while README says about 70 %. With a fixed duty, rpm falls about 17 % from 8.4 V to 7.0 V, roughly 1.2 g on a 7 g dose. Geometry from aug2.py (Ø13 bore, Ø5.2 hub, 16 mm pitch, two 2 mm flights) gives about 1.55 mL swept per rev, or roughly 0.28-0.42 g/rev at 0.6 g/mL bulk density and 30-45 % fill. So one rev already exceeds ±0.3 g, and §6's ceil(short/g_per_rev) correction overshoots by up to a full rev. The PRECHECK 'first revolution ≥ 0.2 g' and README's 'full speed until 1.5 g short' both need a live weight under the auger, which is not over the scale. README's 'reverse 0.3 s if it stalls' needs stall sensing, but the TB6612 has no current sense and there is no encoder.
findings.required_change: Settle §10's open question: buy the encoder N20 now (7 PPR, encoder on D18/D19 interrupts) and make the A0 battery divider mandatory. Set duty = min(1, 6.0 V / V_batt). Dose the first pass to 85 % of target, verify on the scale, then top up with round((target - m)/g_per_rev, 0.1) revs counted on the encoder. Stall means no encoder edges for 200 ms, then reverse 0.25 rev. Delete the hopper test from PRECHECK and fault 'hopper empty' when 10 revs add less than 1 g. Relax the yeast tolerance to ±0.7 g (see S-29).

findings.title: The 'flask detected' interlock is not a sensor, and SAFE_STOP's 'stage home' contradicts the watchdog
findings.evidence: §8 says 'flask collar is detected (stage servo at its WORK angle)', but the M45CHW has no feedback, so this is only the last commanded value. The interlock also sits on the B_POUR_* states, which pour onto the scale. The states that actually pour into the flask are A_DEV_TO_FLASK and A_YEAST_TO_FLASK. The §4 SAFE_STOP 'stage home' conflicts with §7's watchdog 'holds servos'. Home (α = 0, 1500 µs) is mid-travel, about 90 mm toward the audience with the flask.
findings.required_change: Put the interlock on A_*_TO_FLASK. Detect the flask with a microswitch in the ST-05 socket on a Mega input, or require an explicit operator confirmation per run. Define SAFE_STOP for the stage as hold (no motion) everywhere, and make the stage move only on an explicit operator command.

findings.title: Plan, simulator and schedule cannot deliver a tuned closed-loop system in Friday's window
findings.evidence: §2 says everything is 'to be written Friday'. Friday 9 AM-4 PM ET also covers mechanical assembly, teach, scale and auger calibration, and the water and chemical runs (README). The §9.1 simulator q = k·max(0, θ - θ_start) has no level dependence (θ moves 13-29 deg per pour, S-08), no transport delay, no stream momentum (S-07), no HX711 noise, rate or median (S-10), and no servo rate limit, so controller code that passes these tests proves little. The scope also includes a web page for the judges.
findings.required_change: Before the Thursday flight, write and commit firmware, MegaLink, the trajectory exporter fixes (S-01 to S-06) and a pour simulator that includes the tilted-cylinder volume model, weir flow q = C·h^1.5, 0.12 s fall delay, momentum force, σ_m = 0.05 g at 80 Hz, the production filter chain and a 270 deg/s tilt-rate limit. Add a STEP mode (Enter advances each state) for bring-up. Add a DEGRADED pour mode: ramp to the S-09 fill-derived angle, timed pulses, scale verification, ±2 g. Cut the web page. Friday order: Mega bring-up → scale calibration → one arm teach + dry replay with empty beakers at 30 % speed → water pours (log and refit S-07) → full water run → chemicals.

findings.title: Top-up pulses and the snap-back excite slosh and make overshoot more likely
findings.evidence: §5.5: tilt back to the last flow angle for 150 ms after a 25 deg full-speed snap-back. The stream needs at least the 0.38 s loop delay to re-form, so a 150 ms pulse yields between 0 and several grams. The first slosh mode in a Ø52 beaker is about 4.2 Hz (ω = √(1.841·g/R)), which a 25 deg snap at about 270 deg/s excites. §5.7's 'hold at -10 deg from the cut angle' means re-tilting 15 deg forward after the snap.
findings.required_change: Untilt at most 60 deg/s by 15 deg. For a top-up, ramp to θ_cut - 3 deg, then step +0.5 deg every 0.6 s, stopping when q̂ > 0.3 g/s or m_f reaches the cut law. Hold the drip at θ_cut - 15 deg for 1.5 s. Count pulses and fault after 6.

findings.title: Servo load guard thresholds are arbitrary and miss light collisions
findings.evidence: §8 sets >70 % load for 0.5 s on any joint. With a full 100 mL beaker at reach and fast moves, the shoulder of the 7.4 V variant can exceed this in normal operation, while a finger striking a 50 g beaker never reaches it. guard.py lists 'joint error' with no number.
findings.required_change: Set per-joint load thresholds from Friday's logged water runs (99.9th percentile + 15 %). Add a tracking-error guard: |goal - present| > 4 deg for more than 0.3 s on any body joint triggers a retreat (S-22).

findings.title: Documentation disagrees with itself; config needs a single source of truth
findings.evidence: README run step 1 says arm B carries the measuring beaker to the funnel; §4 and plan3.py say arm A. README's pour section says 'wrist-flex steps'; §5 and plan3 (q[4]) say wrist-roll. The README rack table lists 4 pockets at Y 392/456/520/584, but RK-02 has 3 pockets at (670,414), (717,495) and (707,587). README uses serial commands `C2`/`S1` versus §7's TT/ST, and 'step a few µs every 10 ms' versus §7's 20 ms smoothstep. README says the animation is about 98 s; frames.json is 142 s. The recipe is 50-75 mL developer + 15 mL soap (README) versus 40 g + 10 g (§1). README has two contradictory gripper sections: the stock jaw at +20 to +40 deg and the fin-ray at -60 deg.
findings.required_change: Generate config.yaml (fixture XYZ, pocket angles, gripper angles, recipe) from design_data.json and gripper_design.json with a script. Make the README and §1-§8 refer to config.yaml, and delete the stale stock-jaw gripper section.

findings.title: Tolerances are far tighter than the chemistry needs and force slow correction loops
findings.evidence: §5.6 sets developer ±1.0 g, water ±0.5 g and yeast ±0.3 g. Elephant toothpaste tolerates ±20 %. Each yeast correction costs about 25-30 s: back to the carousel, +135 deg in 4 s, dose, -135 deg in 4 s, pick and place. A realistic run (closed-loop pours about 15-22 s each, auger 30-40 s, the 60 s WAIT_ACTIVATE) is about 4.5-5 min, compared with 142 s in the plan.
findings.required_change: Demo tolerances: developer ±2 g, water ±2 g, yeast ±0.7 g, with actual values shown on the dashboard. Keep the tight values as a stretch goal behind a config flag.

findings.title: Logging, calibration and platform details are missing
findings.evidence: §9.3 logs states and grams only. There is no raw HX711 count (needed to recalibrate afterwards), no config, trajectory or calibration hash, no servo status register, and no host-clock-to-Mega-clock pairing. The scale calibration mass is unspecified. The OS is unspecified: spacebar e-stop needs terminal focus, COM vs /dev/tty naming differs, and Windows USB selective suspend can drop CH340 devices. §8 gates moves at 7.0 V, but a 2S pack sags 0.3-0.5 V while the servos move.
findings.required_change: Log raw counts, grams, Mega millis and host monotonic time per sample, plus per-run SHA-256 of config.yaml, the trajectories and the calibration. Use a bounded writer queue and flush on fault. Calibrate the scale with 20 US nickels (5.000 g each, 100.0 g). Pin the OS (Ubuntu 22.04 recommended for LeRobot), disable USB selective suspend, and use a global key hook as well as the UI button. Gate on resting LiPo voltage ≥ 7.2 V before a move and fault only if the voltage under load stays below 6.6 V for more than 1 s.

defense.argument: Verified against C:\Users\User\fusion_bridge\frames.json (1707 frames, 12 fps, 142.25 s). Span of each joint in CAD-zero degrees: arm A [269.0, 192.9, 134.7, 384.0, 122.7, 18.0], arm B [188.2, 145.0, 106.9, 319.6, 280.2, 17.0]. Arm A wrist_flex (q[3]) runs -185.9 to +198.1 and arm B wrist_roll (q[4]) peaks at +188.3 at frame 1207. These numbers do not depend on where the offset sits: a 384 deg span cannot fit on a 4096-tick single-turn STS3215, and the SO-101 wrist_flex link hits itself long before ±180. The only bound in plan3.py is the hard-coded |q[:5]| < 2.8 rad, in grasp_solutions line 74, make_ready line 155 and rrt_connect `lo, hi = -2.8, 2.8` line 92. pour() does `qt[4] += sign*radians(100)` with no check. The planner was meant to be the collision-checked source of truth, and as written it is not a valid one. I concede the finding fully.
defense.proposed_change: Change §3 of docs/software_architecture.md to add a 'Joint limits' paragraph. (1) planner.py gets JOINT_LIMITS[arm][j] = (lo, hi) in the CAD zero frame. Derive it from so101_new_calib.urdf <limit>, shifted by each arm's CAD-to-URDF zero offset and shrunk by 5 deg on each side. Do not merge the two arms' limits, because each arm's calibration differs. (2) ik_grasp clamps q into [lo, hi] after every Gauss-Newton step and rejects the solution if it is clamped at convergence. grasp_solutions and make_ready replace the ±2.8 test with the per-joint test. rrt_connect samples uniform(lo, hi) per joint. edge_free rejects any interpolated sample that is out of range. pour() checks qt and every 1.5 deg sample between qp and qt. (3) export_trajectories.py converts every waypoint to raw ticks: tick = tick0_j + s_j*q*4096/(2π) (S-13). It fails the export, with joint, segment and frame index, if any tick lies outside [range_min_j+20, range_max_j-20] from that arm's LeRobot calibration JSON, or if consecutive waypoints differ by more than 2048 ticks (wrap crossing). (4) The whole storyboard is re-planned under these limits. The current frames.json is declared invalid in the doc: 'no trajectory exported before the limits commit is flown'.

defense.argument: Verified, and the root cause is worse than reported. Arm A, frames 551-599: the measuring beaker 'M' still shows liquid level liq5 (40 g developer) while its tilt goes 10 → 97 → 117 → 157 → 178.5 deg. Its lowest rim point drops to Z 23-34 mm at frames 563-566 and swings round behind the arm base at (318, 525), 270-363 mm from the funnel axis. Arm B, frames 1146-1173: the water beaker tilts 43-109 deg in transit. Root cause 1: grasp_solutions() tries hinge_sign in (1, -1). For a beaker that is already held, hs = -1 is the gripper flipped about the vertical, so it is a solution with the beaker upside down. The funnel 'pre-pour' pose at frame 584-587 really is inverted (175.6-178.5 deg), and the '+100 deg pour' then rolls it back to 80 deg (frames 600-628). So the funnel pour as planned is an inversion followed by a partial un-roll. Root cause 2: go(), line_pose() and the RRT interpolate in joint space and never constrain the held beaker's orientation. ik_grasp only forces the hinge to be vertical at the end poses.
defense.proposed_change: Change §3 of docs/software_architecture.md to add 'Carrying liquid'. (1) While W.held[t] is not None, grasp_solutions and line_pose use only the hinge_sign that was recorded at grasp time. hs = -1 is never allowed for a held beaker. (2) free()/edge_free() take an upright_tol argument. Any held beaker outside a declared pour segment must keep its axis (M[:3,2]) within 10 deg of +Z at every 1.5 deg sample, and the same predicate gates the go() fallbacks (direct, lifted, rest) and RRT extend. RRT samples for a held beaker are drawn from the 4-DoF upright submanifold (project each sample with ik_grasp's orientation residual) so the planner does not stall. (3) Time-parameterise held-liquid segments to beaker-centre speed ≤ 250 mm/s and acceleration ≤ 1.5 m/s^2, computed by finite differences on FK at export resolution. (4) export_trajectories.py recomputes tilt, speed and acceleration for every exported segment and refuses export on any violation, naming the segment and frame. (5) Add a test in tests/test_export.py that feeds frames 541-599 of the current frames.json and asserts the exporter rejects it.

defense.argument: Verified from the b100 transforms in frames.json. During the developer pour (frames 333-349) the lowest rim point of the 100 mL beaker is at (501-504, 429-432, 156-183). That is 53.7-58.2 mm horizontally from the measuring-beaker axis (468, 475). The receiver rim radius is 21.5 mm, so the lip is 32-37 mm outside the rim at every tilt from 30 to 100 deg. pour_pose() aims the lip 12 mm above the receiver axis, so the design intent was right. The model it uses, a rotation about the horizontal radial direction f through the grasp centre, is not the motion the arm executes (q[4] += 100 deg about the real wrist-roll axis). pour() never checks where the lip ends up. A closed-loop pour also dwells at whatever tilt between θ_first and about 100 deg the controller is using, so one checked pose is not enough.
defense.proposed_change: Rewrite §5 of docs/software_architecture.md around a 'pour manifold'. (1) For each pour (B to scale for developer and water, A to funnel for developer and catalyst), the planner solves q(θ) for θ = 40..105 deg in 1 deg steps. It uses real-FK IK with the residual [lip_xy - receiver_axis_xy (target ≤ 8 mm for the scale, ≤ 30 mm for the funnel), lip_z - (rim_z + 15) (band 10-20 mm), beaker axis tilt - θ in the vertical plane through the receiver]. Each step is warm-started from the previous one so the manifold is continuous, every Δq between steps is ≤ 2 deg per joint, and every step is collision-checked including the S-01 joint limits. (2) Export it as trajectories/<pour>_manifold.json, a 1-D table θ → q[0..4]. The pour controller commands θ only, and player.py interpolates q(θ) linearly. (3) The export asserts lip-to-receiver horizontal distance and lip height at every θ and fails otherwise. (4) The approach segment ends at q(40 deg) with the beaker upright-constrained (S-02) up to the pre-pour pose q(0) on the same manifold branch.

defense.argument: Correct on both counts. Holding the pose during a pour keeps the weir flowing. The 50 mL measuring beaker's brim volume (about 74 mL) is below an 80 mL reagent fill, so a held pose overflows onto WS-02/HX711. I confirmed in the installed LeRobot 0.6.0 (lerobot/robots/so_follower/config_so_follower.py line 31) that disable_torque_on_disconnect defaults to True, and so_follower.disconnect() passes it straight to bus.disconnect(). A plain `with` block or an exception path therefore drops the beaker. §8's 'pull the barrel jacks' has the same effect. One refinement: the emergency untilt should run at full servo speed for the first 25 deg. Stopping the flow matters more than the slosh concern in S-26, which applies to normal cut-off.
defense.proposed_change: In §4/§8 of docs/software_architecture.md, define SAFE_STOP per state. (a) Arm in a pour segment with θ ≥ θ_first - 10 deg: command θ_target = max(40 deg, θ_first - 25 deg) along the pour manifold (S-03) at full speed (about 75 deg in ≤ 0.3 s at about 270 deg/s), then hold torque. (b) Arm carrying a beaker: decelerate to stop along the current segment within 0.2 s and hold. (c) Otherwise hold. Mega STOP is sent in parallel. Implementation rules: main() is wrapped in try/finally. SIGINT and SIGBREAK (Windows) handlers and an atexit hook all call safety.safe_stop(). ArmDriver never uses SO101Follower.disconnect(). It calls bus.disconnect(disable_torque=False) and only from the RESET state with both grippers open and empty. Remove 'pull the barrel jacks' from the stop list. It becomes a last resort, with the warning that it drops the beaker (see S-16). Add tests/test_safe_stop.py: in the simulator, raise an exception at t = 2 s into B_POUR_DEV with θ = θ_first + 8 deg, and assert θ < θ_first within 0.5 s and torque still enabled.

defense.argument: Correct. On the Mega 2560 Pro, CH340 DTR is AC-coupled through 100 nF to RESET. pyserial asserts DTR on open by default. Servo objects initialise ticks to DEFAULT_PULSE_WIDTH = 1500 µs, so the first pulse after attach() slews the deck from station 2 (1333 µs on the 270 deg unit) or the crank from WORK (1500 ± 273 µs) to centre at full speed. The M45CHW gives no feedback, so the host cannot know this happened. One limitation: the 10 µF RESET-GND capacitor stops auto-reset but also stops IDE uploads, so it must be fitted after the final flash and noted in the bring-up checklist. On Linux the DTR glitch on open happens even with dtr=False unless HUPCL is cleared, which is another reason to pin the OS (S-30).
defense.proposed_change: Add to §7 of docs/software_architecture.md. Firmware: on every DONE of TT/ST, write the last commanded µs per servo to EEPROM. EEPROM endurance is 100k writes, about 30 moves per run, so this is fine. In setup(), drive STBY low first, then servoX.writeMicroseconds(eeprom_last) BEFORE servoX.attach(pin, 500, 2500), but do not attach until the host sends `INIT`. The host sends INIT only after the operator confirms in the UI that the deck and stage positions match the displayed last-known values. At boot, print `I BOOT <fw_ver> <MCUSR reset cause> <hx_rate_hz>`. The host latches fault F_UNEXPECTED_RESET whenever an I line arrives after INIT. Host MegaLink: s = serial.Serial(); s.port = p; s.baudrate = 250000; s.dtr = False; s.rts = False; s.open(). Bring-up checklist: fit the 10 µF capacitor RESET-GND after the final flash and remove it to reflash.

defense.argument: Verified the timestamps: frames.json 02:21, gripper_design.json and grip_frames.json 02:59, meshes.json 03:43, plan3.py 03:49, plan3.log 03:49 at 0 bytes. plan3.py itself writes frames.json (line 324), so the current planner has never completed a run, and the only trajectories were checked against the old jaws.
