rejected.reason: The Ø53 spigot on TT-01 (already printed: a 4 h 31 reprint) and the PTFE sheet are unnecessary. Floating the lazy-Susan bottom plate removes the redundant constraint at zero cost, and the reviewer accepted that.

Ø22 posts with a 3 mm sleeve move the stop to 31.5°, below the 36.87° that WORK/ERUPT need. The Z5-root failure claim (air gap, 26 MPa) is disproved: CE slices of the ST-01 STL at Z 7.3-34 show material continuous from y -38.8 to -10.3. The 0.5 kN/58 MPa impact figure ignores crank compliance. Replaced by CDR-07/08/09.

M4 x 22 rejected. ISO length tolerance (±0.42 mm) against a 0.5 mm window would bottom some screws on the 2020 core and unclamp the arm. M4 x 20 at 2.0 mm engagement is adequate because preload is limited by the borrowed PLA boss.

Moving AG-01 off the A1 is rejected. With the 90 x 80 foot and 230 mm bar footprint the part is stable on a bed-slinger, and the move only adds schedule risk. The reviewer's 7.5 MPa/3.5° numbers were for the bar and a free-pivot model, not the post.
Reprinting already-printed parts (ST-04, ST-01 idler, TT-01) only for fillets is rejected. They are stall-only accident cases with SF ≥2 against 10 MPa including Kt. ST-01 is covered by CDR-07.
The Ø3 tip pin in a Ø3.4 bushing is rejected. A 0.2 mm journal at the outlet would pack with yeast and become the jam point, and free-end runout (≤0.5 mm) fits inside the new 1.0 mm radial clearance.
The spout key notch in the pockets is rejected. The EISCO spout is a pinched lip 45-60 mm above any pocket wall, so a notch cannot index it. Engraved arrows (CDR-14) instead.

The fixed 0.4 mm printed gap is rejected (print tolerance ±0.2 mm against a 0.2-0.3 mm full-scale deflection); an adjustable set-screw stop is used instead. The Ø90 pan and skirt are rejected by CE check: Ø90 leaves ~0.9 mm to the arm-B base bbox corner (510.1, 493.3). Capped at Ø80 with an 8 mm lip (CDR-17).
Reprinting ST-07 with 3.2 mm walls is rejected. It carries kPa-level stress for minutes, roundness is checked each run, and it may already be PETG (CDR-18).

The ≥6 L basin under ERUPT is rejected. It sits in the PTFE-glide tray's travel path (Y214-420 → Y34-240), so the tray cannot reach ERUPT. Replaced by the 40 mL cap plus drop cloth, pads and a cling-film-protected servo.

Reprinting TT-01/ST-01 for counterbores is rejected (PLA-roof-limited preload, SF >40 in service). The 2 mm counterbore is rejected on M5x12 length tolerance (tip could reach Z13.65, below the core at 13.9); 1.5 mm used instead.
'DIN 988 5x7x1' is not a standard size (d5 shims are 5x10, which would hit the shield). The 1.5 N·m pivot torque would crush any PLA spacer (~90 MPa); a pivot pin needs no preload.
The table-height foot is rejected. It would have to match the rail height exactly and would rock, and the plate is adequate on its own (σ≈1 MPa, δ≈0.04 mm).
Extending the ST-01 saddle to Y330 is rejected (reprint). Two M5 at ~1.6 kN preload give ~1 kN of friction against ~10 N of reactions, so any yaw is a fixed offset absorbed by teach.

The 10 µF RESET-GND capacitor is rejected. With servo power relay-gated (off at reset, in the bootloader and with USB unplugged), a reset only makes the servos limp, and a cap that must be removed before flashing is a trap for teammates. S-05's writeMicroseconds-before-attach sequence is superseded because the Servo library is dropped (Timer4 PWM, CDR-41/43).

Per-branch INA219s are rejected. One INA226 on the bus sum identifies a single 6.8 A stall against a <2.5 A legitimate sum. The '≥8° clear of the stop' commissioning criterion is impossible against 8.13° of design clearance; replaced by ±1.5° (CDR-09).

M2 pilots on WS-01 are rejected in favour of VHB on the -Y face, which needs no generator change. The -X face is about 5 mm from arm A's shoulder sweep. The printed drip skirt is replaced by the WS-02 lip (CDR-17).

D2F-L lever microswitches are rejected (4.3 mm of stop overtravel would crush them, and they need features on the printed ST-01). The deck-home Hall is rejected (a carousel mis-index is not a hazard and the grasp check catches it). The INTERNAL 2.56 V reference is rejected (±9%); the INA226 is used instead.

The XT30 split power connector per servo is rejected. It doubles mis-mate risk for unsupervised assembly, and 20 AWG HD JR extensions meet the <0.7 V drop target while the 300 ms INA trip bounds stall duration.
Charging to 4.15 V/cell is rejected. The M45CHW HV rating (6.0-8.4 V) covers a standard 4.20 V/cell 2S charge, which sags within seconds under load. A firmware >8.50 V warning is added instead.

An orientation slot on WS-01 is rejected. WS-01 is located by T-nuts that slide by hand, so its placement error would enter tick0. A slot seating the TPU fin-ray fingers would use the most compliant element as the datum. Replaced by arm-registered CAL-01 plus the rigid CAL-02 probe (CDR-33).

A ≥80 mL spill tray under WS-02 is rejected as sized. With the 80 mL fill line, the worst-case host-hang overflow into a 74 mL-brim beaker is ≈13-18 mL, covered by the ~24 mL WS-02 v2 lip. The fixed 6.0/10.5 V thresholds are rejected because they would fault a healthy 5 V arm; relative thresholds are used (CDR-50).

Keeping the Servo library on D9/D10 with bit-level critical sections, and the Timer5 D45/D46 fallback, are superseded by the E-04 Timer4 hardware-PWM design, which is immune to interrupt latency and also avoids USART RX overrun (CDR-43).
Sourcing the 'V <mV>' message from an A0 divider is rejected; pack voltage comes from INA226 VBUS and bus presence from the A1 divider (CDR-35/46).

Port resolution by USB VID:PID plus serial number is rejected. The CH340G reports no serial number and the CH340/CH343 bridges can share VID:PID. Hub-port location plus an identity probe is used (CDR-54).

The mandatory A0 10k/4.7k battery divider is rejected; it is superseded by INA226 VBUS (±0.1%, no AVcc dependence). The separate 200 ms no-edge stall rule is replaced by the single E-10 rule (CDR-49).

The microswitch in ST-05 is rejected for this event (reprint and wiring of a printed part). The interlock uses the E-07 WORK Hall, the EEPROM last-DONE and operator confirmation instead. 'Stage moves only on operator command' is rejected without the catalyst-in exception (CDR-20).

Writing and committing firmware, MegaLink and the simulator as part of this CDR is rejected: the user directed that the software not be written beforehand, only structured in the repo. The pre-flight code list stays in §9 as the team's recommended schedule (CDR-37).

Pinning to Ubuntu 22.04 is rejected (the demo laptop runs Windows 11 with LeRobot 0.6.0 installed; re-imaging two days before the flight is the bigger risk). 20 nickels as the primary calibration mass is rejected (±0.5% scatter); a 100 g class M2 weight is primary and the nickels are the logged backup.

Neither the flat 20 mm pour clearance nor the 10-20 mm lip band is adopted as written. CE ruling: 15-20 mm above the receiver rim for scale pours (≥10 mm margin over post-teach arm error while keeping the stream short) and 20-30 mm above the funnel rim (CDR-31).
